## 2026-08-17 — #1029 (imag HDMI burn-square forward JUMP: durable program-render observability) — worktree worktree-1029-burnjump, base f1384fe1e

- **Validation (live, read-only imag 10.77.9.182):** genlock FIFO CLEAN at rest — `NDI CAM1..4` @3ms `holds=0`, `dropped_due`/`relocks`/`underruns` FROZEN over 5s windows, `backward_steps=0`, `converge_sheds=0`, `locked=1`. Log carries `genlock-fifo audit` (32412×) + `multiview-audit:` (8109×) but ZERO renderSkipped/lagged lines — the render-path signal is not durably logged (only transient WS GetStats, whose `activeFps` lies during a stall, #935). Pure-std Tier-0 parser `src/program_render_audit.rs` + `is_render_path_jump` discriminator (lagged>0 = render-path origin vs FIFO/scanout). No gate (gate is issue 798). Distinct `program_render_audit_*` struct fields to avoid the #771 `render_audit_*` anchor collision.
- **TDD/verify (Tier-0, cargo does NOT run here #477):** parser 7 tests GREEN + emit-anchor `tests/program_render_audit_emit.rs` RED→GREEN via `rustc --test`; lift-compile harness of the blog block clean under `-Wformat=2 -Wconversion -Werror` + correct output; `fmt`/`check`/`clippy -D warnings` clean; brace/paren balance vs HEAD OK. ## 2026-08-17 — #1066 (setup-device.sh provisions the RemoteOS MCP agent — cam1-4 parity with the 858 imag fix) — worktree worktree-1066-mcp, base 091505aa7

- **Root cause:** `grep -niE 'remoteos|mcp' scripts/setup-device.sh` returned nothing — the cam1-4

  surface); it survived only as a hand-install on each live box (verified live on CAM1: active +
  enabled, unit `/etc/systemd/system/remoteos-mcp.service`, config chmod-600
  `/etc/remoteos-mcp/config.json`, module `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/remoteos`). A
  fresh reprovision / new box came up with the MCP surface DEAD — the exact gap the 858 imag fix
  closed via `setup-imag.sh` step 23. verify-device.sh also had no check proving it.
- **Fix:** new lettered STEP 17b in setup-device.sh (mirrors the STEP 3b sub-step idiom, no
  renumber; placed after STEP 17 dantesync, BEFORE STEP 18's ro-root flip so the installer writes
  in the rw window). Invokes the canonical `zbynekdrlik/remoteos-mcp` `install-linux.sh` (never a
  re-pinned inline pip), pre-seeds `/etc/remoteos-mcp/config.json` (chmod 600, umask 077,
  alphanumeric-guarded) from the `REMOTEOS_MCP_AUTH_KEY` env-secret BEFORE the installer runs (so it
  reuses the known key — dev1's .mcp.json stays valid), then gates on a LITERAL `is-enabled ==
  enabled` compare. New verify-device.sh acceptance check `(ab)` (next two-char letter after `(aa)`,
  the 782 precedent), inserted before the intentionally-last `(q)` check, documented in all three
  lists; proves the LIVE surface post-reboot (enabled + active + :8092 listening, fail-closed).
- **The one imag→device adaptation:** setup-device.sh follows the enable-only/defer-to-reboot
  convention, so provisioning gates on is-enabled (reboot-survival) rather than imag's is-active; the
  post-reboot `(ab)` check proves is-active + :8092. Secret never committed (env-secret only).
- Commits: RED `d071461df` (`tests/setup_device_remoteos_mcp_1066.rs`); GREEN `6004b002c`;

## 2026-07-13 (night) — #707 event-level anatomy (2nd supervisor follow-up): no forced mechanism, root cause still open

- **Follow-up dispatch**: extract exact per-event anatomy (frame indices, tick values, ±5-frame
  context, wall-clock spacing) for the two spike windows (CAM1 33/33, CAM6 15/15) + 2-3
  small-residual windows for contrast, using the corrected `--merge-partials` reproduction.
- **Delta-histogram shape is IDENTICAL across every window checked, spike or small**: dominated by
  Δ=1 (~80%) + a periodic Δ=6/7/8 catchup cluster (~130-140/window, roughly CONSTANT regardless of
  duplicate count 1-33 — decoupled from whatever produces the duplicates) + the duplicates
  themselves. ZERO outlier deltas (>10 or negative) in any window — no backward jumps, no oversized
  skips. The 1-then-7 alternation matches the ALREADY-DOCUMENTED normal dual-QR Vernier sampling
  beat (`painted_tick_gaps`'s #681 docstring); every window's mean delta is exactly 2.0.
- **The two spikes are TIGHT TEMPORAL BURSTS, not a slow drift across the window**: CAM1's 33
  duplicates pack into 5.3s of the 30.2s window (~6.2/s while bursting); CAM6's 15 pack into 6.4s
  (~2.3/s) — both front-loaded into roughly the first 1/5-1/6 of their window, NOT spread evenly
  (contradicts the "slow drift-through... ~1/s crossing rate" framing from the beat hypothesis).
- **Small-residual windows: duplicates are ISOLATED, well-separated (8-14s apart)** — a
  qualitatively different temporal shape from the spikes' tight bursts, though possibly the same
  underlying event type at a much lower rate (2 data points is not enough to be sure).
- **No mechanism proposed** — the pattern rules out real loss (no outlier/backward deltas), the
  immediate dup+catchup pairing (already refuted), and a simple frozen-camera long stuck run
  (every duplicate is an isolated single Δ0, never a run). Posted the full anatomy tables to #707
  honestly with no forced fit — root cause of the two large spikes remains genuinely open after
  THREE independent, evidence-backed investigation rounds tonight (painter-common-source,
  optical-sampling-beat, event-level anatomy).
- **imag stuck_density**: the fresh E2E run triggered by the earlier docs push (`29219154256`,

  and grabbed 600 raw YUYV frames over a genuine 10.0s/60fps window with `camera-box.service`
  briefly stopped (~12s) and cleanly restarted after. A per-frame "roughness" (adjacent-byte-delta)
  statistic stayed tight (6.48-7.15, zero outliers over 598 frames) and a pulled sample frame
  decoded to a crisp, uncorrupted image — the raw driver path is healthy right now (expected; the
  original defect is a single rare ~5m20s episode, not reproducible on demand). (c) Confirmed via
  `VIDIOC_ENUM_FMT` that the ShadowCast 2 supports both YUYV (always used) and MJPEG, but the
  device negotiates USB 3.2 SuperSpeed (5000 Mbps, ~2.5x headroom over the ~2Gbit/s raw YUYV
  1080p60 need) — ruling out bandwidth exhaustion as the obvious driver — and switching to MJPEG
  would need a new JPEG-decode step in the hot capture path (new dependency, new corruption-
  detection surface), NOT a trivial swap, so did not implement it blind. Conclusion unchanged from
  the issue's own prior framing: a hardware-class intermittent USB-transport defect, matching
  #685/#687's forensics; left OPEN referencing #688 (technician session), no purchase
  recommendation. Full findings on #696's own thread.

Fixed ONLY that; did NOT touch the #360 strih gap-ignore or `src/probe/burn_contiguity.rs` (#216/#226/#267 untouched).
- **Root cause**: cam1 contiguity is read from the CLEAN strih recording (#133); at the 60→30 hop with ~450ms latency the small cam1 burn QR softens → some cam1 ids UNREADABLE in the strih recording though the frame WAS delivered (present downstream) → wrongly counted REAL DROP, inflating the merge headline.
- **Fix**: new pure Tier-0 kernel `src/burn_reconcile.rs::cam1_real_drops_proven_delivered_downstream` = `real_drops ∩ downstream_cam1_ids`. Wired in the shared verdict loop of `src/bin/recording-verdict.rs` (cam1 node only, gated `strih_data.is_some()`): `burn_ids_in(stream_frames, burn_cam1_run_id)` → downgrade matching cam1 `ClassifiedMissing` from `RealDrop`→`BurnUnreadable`.
- **STRICT-TEST SAFETY**: only moves the CLASSIFICATION bucket; never touches `missing_ids`, so `is_contiguous()`/`is_zero()` are unchanged → a downgraded id still makes the node NOT-zero → NO false ZERO possible (verified by adversarial safety review). An id absent from the stream recording (genuine loss OR 30fps-decimated) is NEVER downgraded — stays REAL DROP.
- **TDD** (bug fix, RED→GREEN): version bump `c96707b31` → RED `c8cb21c5f` → GREEN `f50f194e5`. Pure locks: `real_drop_present_downstream_is_flagged_for_burn_unreadable`, `only_the_present_subset_is_flagged`, SAFETY `real_drop_absent_downstream_stays_real_drop` (burn_reconcile.rs). End-to-end (probe-gated): `cam1_real_drop_present_downstream_is_burn_unreadable_not_real_drop_356` + SAFETY `cam1_real_drop_absent_from_both_stays_real_drop_356` (recording-verdict.rs). Fixed `merge_of_partials_reproduces_the_fused_verdict` drop-case (stream gap None→Some(5) so the real drop is absent from BOTH recordings, still a genuine drop under reconciliation).
- **Local verify**: pure tests RED→GREEN observed on default features (`cargo test --lib burn_reconcile # airuleset:build-ok`); fmt/check/clippy default-features clean. Probe-gated E2E + fixed equivalence test verified on CI (Test job green). Did NOT compile `--features probe` locally (Tier-0 policy).
- **Merge**: PR #383 merged `303d076760a91170237e674f49b30974e59144e1`, main CI all green. No deploy (recording-verdict is a CI-built probe artifact; no web dashboard). Closes #356.

## 2026-06-30 (cont.) — #373 + #374 (bundled, joined PR #378, NO rig, v1.7.0-dev.170)
- **Version bump**: `e61f1c410` (dev.169→dev.170), FIRST commit. Same `dev` / PR #378 (the #364 colour-gate PR — these commits join it).
- **#373 — E2E STRICT GATE: optical-span collapse can vacuously PASS.** The recording-verdict headline proved DELIVERY (per-node burn contiguity) + the #363 optical read + #364 colour, but never how LONG the analyzed optical span was. When the cam2 optical read COLLAPSES (green-cast camera: dies partway, only a small early cluster, or never decodes), the span shrinks to a handful of frames; over it `optical_undecodable==0` and the burn window is trivially contiguous, so `is_zero()` alone vacuously PASSED the headline (live repro: `nodes.strih.analyzed_secs=0.0`, `frames=0`, yet `overall_pass=true`). Fix: new pure Tier-0 crate-root module `src/recording_span_gate.rs` (`span_secs(frames,fps)` + `analyzed_span_long_enough(secs,min_secs)` = `secs>=min_secs`). `NodeVerdict` carries `optical_span_frames`; the #186 headline ANDs `is_zero()` with `nv.span_ok(capture_fps,min_secs)` (and `all_zero` likewise). `is_zero()` UNCHANGED (still the per-node delivery+optical+colour gate, matched to the fixtures); the duration FLOOR is a run-level headline term. Per-node JSON now carries `analyzed_secs`/`span_ok`/`min_secs`. **Reconciliation** (e2e skill says the analyzed span is "DIAGNOSTIC only — does NOT gate the headline"): that guards against FAILING a real full-length run for a short diagnostic NOTE; #373 is the opposite — a COLLAPSED span vacuously PASSING. A duration FLOOR rejects only the collapsed/partial read; it never fails a real `>=min_secs` run (test: 9000-frame/300 s run still passes). **RED→GREEN** (Tier-0, observed `cargo test --lib recording_span_gate # airuleset:build-ok`): `test:[red]` `d20e1bfbe` — `collapsed_optical_span_must_fail_the_headline_373` + `partial_early_cluster_below_floor_must_fail_the_headline_373` FAIL with the vacuous stub (returns true); `fix:[green]` `12f339a08` — real `>=min_secs` floor ⇒ all 4 pure tests GREEN. Probe-gated binary locks (CI): `collapsed_optical_span_fails_the_headline_duration_gate_373`, `empty_optical_span_has_zero_frames_and_fails_the_duration_gate_373`. (Closes #373)
- **#374 — recording-verdict 2 minor nits** (refactor `78ea28191`, Closes #374). nit 1: strih+stream read the SAME stream recording, so each `node_verdict` recomputed the optical-span scan — now `OpticalSpanFacts` + `optical_span_facts()` derive undecodable count + span frames from ONE `optical_span`; the headline computes facts ONCE per source (`stream_optical` shared by strih+stream, `cam1_optical` for cam1) and passes them to `node_verdict_with_optical`. A `mod tests` `node_verdict` helper keeps the 13 existing call sites unchanged (and avoids a dead-code wrapper in the non-test bin build). nit 2: extracted the pure `node_verdict_lines()` (unit-testable) + an `explained` guard so an empty burn window WITH an interior optical hole no longer co-prints BOTH the OPTICAL-UNDECODABLE line AND the generic "NO burn id decoded" line; the sole-reason no-burn line still prints. Tests `print_node_verdict_does_not_co_print_no_burn_with_optical_374` + `…keeps_no_burn_line_when_it_is_the_sole_reason_374`.
- **Tier-0 discipline**: the gate DECISION is the pure default-features `recording_span_gate` (RED→GREEN observed locally). `bin/recording-verdict` is `required-features=["probe"]` → compiled ON CI ONLY; binary edits verified by careful review + the probe-gated locks (the SUPERVISOR owns CI for PR #378). Local cheap checks green: fmt/check/clippy/test --no-run + 247 lib tests.

Updated 4 apply-path tally tests (2-control set: NZXT failed 2, ShadowCast applied 2, partial-support uses contrast as the missing control, clamp adjusted 2) + the 3 selection/value tests (renamed `_no_hue_338`, `_uses_color_set_not_sharp_312`; production-path no-hue assert) — each commented that the old assertion encoded the regression.
- **scripts/recording-e2e.sh:** the two `v4l2-ctl --set-ctrl` preflight/launch lines → `saturation=50,contrast=50` (device defaults); `[0/8]`/comment text updated to cite #338/#312.

- **Problem:** `isolcpus=3` reserved core 3 on every box but NOTHING pinned to it — the SCHED_FIFO capture/emit ran on the loaded general cores (0-2: USB kworkers, ssh, painter), so it wobbled under box load (CAM2 55-60fps + underruns + 28ms head_skew); core 3 idle. The in-binary affinity was pinning to core **1** (`main.rs apply_cpu_affinity`), not the isolated core.
- **VALIDATED still real:** current `main.rs:104` pinned capture to core 1, `intercom.rs` to core 1, `ndi_display.rs` to core 0; systemd unit had NO `CPUAffinity=`. So the grab was NOT on the isolcpus core. Confirmed against current code (the partial-fix comment on #289 had only applied a runtime taskset + a `CPUAffinity=3` drop-in by hand, not in-tree).
- **RED `e1837064e` → GREEN `96fbb201e`** (version bump `66cb5b1a6` first). New `src/affinity.rs` — pure, unit-tested: `parse_cpulist`, `select_capture_core` (derive isolcpus core from /sys robustly; highest online isolated; fallback last online; `CAMERA_BOX_CAPTURE_CORE` override), `select_painter_cores` (online minus capture core), `parse_capture_irqs` (generic xhci/ehci/ohci/uvcvideo discovery from /proc/interrupts), `smp_affinity_mask_hex`. Glue (sched_setaffinity / /sys / /proc-irq IO) is thin.
- **Wiring:** capture+emit thread → isolated core (`main.rs pin_capture_thread`); painter (`probe/painter.rs`), `--display` (`ndi_display.rs`), intercom (`intercom.rs`) → OFF it via `pin_off_capture_core`. New `--setup-irq-affinity` flag runs `setup_irq_affinity` (route USB capture IRQ→isolated core, idempotent, best-effort, managed-MSI rejects logged non-fatal). systemd unit: `ExecStartPre=-...--setup-irq-affinity` + `CPUAffinity=3` (soft belt-and-braces; binary refines aux threads off it; binary's /sys derivation is authoritative).
- **CI:** coverage `--ignore-filename-regex` adds `src/affinity.rs` (syscall/IO glue, kms.rs precedent — pure fns still unit-tested); mutants `--exclude-re` the 7 glue fns, pure selection/parse fns stay mutated (added 3 edge tests: isolated-not-online, duplicate-cores idempotent, out-of-range skip; dropped a redundant empty-guard that would survive mutation).

Bug confirmed against current code.
- **§A decimation-aware verdict (the load-bearing fix):** RED `740b51c0e` → GREEN `6155f7356`. `burn_contiguity_in_window_with_step(expected_step)` in `src/probe/burn_contiguity.rs:~380` — for a PerRenderTick node with `expected_step >= 2`, a forward gap == step is the by-design decimation (not loss); gap > step charges the excess `gap/expected_step − 1` (integer; jitter of step±1 charges 0) as `RealDrop`. `expected_step == 1` = today's unconditional-ignore (back-compat wrapper `burn_contiguity_in_window` passes 1). `recording-verdict.rs` (`build_and_print_verdict` NodeSpec.step + `node_render_step` + `extract_partial_flagged_frames`): strih burn=2 (read from 30fps stream rec), stream burn=1 (own OBS), cam1 set-based. RED→GREEN tests: decimation passes; decimation+real-drop FAILS (no masking); step=1 still catches a real drop; `node_render_step` topology map. cam1→strih leg UNCHANGED (PerEmittedFrame set-based catches every real 60fps drop).

Tests: drift_guard, version_integrity_gate (STREAM_PINNED→30), harness_recording_e2e_paths, harness_genlock_sender_env updated.
- **Genlock 60→30 decimator (§3):** no change — already supported (`genlock_decide` STEADY consumes one queued frame per 30fps render tick; preload=1 absorbs jitter; `tests/genlock_preload.rs`).

## 2026-06-24 — #226 cam1 contiguity over-count: blurred-but-PRESENT cam1 burn now BurnUnreadable, not RealDrop
- **Validated STILL VALID (against ticket-validator's "OVERCOME(soft)").** The validator only traced the `None`-frame path (a blurred burn → `burn_id == None` → already BurnUnreadable via `unreadable_consumed`). But the run-1924001 signature is `present_count == expected_count == 7538`, `burn_unreadable == 0`, 107 phantom REAL DROP on a periodic ~23-emit beat — i.e. NO `None` frames. RED tests (`842d3b665`) reproduced it: the over-count code path provably still existed; no regression guard existed. So FIX, not close.
- **Mechanism:** CRC32 (`Payload::decode`) makes a wrong-but-valid id impossible, so a blurred cam1 burn on a DELIVERED frame re-decodes to a CRC-valid DUPLICATE of a neighbor id. The id it should have carried is then absent from `present_set` with no `None` charging it via `unreadable_consumed` → the #216 set-based loop leaked it as a phantom RealDrop. (Corroborated by this log's run-1924001 note: "even from the 1080p strih recording, the `unreadable_consumed` accounting mischarges on the periodic decode beat".) This is the DISTINCT case the #216 fix did not cover (#216 only handles a reordered id that appears ELSEWHERE in the set).
- **Fix (`src/probe/burn_contiguity.rs`, GREEN `13223117e` + review-correction):** classify an absent id BurnUnreadable iff a delivered frame demonstrably fell IN its gap. **PER-GAP interstitial-frame check** (NOT a global duplicate budget — the deep-review catch): the chain ALSO legitimately re-samples a PRESENT id onto several frames via the 60→30 beat (a BENIGN oversample, the dominant duplicate source); a global `present_ids.len()-present_set.len()` budget would MASK genuine drops that merely coexist with oversamples. So instead: walk recorded order, and for each forward gap count only the recorded frames that sat STRICTLY BETWEEN the two bounding present ids (interstitial = a misdecode that fell in the gap). Each interstitial frame → one BurnUnreadable in that gap; the rest of the gap → genuine RealDrop. A benign oversample sits AT its own id (not inside a gap) and credits nothing. Only a GENUINE DUPLICATE (an id already seen — the misdecode fingerprint) counts as interstitial; a present-set member arriving LATE/out of order (the #216 reorder, a single occurrence) does NOT (deep-review #2 — else a genuine drop in a later gap is mislabeled). **Label-only — `missing_ids` unchanged, so `is_zero()`/`is_contiguous()` still FAILS on any absent id; the fix can NEVER create a false ZERO**, it only moves an honest not-zero id from REAL-DROP to BURN-UNREADABLE (the issue's exact ask).
- RED→GREEN tests: `in_window_cam1_blurred_present_burn_is_unreadable_not_real_drop` (1/0), `..more_blurred..` (2/0), `..mixed_one_blurred_present_and_one_genuine_drop` (1+1). **Masking guards** (lock the deep-review counterexamples): `..benign_oversample_does_not_mask_coexisting_genuine_drops` (real=2; only the 1 interstitial frame credits unreadable), `..oversample_only_no_gap_is_zero_loss`, `..genuine_loss_with_benign_oversample_before_the_gap_not_masked` (real=3, 0 masked), `..late_present_id_reorder_does_not_credit_a_later_gap` (reorder ≠ duplicate; 102,104 both RealDrop). 34 burn_contiguity tests + full lib suite green. Reviewed by 3 code-review agent passes (caught the global-budget masking bug → per-gap; then the late-reorder mis-credit → is_duplicate guard).
- Version bump 1.7.0-dev.99 → dev.100 (`f85b457d2`). PR #228 (Closes #226). CODE/VERIFICATION ONLY — no rig recording, no dev1 decode, no dev1 build.

- **THE 1 cam1→strih "REAL DROP" (id 6485, frame 5907) = an EDGE ARTIFACT, NOT a genlock drop.** VIEWED frame-5907.png: it is a FULLY DELIVERED frame (top dual-QR + bottom-left cam1 burn + bottom-right strih burn all present, NO black/garbage). cv2 decodes its cam1 burn = `P911001.6486` (id 6486 present). So 5907 is delivered with a readable cam1 burn; id 6485 sits between two delivered frames whose burns rqrr missed — a residual of the per-emit gap math when ADJACENT cam1 frames are both burn-unreadable (the #133 `unreadable_since_prev` accounting covers one consumed id but a 2-id gap with one unreadable frame leaves a 1-id residual mislabeled REAL DROP). **FIFO CROSS-CHECK: agrees** — strih genlock FIFO received==consumed, 0 overruns (run 911330 = 11966==11966). **cam1→strih genuine drops = 0; the "1" is an edge artifact, eliminated once the decoder reads the burns (below).**
- **THE ROOT CAUSE OF #202/#186 IS THE PROBE'S rqrr DECODER, NOT BURN SIZE.** PROVEN: of ALL 17 flagged-unreadable frames (11 cam1 + 5 strih + 1 stream), **cv2's QR detector decodes the flagged node's burn from the IDENTICAL pixels in EVERY ONE** (full-frame multi-detect). The burns are present + SHARP (cam1 burn LaplacianVar 6564 > optical QR 1399, contrast 0-255). The cam1 burn is already 320px = the dual-QR-clearance MAX (can't grow). rqrr's single full-frame `detect_grids` intermittently misses the small burns when several QRs of very different sizes share one full-res frame; cv2 (and rqrr given a focused sub-region) reads them. So the fix is decoder-side, **dev1-only, re-runnable on the EXISTING recording — NO rig deploy / fresh run needed** (the burns are already in the recorded pixels).
- **FIX (#202): `decode_qr_luma_all_robust` (src/probe/qr.rs)** — the OFFLINE-recording decode now runs the plain full-frame pass PLUS a 3×3 grid of OVERLAPPING tiles, each cubic-upscaled to ≥1280px long-side, rqrr-decoded, all merged + de-duped by (run_id,frame_id). In a tile a 320px burn is large-relative so its finder locks. Wired into `decode_recording_frame` ONLY (the parallel #166/#187 worker pool) — NEVER the latency-sensitive live tap. Tile passes are panic-safe (`catch_unwind` around rqrr — rqrr-0.9.3 grid.rs:206 `assert!(scan>=1)` can panic on a degenerate tile; a panicking tile yields "nothing" instead of aborting the verdict). TDD: RED proven by stubbing robust→plain-only (the softened-burn test fails: robust returns only the 2 big QRs); GREEN with the tiling. Real-data proof: robust recovers the cam1/strih/stream burn on EVERY one of the 17 real flagged PNGs that plain misses.

## 2026-06-23 — #166 recording-verdict perf + crash-safety (PR pending)
- **Issue still real (validated):** read src/probe/recording.rs — `analyze_recording` decoded each ffmpeg gray8 frame SERIALLY on the main thread (no rayon/par_iter/threads, only the ffmpeg/ffprobe spawns), and `extract_frames_png` had NO cap (a PNG for every flagged frame). - **Fix 1 (parallelize):** new `decode_stream_parallel(workers, produce)` in recording.rs — std::thread + bounded sync_channel worker pool mirroring #160's `decode_spool`; producer (ffmpeg I/O) on the calling thread, N decode workers, collector re-sorts by frame_index → byte-identical to serial. `CAMERA_BOX_DECODE_WORKERS` env override. **Measured:** serial 50.1s vs parallel 27.0s on a 1000-frame slice; FULL 7.3GB/10025-frame grab decoded in **6m37s parallel (4 cores, 344% CPU)** vs >1h serial on the #163 night. parallel CSV == serial CSV byte-for-byte.

Verdict counts stay complete; only the visual proof is sampled.
- **Fix 3 (liveness guard):** new scripts/verdict-monitor.sh (DEAD=126 when pid gone + no exit marker; STALL=124 when no output growth for T + kills the wedged proc; returns verdict's own code on clean completion via exit marker). Wired into recording-e2e.sh step 8: verdict runs backgrounded (RUST_LOG=info for progress signal), monitor drives it to terminal. **Live-demoed:** killed fake verdict → 126 in ~5s (no hang); wedged fake → 124 + killed.

On the genlock build (`OBS_GENLOCK_WALL_CLOCK=1`, wall-clock render tick), a non-FIFO source takes the normal async cursor path; the camera-box sender's wall-clock-epoch timecode (src/ndi.rs) goes out-of-bounds vs the monotonic compositor cursor → every frame discarded → black. This is why the #7 worker saw 0 at strih/stream and attributed it ALL to the black render. Fix: extract pure `settle_cutoff_ns`/`trim_to_settle` (src/probe/differ.rs) + derive `stop_ns = clock_ns(start, args.wall_clock)`. ## 2026-06-15 — cam→strih latency investigation + probe instrument hygiene

- **Trigger:** user flagged cam→strih latency as a regression ("we had lower; aim ~0 not 500ms; the cam inconsistency is from your debugging"). Goal: lowest-possible cam→strih latency WHILE zero-loss.
- **Finding (proven by the live genlock-FIFO audit, ~73 min, Lowest latency + preload=1):** production cam→strih is ALREADY at the lowest DistroAV latency (latency=2/unbuffered) AND ~zero-loss — **NDI cam1: 131074 frames underruns=0**, cam3 underruns=1, cam5 underruns=2. Not a regression.
- **The "460ms" was an instrument artifact:** the probe's per-hop latency (recv−recv first-occurrence) gives physically-impossible negatives (cam→strih `min_ms -182`) because a QR id spans multiple frames (oversampling). Per-hop latency ms are UNTRUSTWORTHY; only single-copy loss + absolute (gen_ts) latency are reliable. Filed **#74**.
- **Lowest experiment on the PROBE path** (latency=2 on the freshly-added probe input) showed 2–4 single-copy losses — freshly-injected probe priming + decode tearing, NOT the production path (live audit = 0 underruns).
- **Fixes this PR:** (1) `NDI cam5` was at Normal (my debug artifact) → restored to Lowest live, all 3 genlock cams now consistent. (2) `_PROBE_NDI_SETTINGS` += `latency:2` so the harness measures the real min-latency config. (3) **teardown bug:** the idle probe input kept `genlock_fifo=True` and (Studio Mode) sat in PREVIEW → render-ticked an empty FIFO forever → perpetual underrun-audit spam (saw 91k+) that corrupts the cumulative audit. Fix: teardown now disables `genlock_fifo` on idle AND restores the prior PREVIEW scene; setup records `prev_preview`. End-state live-verified on strih+stream (audit spam stopped; program+preview back to Test / PRO KLAPKA).
- **Rig restored:** both boxes program+preview on production scenes, probe idled (genlock off). No device firmware deploy.

## #150 — lock down genlock NDI source config (expose only source + preload; hardcode the rest)
- **Root cause** (user-confirmed live 2026-06-22): a genlock NDI source that is incompletely configured decodes 0 at strih while a fully-configured one decodes 100% off the SAME NDI source. The real in-code gaps: `ndi_recv_hw_accel` absent→false (no getdefaults entry), `ndi_audio` true (getdefaults forces true), `genlock_fifo` per-source. (`ndi_sync_lock` cited in the live diff does NOT exist in our vendored DistroAV/OBS — it's an orphaned/foreign key; the real sync key is `ndi_sync`=2 + `genlock_fifo`.)
- **Fix** (vendor/distroav/src/ndi-source.cpp, ROOT not harness): `force_genlock_certified_settings()` forces sync=2, behavior=2, bw=0, latency=0, timeout=KEEP, yuv=partial/BT709, hw_accel=true, audio=false, framesync=false, alpha=false into `settings`; called at top of `ndi_source_update` GATED on PROP_GENLOCK_FIFO (so non-genlock aux/preview inputs untouched). `apply_genlock_lockdown_visibility()` hides all 11 non-essential props on the genlock path (wired into genlock-checkbox modified-callback + initial-open pass). bw_modes callback made genlock-aware so the YUV pair can't leak the lockdown. Supersedes the #149 harness "full clone" workaround.
- **TDD**: RED dd0eb1700 (tests/distroav_genlock_lockdown.rs — forcer/visibility absent) → GREEN fa45fcb5; review fixes 01aefde68 (YUV-leak + comment + 3 more must_force needles). 4 source-guard tests, lock-step pwsh gate in windows-genlock.yml.
- **PR #158** dev→main, Closes #150. CI green; windows-genlock build dispatched on dev HEAD for the DistroAV.dll. Deploy target on strih+stream: C:\ProgramData\obs-studio\plugins\distroav\bin\64bit\distroav.dll (617472, 2026-06-17), backup to C:\obs-backup\2026-06-22-150\.

## 2026-06-24 — #198 in-window burn-id contiguity (stop counting per-render-tick skips as missing) — PR pending
- **Validated still real** (probe-tools-linux-amd64 from merged-main run 28058743392, NEW contiguity binary, stream-only on the EXISTING run 136141133 — NO rig, NO dev1 build): the bug reproduces EXACTLY — strih **18056 missing** (ids 1670..=28676, 8951 present ⇒ range 27006 / ~9000 frames ≈ **3x**), stream **8967 missing** (ids 394..=18359, 8999 present ≈ **2x**), cam1 clean **65** (ids 582..=9584). Confirms the issue: strih/stream burn id is the DistroAV per-RENDER counter, cam1 is per-EMIT.
- **ROOT CAUSE (burn-id RATE, #198 point 2)**: the strih/stream burn `frame_id` is the DistroAV burn filter's per-render `f->frame_id++` (vendor/distroav/src/ndi-burn-filter.cpp:261, in the OBS `video_render` callback) — it advances FASTER than the emitted output rate, so the integer-range `min..=max` contiguity flagged every un-emitted render tick as "missing". cam1's burn increments once per EMITTED frame (src/main.rs:446, after the genlock decimation gate, before NDI send) → clean. The counter CANNOT be made 1-per-emitted-frame inside the filter (video_render is decoupled from the NDI output path ndi-output.cpp `raw_video`, so the filter can't know which renders are emitted) → documented the correct per-recorded-frame interpretation instead.
- **FIX (burn_contiguity.rs)**: `burn_contiguity_in_window(node, &[RecordedBurnFrame])` over the per-recorded-frame in-window burn-presence sequence (one entry per in-window DELIVERED frame = one emitted output frame). Loss = a delivered frame with NO node burn (drop/unreadable) OR a backward jump (reorder). FORWARD integer skips are EXPECTED (un-emitted render ticks) ⇒ NOT loss. Out-of-window pre-/post-signal frames (no cam2 QR) excluded so render-tick ids can't inflate the range (#198 point 1). `expected_count` = in-window emitted-frame count, not the integer span.
- **WIRING (recording-verdict.rs)**: `node_verdict` builds the window via `in_window_burn_frames` (leading-discard on cam2's optical QR, delivered frames only) + classifies each missing slot by the exact recorded frame (delivered ⇒ BURN-UNREADABLE, absent ⇒ REAL DROP — kept, #198 point 3). Removed the dead integer-range `classify_missing`/`frame_has_burn`.

### #198 — deep-review hardening (rate-aware + count fixes) before merge
- Two parallel review agents flagged 5 issues on the first in-window cut; all FIXED in ed4148772 (still pre-merge, same PR #199):
  1. **cam1 per-EMIT drops were silently passed (HIGH)** — cam1's burn is per-emitted-frame, so a forward integer gap between delivered frames IS a real cam1 drop; the first cut treated ALL forward skips as non-loss (correct only for strih/stream's per-render counter). Added `BurnRate` (PerEmittedFrame/PerRenderTick); cam1=PerEmittedFrame, strih/stream=PerRenderTick.
  2. **REAL DROP was structurally unreachable (HIGH)** — the window holds only DELIVERED frames so the inline classifier always returned BURN-UNREADABLE; the kind (`InWindowMissingKind`) is now decided IN the pure walk (per-emit gap / backward jump = RealDrop, delivered None-burn = BurnUnreadable) — both reachable.
  3. **Consecutive None frames got duplicate synthetic ids** — a monotone synthetic cursor seeded ABOVE max-present gives each None a distinct id that can't collide with a real id.
  4. **present_count could exceed expected** (backward jump counted both present+missing) — present derived from non_present_delivered so present+per-frame-misses==expected always.
  5. **Duplicated walk** — `burn_contiguity_in_window` returns `InWindowContiguity{contiguity, missing_slots}` (single source of truth); node_verdict pairs pixel proof onto it. NodeSpec groups node/run_id/rate.
- 19 burn_contiguity lib tests + 24 recording-verdict binary tests + 435 total lib tests; clippy --all-features clean. RED→GREEN order preserved (RED d6795e61e is the only test-FIRST commit; subsequent commits harden GREEN).

### #207 — recording-verdict decode ~10x faster: plain rqrr first, robust tiles only on a missed burn, version 1.7.0-dev.91
- VALIDATED (verify-issue-still-valid): STILL_VALID. `src/probe/recording.rs::decode_recording_frame` called `decode_qr_luma_all_robust` UNCONDITIONALLY → `decode_qr_luma_all_robust` (qr.rs:509) ran the plain full-frame pass THEN the bottom-band 3-tile cubic-upscale recovery on EVERY frame (~10x cost). At ~26 fps a 30-min run (~54k frames, strih 1080p + stream 4K) verdicts in ~50 min. Confirmed by reading the current call graph (codegraph + grep), not the stale issue text. Rig/stream box NOT touched (in use; CODE/CI-ONLY task).
- FIX (qr.rs): extracted the tile loop into `robust_tile_passes(&img, &mut out)` (pure refactor, no behavior change). New `decode_qr_luma_all_fast_then_robust(img, expected_burn_run_ids)`: plain pass FIRST; if all expected node burns already decoded → return (FAST, the ~99%+ clean-frame case); else run `robust_tile_passes` (ROBUST fallback). `decode_qr_luma_all_robust` keeps the always-robust behavior (used by the recording.rs:607 undecodable self-check + the diagnostic dump tools).
- PER-RECORDING burn set: threaded `analyze_recording_with_burns(path, expected)` → `decode_stream_parallel(workers, expected, …)` → `decode_recording_frame_with_burns(idx, luma, expected)`. The verdict's `ticks_of(path, expected)` passes the burns each recording ACTUALLY carries — strih=`[cam1,strih]`, stream=`[cam1,strih,stream]`, cam1 grab=`[cam1]` — so the fast path fires on every recording (requiring all 3 would force tiles forever on a strih recording that never has the stream burn). `analyze_recording`/`decode_recording_frame` keep the full-set (max-robust) default for forensic-dump/recording-probe.
- OBSERVABILITY: `decode_path_counts()` (process-wide AtomicU64 fast/robust counters) logged at recording-analysis-complete so the verdict shows fast ≫ robust (the speedup is real).
- TDD (same PR): tests/burn_fixture_decode.rs — `fast_then_robust_recovers_every_real_burn_unreadable_frame` (every #186 real fixture still decodes via the fallback) + `fast_then_robust_matches_robust_always_on_every_fixture` (identical reads). qr.rs unit tests — `fast_path_taken_when_plain_already_reads_every_expected_burn` (FAST counter=1/ROBUST=0, deterministic via the always-readable optical id), `robust_fallback_taken_when_plain_misses_an_expected_burn` (ROBUST=1, softened burn recovered, same blur 2.8/260px the #202 synthetic test proved), `fast_then_robust_is_identical_to_robust_always`, `empty_expected_burns_always_takes_fast_path`. The #186 fixtures stay GREEN through the fallback = 0-miss guarantee preserved.
- Expected speedup: tiles run only on the rare burn-missed frame (≪1%) instead of every frame → ~10x faster verdict (~50 min → ~5 min for a 30-min recording).
- Version: merged origin/dev (which had bumped to dev.90 for #101) mid-flight; my bump collided at dev.90 so re-bumped to dev.91 (distinct, strictly > main dev.89).

## #216 — ~150s latency-pairing GAP (~900-1050s) explained + fixed (cam2 optical-decode dropout) — 2026-06-24
- ROOT CAUSE (investigation-only, NO rig touched — user was running a live test): read straight from `proof-2026-06-24/latency-per-frame.csv` + `verdict-clean.json`. The per-frame CSV has a 175.2s gap (rel 861.5s→1036.7s); cam2 tick jumped 52293→62805 = 10512 ticks ≈175s @60fps == the gen_ts gap, so the cam2 PAINTER never stopped — only cam1's OPTICAL read of the cam2 QR failed for that stretch. `53993 stream frames − 44052 CSV rows = 9941` == `nodes.stream.undecodable` exactly: every undecodable frame = no cam2 optical tick = no CSV row. cam1/strih/stream BURNS present the whole time (cam1 present_count==expected_count, 235 isolated drops, none clustered). Verdict = (c) optical cam2-QR decode dropout MASKED by (b) a code skip. NOT (a) painter-CSV gap (painter CSV is only an optional flip-map; gen_ts comes from QR decode), NOT a chain loss.
- THE BUG: `per_frame_latency_csv_rows` (src/probe/recording_latency.rs ~894) did `let Some(frame_id) = cam2_tick else { continue }` — skipping the ENTIRE row when the cam2 optical tick was absent, which also suppressed the three BURN-ONLY hops (cam1→strih, strih→stream, cam1→stream) that need ONLY the burns and were computable. The #209 plotter then drew a blank band where rows were missing.
- FIX (GREEN b0e75b9f3): emit a row whenever there's a valid x-anchor (positive cam1/strih burn or cam2 paint stamp), even with no cam2 tick. `LatencyCsvRow.frame_id` → `Option<u32>` (empty CSV cell on a dropout row); `flip_ts_ns` looked up only when a tick exists; the three burn hops fill in → lines stay UNBROKEN across an optical dropout. Only a frame with NEITHER cam2 tick NOR any positive stamp is still skipped. Plotter unchanged (plots by gen_ts_ns, never parses frame_id).
- TDD RED→GREEN: RED 5f291231b — `per_frame_csv_optical_decode_dropout_keeps_burn_hops_unbroken_216` (got 2 rows, want 5) + reworked the bug-enshrining `..._no_cam2_optical_is_skipped` → `..._no_cam2_but_burns_still_emits_a_row_216` + new `..._no_cam2_and_no_stamp_is_skipped`; proven RED against a reinstated guard, then GREEN. Real-pixel integration ba230b305 — `per_frame_csv_keeps_burn_hops_unbroken_across_real_optical_dropout_216` in tests/recording_latency_decode.rs (6 frames via real rqrr decode, 4 with NO cam2 QR rendered but all burns → all 6 emit rows w/ +60/+59/+119 ms hops). All green locally (52 recording_latency unit tests, 3 integration tests).
- Version bump 1c699b140 (1.7.0-dev.92→93). PR #217 (Closes #216).
- GOTCHA: pre-push Gate-1 (PATH-only "feature .rs changed but no test-named file") false-positives on Rust INLINE tests — adding the `tests/recording_latency_decode.rs` integration test (a genuine real-pixel coverage add) satisfied it cleanly; Gate-2 (the real RED-before-GREEN ordering) already passed via inline-test diff detection.

- Validated STILL_VALID on the live stream box (10.77.9.204): `ffprobe` of the latest recording `2026-06-23 20-32-26.mp4` = **3840x2160 h264 30fps** while the OBS canvas/output is 1920x1080 (`[Video] Base/Output CX/CY=1920x1080`). #196's "stream is 1080p" was about the CANVAS; the RECORDING was the 4K-upscaled one. Healthy: PID 17224, 1330MB, port 4455, genlock tick ENABLED + DistroAV loaded + NDI output started, no locale/video failure.

OBS encoder log: `advanced_video_recording` width 1920 height 1080 (no GPU scaling); `advanced_video_stream` width 3840 height 2160 + "GPU scaling enabled" → PROD STREAM UNAFFECTED. Test clip deleted after.
- Before→after recording: 3840x2160 → 1920x1080. Stream encoder: 3840x2160 (unchanged). Result: crisp burns, ~4x faster proof decodes (helps #226 cam1 over-count + the optical/burn reads).

## #128 — deterministic env-safe genlock OBS relaunch wrapper (2026-06-25)
- PR #231 (dev->main). Commits: 03b70a253 (feat: wrapper+test+skill), 8d1fadb43 (review fixes), c23e78265 (playbook PEB snippet). Closes #128.
- PROBLEM (the recurring "stale-env trap", systematized): an OBS relaunch from a long-lived win-* MCP shell whose env snapshot predates the Machine-scope write → child obs64 inherits the STALE snapshot → a genlock var UNSET → render tick silently OFF, genlock guarantee gone invisibly (#126 near-miss; #110's manual recovery was this exact issue done by hand). `$env:` read in that stale shell agrees with the wrong value — only the launched process's own PEB env is truth.
- VALIDATED still real (ticket-validator + live): NO launch wrapper existed in the repo or on either box; obs-ops skill documented the recipe in prose only, no scripted+verified mechanism. Both boxes' running OBS were already correct (PEB-read pre-check), but the deterministic relaunch mechanism was the gap.
- FIX: scripts/launch-obs-genlock.sh — pure testable PLANNER (same model as recording-verdict-on-stream.sh; scp/ssh to Windows denied, agent drives win-* MCP). Emits a self-contained PowerShell program: reads the four OBS_GENLOCK_* vars FRESH from Machine scope, sets them EXPLICIT in the spawning shell (defeats stale snapshot), clears .sentinel\*, launches obs64 cwd=bin\64bit, then VERIFIES child PEB env (NtQueryInformationProcess+ReadProcessMemory via Add-Type) matches Machine AND log shows `render tick ENABLED`, exits non-zero (fail loud) otherwise. --force=documented obs-ops kill; no-force refuses double-launch. Reserve/audit absence = non-fatal WARNING (PEB already proves RESERVE_MS=3, source-dependent).
- TESTS: tests/launch_obs_genlock.rs — 14 guards (sources the script, asserts: exactly the 4 vars; reads Machine; sets explicit BEFORE launch; cwd=bin\64bit; clears sentinels; PEB-verify+fail-loud; render-tick/reserve log checks; final verdict gates exit0 on $pebOk -and $tickOk; force vs no-force; CLI box→MCP mapping; source-safety; trailing-flag exit-2; single-quote '' escape). RED-proven (remove explicit env-set → stale-trap test fails; remove need_val → exit-2 test fails).
- PEB OFFSETS (x64): PEB+0x20=ProcessParameters, RTL+0x80=Environment, +0x3F0=EnvironmentSize. Confirmed reading correct values live on both boxes.
- LIVE PROOF (via the wrapper, both boxes 2026-06-25): strih obs64 PID 6244 + stream obs64 PID 10844 each PEB-verified WALL_CLOCK=1 RESERVE_MS=3 TS_ALIGN=1 PRELOAD_FRAMES=1 + render tick ENABLED; stream further showed timestamp-aligned release ENABLED + sub-frame jitter reserve=3ms + live reserve_ms=3 audits (had a live 2ME PGM source). Both left on #184-validated reserve=3, healthy, NOT on a wrong config.
- SIBLINGS (out of scope here): #121 post-deploy verify + #123 pre-test gate should assert render-tick (this issue is the LAUNCH wrapper + child-PEB verify, distinct from those).
- DECISION: gated the hard FAIL on the always-emitted `render tick ENABLED` line + PEB (not on the source-dependent reserve audit) — so an off-air box with a dark program scene still verifies correctly.

## 2026-06-27 — autopilot: #266 NDI-receive stuck-state watchdog REDESIGN (PR #270, v1.7.0-dev.120) — PUSHED, not merged
- #266 was auto-closed by PR #268's merge (its body still had `Closes #266`) despite the watchdog being SPLIT OUT for redesign → reopened; validated still real (watchdog absent on main; #265 collapse verified live).
- Built `scripts/stuck-watchdog.py` fresh (the old one generated 14+ false-neg/false-pos findings over 2 rounds). RED 3cbad2141 → GREEN a6504db34; refinements 590b35801 (sustained-freeze+staleness) + 916626d85 (deep-self-review fixes). 49 watchdog tests (92 total) green; ci.yml python job green.
- DISCRIMINATION (the core): read a WINDOW (60≈5min) of genlock-fifo audit per source. STUCK = was-HEALTHY (peak fps≥floor in window, the collapsed-vs-always-low baseline) + NOW collapsed (recent fps<floor, incl 0fps) + STARVED (recent underruns climbing + window overruns NOT dominant + recent depth≤floor). benign IDLE = never-delivered (peak~0) / steady-low / overrun-dominant. NAMED = stricter (any below-floor → alert; absent/stale → vanished, single FRESH sample NOT vanished). dantesync runaway checked INDEPENDENTLY. STALENESS (`--now`=box clock): newest sample older than max-age → skip (named→vanished); `age>max_age` not abs (future sample = freshest, never stale). Robust parse: field-by-field (#148 holds=), tail sized to window, pair_dt floor, midnight-wrap only on large-negative, per-window cadence for missing ts. Exits 0/1/2/3 (3=delivery-FAILED).
- TWO self-reviews (correctness + discrimination, parallel agents) found: lax absolute-counter was_delivering + no baseline (steady-low false-pos) → peak-fps baseline; is_stale abs() flipping future/skewed sample to stale → `age>max_age`; recent-only overrun gate → window-level; named single-sample false-vanish → absent/stale only. All fixed + locked by tests.
- LIVE-RIG VERIFY (read-only, win-strih MCP, no Discord sent): real strih OBS log (cam1=`NDI cam5` clean 30fps post-19:45-reboot, collapsed+froze 20:11 received=41421 underruns climbing ~30/s depth=0, logging stopped 20:13:56). Watchdog vs current state (now=03:59, dantesync 0%) → OK, NO false alert (frozen tail 7.7h stale/off-program); vs collapse caught live (now=20:14:30) → stuck alert; dantesync 97% no-audit → runaway alert.
- DO NOT MERGE (per dispatch) — supervisor reviews + merges. Script-only, Tier-0, no deploy.
- 📔 Playbook: genlock skill gained a "#266 stuck-state watchdog" section (audit-log location + LastWriteTime-stale gotcha, the #265 signature, the discrimination design, the --now/staleness rule, the run recipe); CLAUDE.md router updated.

- BUG: backward wall-clock step → `present_ts = wall_now - reserve` regresses below every queued (pre-step) frame ts → due==0 forever → HOLD/FREEZE of the live program feed (always-on since #257).

Chose head-future over a stored `last_wall_now` one-shot because the stale future-stamped head PERSISTS over the seam (one-shot would re-freeze next tick); head-future self-heals, stateless. Large per-source latency (≤2000ms) is past-stamped → never triggers.
- C: vendor obs-source.c ts-align `due==0` branch (~4832-4880) → `head_future` check + `genlock_backward_steps++` re-anchor + `to_drop = num-1`; obs-internal.h `genlock_backward_steps` field; audit line gained `backward_steps=%llu`. ## #293 — strih OBS Multiview FROZEN (regression of #278): add anti-starvation floor (2026-06-28, SOLO PR)
- VALIDATED still real: read `vendor/obs-studio/libobs/obs-display.c` render_display() — the #278 skip `if (elapsed + ewma > budget) return;` had NO liveness floor; comment even admitted "may drop to a low fps / freeze under sustained over-budget load — fine". A 4-cam Multiview ewma (~18-23ms) alone > ~15ms budget every tick → skipped forever → frozen. RED C-harness proved the freeze (over-budget display never rendered over 240 ticks). ## #292 — stream genlock latency capped at ~450ms (can't A/V-align to ~1s-late audio) (2026-06-28, SOLO PR)
- VALIDATED still real: read `vendor/obs-studio/libobs/obs-source.c genlock_source_drop_cap` — the per-source latency drop-cap budgeted `latency_frames` at the CANVAS output fps (`genlock_video_fps` = obs_get_video_info). But the ts-align deadline (`ready_async_frame`, `present_ts = wall_now - latency_ms`) holds every queued frame younger than latency_ms, so the FIFO fills at the SOURCE ARRIVAL rate. The stream box receives a 60fps NDI feed from strih into a 30fps canvas (the "60→30 strih→stream" topology, MEMORY final-mixed-60-30). At canvas fps, 1000ms budgeted 30 frames while the buffer parks ~60 → the overrun force-drain capped the delay ~half-way (~450ms, ≈27-29 frames near MAX_ASYNC_FRAMES=30 floor at 60fps). The #245 scaling + #257 UI int (max 2000) were present but used the WRONG fps. CI never caught it: the old `drop_cap_accommodates_deep_per_source_latency` budgeted at 30fps and always passed.
- ROOT CAUSE: drop-cap depth derived at canvas fps, not source arrival fps. new_max delivered: 2000ms (setter clamp unchanged) now actually delivered up to that at any source fps (was ~450ms). 2000ms@60fps = 120 frames + RESERVE 4 = cap 124 < abs-max 132 (GENLOCK_PRELOAD_MAX 128 unchanged — already sufficient; the binding constraint is depth+reserve, not abs-max).
- RED 3a5af16d8 (`test:[red]`): `tests/genlock_preload.rs` `drop_cap_delivers_high_latency_at_max_source_arrival` + `latency_depth_frames_budgets_at_source_arrival_rate` — extracted pure helper `genlock_latency_depth_frames(latency_ms, canvas_num, canvas_den)` with the buggy canvas-only body; cap 34 < 60 held @1000ms, helper returns 30 not 60. Proven RED locally via `cargo test --features probe --test genlock_preload  # airuleset:build-ok`.
- GREEN b22400d3f (`fix:[green] Closes #292`): helper budgets at max(canvas, arrival@GENLOCK_MAX_SOURCE_FPS=60); C `genlock_source_drop_cap` mirrors it; new `#define GENLOCK_MAX_SOURCE_FPS 60` (C) + `pub const GENLOCK_MAX_SOURCE_FPS: u32 = 60` (Rust mirror). C divide `(latency_ms*60+500)/1000` exactly mirrors `ms_to_frames(ms,60,1)`. 97 genlock tests GREEN locally.
- Mirror guard (lock-step #269): new `drop_cap_budgets_at_source_arrival_fps_in_vendored_source` pins `#define GENLOCK_MAX_SOURCE_FPS 60` + `source->genlock_latency_ms * GENLOCK_MAX_SOURCE_FPS` in obs-source.c so a subtree revert can't silently re-cap latency. YAML gates unchanged (GENLOCK_PRELOAD_MAX still 128, genlock_source_drop_cap still present).
- Local: version bump 3797ea9a1 (dev.133→dev.134); Tier-0 default fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test --no-run clean; clippy --features probe clean.
- RIG: NOT touched. NO OBS build/deploy — vendored-OBS rollout is a coordinated supervisor step (batched with #152 title, #293 multiview, upcoming #294/#297). Live "set 1000ms on stream, measure A/V align" is UNVERIFIED-on-rig (deferred to that rollout); the unit test (drop-cap delivers the requested latency up to 2000ms at 60fps, no 450 clamp) is the code-level proof. PR dev→main, auto-merge.

## #297 — NDI sender re-announce for reliable OBS discovery (2026-06-28/29)
- Problem: OBS/DistroAV mDNS NDI discovery is flaky; the camera-box NDI sender is created ONCE at startup (`NDIlib_send_create`) and never re-registers, so a box whose network came up after start (boot race / late DHCP) or whose link flapped announces on a dead/old network and is never rediscovered (observed live: finder returned only {CAM2} while CAM1/3/4 were up).
- Fix (option 3, sender-side): re-register the sender (re-runs the mDNS announce on the CURRENT network) when the host's usable LAN address set changes OR recovers from an outage.
  - `src/reannounce.rs` (pure, cross-platform, unit-tested): `NetworkSignature` (order/dup-independent set), `should_reannounce(announced, current, saw_down_since_announce)` (re-announce iff current non-empty AND (changed OR recovered-from-down)), `is_discoverable_interface()` (LAN-NIC denylist: drops lo/docker/virbr/veth/tailscale/tun/wg/…), `REANNOUNCE_POLL_INTERVAL=2s`.
  - `src/ndi.rs` (Linux IO): `current_network_signature()` via `getifaddrs` (up/non-loopback/IPv4, LAN-NIC only, `Ipv4Addr` render); `NdiSender::maybe_reannounce()` (throttled) + `reannounce_now()` (create-new-then-destroy-old → always a valid sender; `saw_down_since_announce` tracked).
  - `src/main.rs`: capture loop calls `maybe_reannounce()` each successful-capture tick (non-probe `sender`; probe `capture_sender.as_mut()` — burn mode skips, sender on burn thread).
- TDD: RED 2cb323187 (`test:[red]`) stub `should_reannounce→false` (the "never re-announces" bug) → 2 network-change cases FAIL; GREEN c7d7c305a (`fix:[green] Closes #297`); review fixes 7f5d66afb (LAN filter + down→up) + 04b0a7c3d (Ipv4Addr + docs). `tests/ndi_reannounce.rs` 12 tests GREEN (built-binary-direct, default features, no probe).
- Reviews: `/code-review` (high) + `superpowers:requesting-code-review` — no Critical/blocking; all actionable minors fixed in-PR. Deep review's Important#1 = a rig-verification gate (boxes must have been in boot-race/flap state, NOT stable-lost-announce) → UNVERIFIED-on-rig (supervisor verifies discovery).
- SCOPE: sender-side re-announce handles boot-race/late-DHCP/link-flap. The PERSISTENT mDNS/multicast flakiness for STABLE boxes (the central NDI Discovery Server option 1, or LAN multicast fix option 2) is a separate fleet-infra decision raised to the user (architecture question).
- PR #315 dev→main, merged d15b540c0 (auto-merge default; no manual marker). Version 1.7.0-dev.139.
- RIG: NOT touched (no deploy to cam boxes, no win-*/cam MCP) — supervisor deploys + verifies discovery on the rig.

## #297 (re-opened) — NDI sender re-announce was an infinite failing loop (2026-06-29)
- Symptom (live, CAM2 .62 reboot, dev.139): `reannounce_now` looped every 2s — `network changed [] -> [ips]` → `NDIlib_send_create returned null; kept existing sender` forever; boot-raced box never rediscovered.
- Root cause: the prior cycle's `create-new-then-destroy-old` is SELF-DEFEATING — the NDI SDK refuses a 2nd sender with a name already live in the process, so a same-name `send_create` while the old handle lives ALWAYS returns null → `bail!` → `announced_sig` never advances from the boot `[]` baseline → `should_reannounce([], [ips], saw_down)` stays true → re-fires every poll.
- Fix (`src/ndi.rs` `reannounce_now`): DESTROY old FIRST (guard null handle like `Drop`), THEN `send_create` the fresh same-name sender. Advance the trigger ONLY on create success; on the rare null-create-after-destroy leave `self.sender` null + state unchanged (retry next poll). Emit path `send_frame_data_with_timecode` GUARDS a null sender (drop frame, never `send_send_video_v2(NULL)`=UB). #3 (seed `announced_sig` with live net at create) was already in dev.139 — the `[]` baseline came from a genuine boot race, not a missing init.
- Refactor: trigger state+transitions extracted to pure, unit-tested `crate::reannounce::ReannounceState` (`new`/`should_reannounce`/`mark_down`/`record_reannounce_attempt`).
- TDD: RED d3cf41fb6 (`test:[red]`) 4 pure tests reference not-yet-existent `ReannounceState` → fail to compile; GREEN 5d7f9a0b0 (`fix:[green] Closes #297`) → 4/4 pass + 12/12 existing integration. Review fixes: f243deb07 (null-guard on destroy retry path, `/code-review`), 12f20530f (drop dead `Default` derive, deep review).
- Reviews: `/code-review` (xhigh) found+fixed the destroy-null-on-retry bug; `superpowers:requesting-code-review` (deep) — no Critical/Important correctness; Important#1 = pure tests lock convergence not the literal FFI ordering → filed #317 (FFI test-seam, fails bundling gate: needs a mockable NdiLib function table separate from `libloading::Library`).
- PR #316 dev→main. Version 1.7.0-dev.140. RIG: NOT touched — supervisor deploys to fleet + reboot-verifies CAM2.
- #297 NDI sender re-announce infinite loop fixed (destroy-before-create + init announced_sig) — PR #316 merged febc4a5, dev.140 deployed CAM1/2/4, CAM2 reboot-verified: 0 null-creates, converges, strih reconnected :5961. (#297-A boot test)

## #317 — lock NDI re-announce FFI ordering (destroy-before-create) via a mockable function table (2026-06-29)
- Gap (from #316 deep review): the pure `crate::reannounce` tests lock the convergence/retry CONTRACT but NEVER call the FFI, so a revert of `reannounce_now` to create-first would keep all 4 pure tests green while reintroducing the #297 infinite loop. The literal `send_destroy`-before-`send_create` order was enforced only by doc-comment + review.
- Seam (`src/ndi.rs`): added private `trait NdiSendOps { send_create; send_destroy }` separating the two FFI calls from the `libloading::Library`. `NdiLib` impls it as a thin `#[inline]` pass-through to the loaded raw fn pointers (live path byte-identical). Extracted the destroy-first dance into `fn reannounce_dance<O: NdiSendOps>(ops, &mut sender, settings, &mut trigger, current) -> bool`; `reannounce_now` now delegates to it. No behavior change.
- Test (`mod ffi_seam_tests`): `FakeNdi` records `[Op::Destroy(ptr)|Op::Create]` order and models the SDK one-live-sender-per-name rule (create while a same-name handle is live → null = the create-first trap). 3 tests: `reannounce_destroys_old_before_creating_new_and_advances_trigger` (a+c), `null_create_after_destroy_leaves_sender_null_and_trigger_unchanged` (b), `retry_after_failed_create_then_succeeds` (null-slot retry skips destroy, the Drop-null guard).
- RED-on-revert proof: working-tree revert to create-first → recorded order `[Create, Destroy(4096)]`, tests (a) and (b) FAIL ("MUST destroy the old sender BEFORE creating"); restored → 3/3 GREEN + 214/214 lib + 4/4 pure reannounce.
- Tier-0 local: fmt/check/clippy(-D warnings) clean, default features only. Verified ENTIRELY in CI — NO rig/ssh/OBS. Version 1.7.0-dev.141.
- #317 NDI re-announce FFI ordering locked via NdiSendOps mockable test seam — PR #318 merged 600da602, main CI green. Test-seam only (no behavior change), fleet stays dev.140.

## #309 — rig-test #291 no-display drop-in leaked into sibling e2e harness restores (1.7.0-dev.142)
- Bug (still valid, verified by reading current code): `rig-mode.sh test` installs a TRANSIENT no-display systemd drop-in (`/run/.../zz-rig-test-no-display.conf`, #291) to free /dev/fb0. `recording-e2e.sh` cleanup (`systemctl restart camera-box`, line ~234) and `loopback-e2e.sh` remote cleanup (`systemctl start camera-box`, line ~102) restored camera-box WITHOUT removing it → a leftover from a prior `rig-mode.sh test` brings camera-box back in no-display mode (dark interkom return monitor) while the operator believes broadcast is restored (#246-class silent leak). recording-e2e itself uses a full `systemctl stop` (not the drop-in), so the fix is purely defensive against an operator leftover.
- Fix (DRY single-source): new `scripts/lib/rig-test-dropin.sh` owns the `RIG_TEST_DROPIN` path constant + a PURE `rig_test_dropin_clear_cmds [DROPIN]` builder (emits `rm -f` drop-in + `rmdir` + `daemon-reload`, all `|| true` idempotent). rig-mode.sh sources it (painter_stop_remote now uses the builder; literal path removed from all 3 of its sites); recording-e2e.sh injects `$(rig_test_dropin_clear_cmds)` into the cam2 ssh restore before the restart; loopback-e2e.sh carries it to the remote shell via `build_remote_env`'s `RIG_TEST_DROPIN_CLEAR=%q` then `eval "${RIG_TEST_DROPIN_CLEAR:-}"` in the remote cleanup before the start. Path now lives in exactly ONE place.
- RED→GREEN: `tests/harness_rig_test_dropin_cleanup.rs` (6 tests). RED commit 5dcb0b96b — 6/6 FAIL (no lib, no harness wiring). GREEN commit 5f4ba2197 — 6/6 PASS. Headline behavioral test `shared_clear_removes_the_dropin` runs the builder's emitted bash against a fake drop-in and asserts the file is gone (proven without ssh). No regression: rig_mode 14/14, harness_recording_e2e_paths 37/37, harness_remote_env_quoting 1/1 (the #39 injection-safety still holds with the added RIG_TEST_DROPIN_CLEAR field).
- Gotcha for next time: ANY new path that restarts cam2's camera-box must source the helper + clear the drop-in before restart/start (added to `.claude/skills/e2e` SKILL.md). Tier-0 local fmt/check/clippy(-D warnings) clean, default features. Verified ENTIRELY in CI — NO rig/ssh/OBS.

## #328 — obs_phase2 prod-scene/teardown HANG (no overall timeout) → blocked #312 run + held cam1 /dev/video0
- Version 1.7.0-dev.149 (commit 6d2919fa8). Solo PR; bug fix, regression-test-first.
- ROOT CAUSE: `obs_phase2.py` `_rpc`'s read loop drains op-5 EVENTS until the matching op-7 response; while OBS renegotiates an NDI source it floods events, so every `recv()` keeps succeeding within the 10s socket timeout yet the response never comes → the loop spins forever (the RUN_ID 312001 ~28-min prod-scene, then teardown, hang). NOT a sick WS — purely no overall wall-clock deadline. The hung teardown then never reached cam1's device restore, so the #174 burn binary kept holding /dev/video0 → prod camera-box crash-looped (#281 class).
- FIX 1 (commit 8da0a978e): added `OBS_OP_TIMEOUT_S` (default 60s, env-overridable) + pure `_rpc_timed_out(elapsed,timeout)` helper; `_rpc` raises `TimeoutError` past the deadline (fail loud → non-zero exit for prod-scene/setup/switch, caught+warned inside teardown's best-effort guard). `ignore_err` suppresses a normal failed RPC but NEVER the timeout. Also catches `WebSocketTimeoutException` to re-check the deadline on socket silence.
- FIX 2 (commit 8da0a978e): `recording-e2e.sh` cleanup() now frees the cam1/cam2 capture devices FIRST (pkill -9 -f the burn binary, rm, restart camera-box) before/independent of the OBS restore, and wraps every cam ssh + every obs_phase2/obs_burn_filter call in `timeout` (`CLEANUP_SSH_TIMEOUT`=30s, `OBS_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT`=90s, env-overridable). A stuck OBS op can no longer strand /dev/video0.
- Tests: RED ec139ed08 → GREEN 8da0a978e. `tests/python/test_obs_phase2_timeout.py` (pure deadline helper + named/env-overridable constant, 6 cases). `tests/harness_recording_e2e_cleanup_resilient.rs` (cam-device-free BEFORE obs teardown; every OBS call timeout-bounded; pkill -9 force-kill). Python 60/60 local; Rust CI-run.
- Commit hygiene: NO `fix:/Closes/Fixes/Resolves #312` anywhere (would auto-close #312); only `Part of #312`. `Closes #328` on the fix commit + PR body.

## 2026-06-29 — #334 (solo clean-code PR, NO rig)
- Version 1.7.0-dev.151 (commit cc0b429ad). Solo PR; pure Python fix to `scripts/obs_burn_filter.py` + a Python unit test. NO C++/rig (supervisor does rig verification — #281 discipline).
- #334 (Closes): the strih(911002)+stream(911004) measurement burns were ABSENT from the all-cambox recording because the `DistroAV QR Burn (latency probe)` EFFECT filter on the program input was `filterEnabled=False` (confirmed live by the supervisor: `GetSourceFilterList` on strih `NDI cam5` → ENABLED=False). A disabled effect filter's `video_render` is never invoked, so the burn never renders even though `genlock_burn=true` and the C++ setter fires (OBS log shows `genlock: measurement burn ON`). Pure obs_burn_filter.py bug, NOT a C++/genlock bug.
- Two defects fixed: (1) `cmd_check` computed `burn_on = (genlock_burn is True) and present` — no enabled check, so a present-but-DISABLED filter reported a FALSE-POSITIVE `burn_on=True`, letting `recording-e2e.sh [4b/8]` pre-record gate pass with no burn (#195/#257 the gate was meant to catch this). New pure `compute_burn_on(genlock_burn, present, enabled)` requires all three; `cmd_check` now also prints `filter_enabled=<bool>`. (2) `_ensure_filter` early-returned when the filter existed, so `cmd_add` never re-enabled a present-but-disabled filter — now it unconditionally (re-)enables (idempotent). New `_filter_enabled(ws, input)` helper reads `filterEnabled` from `GetSourceFilterList`.
- RED 820a363bd → GREEN 2f588d343. Tests (`tests/python/test_obs_burn_filter.py`, drives a fake `_rpc`, no live OBS): `test_compute_burn_on_false_when_filter_disabled` (the regression), `test_cmd_check_burn_on_false_when_present_but_disabled` (behavioral false-positive RED), `test_cmd_add_reenables_present_but_disabled_filter`. Full python suite 66 passed, ruff clean.
- RIG VERIFICATION PENDING — supervisor must (a) run `obs_burn_filter.py add` on strih `NDI cam5` + stream `NDI 2ME PGM` via the FIXED script and confirm `check` now reports `burn_on` only when `filter_enabled=True`, and (b) re-run an ALL_CAMBOX `recording-e2e.sh` and confirm strih(911002)+stream(911004) burns are PRESENT and per-hop latency is measured.

## 2026-06-30 — #363 restore the HARD optical dual-QR gate in recording-verdict (clean-code PR, NO rig, v1.7.0-dev.166)

- **Why**: #360 (PR #361) weakened `recording-verdict` so the in-window membership became `is_optical(f) || has_node_burn(f)` — a frame with ONLY a software-injected digital burn (no cam2 OPTICAL read) counted as delivered, so an 87%-optically-undecodable run PASSED on the digital burns alone (the fraud the user flagged). The cam2 OPTICAL dual-QR is the ONLY proof of the real camera-captured pixel path; the burns are injected AFTER capture (node→node digital delivery only).
- **Fix** (`src/bin/recording-verdict.rs`): membership reverted to OPTICAL-only for strih/stream (PerRenderTick): `is_optical(f) || (matches!(rate, PerEmittedFrame) && has_node_burn(f))`. cam1 (PerEmittedFrame) KEEPS its burn in-window (the #204 per-emit anti-phantom fix — its burn is genuine per-emit delivery proof), so removing the fallback for it would re-introduce phantom drops; the task's "NOT a phantom chain drop" is honoured.
- **New distinct hard-fail**: `optical_undecodable` — in-span frames whose cam2 optical QR did not decode. New helpers `optical_span()` + `optical_undecodable_in_span()` (single source of the optical boundary). `NodeVerdict.optical_undecodable` field; `is_zero() = contiguity.is_contiguous() && optical_undecodable == 0`. Surfaced in `print_node_verdict` + `node_verdict_json`. An undecodable in-span frame is NEITHER a phantom chain drop (pre-#360) NOR a pass (#360) — it is its own OPTICAL-UNDECODABLE category. No flag/env/threshold/tolerance — the gate is hard and stays hard.
- **TDD** (probe-gated, CI-only — `recording-verdict.rs` is `required-features=["probe"]`, not buildable/testable locally per CLAUDE.md): RED `07673a2ad` → GREEN `eda38cad1`. New test `node_verdict_optical_undecodable_is_a_hard_fail_363` (minimal 3-frame lock). Inverted the two #360 tests: `node_verdict_strih_zero_loss_when_cam2_optical_mostly_undecodable_360` → `node_verdict_fails_when_cam2_optical_mostly_undecodable_363` (87% case now FAILS, optical_undecodable=60, expected_count=11, real_drops=0); `strih_burn_on_a_non_optical_frame_inside_span_is_included_360` → `..._excluded_and_undecodable_363` (non-optical strih frame now excluded + counted undecodable). Updated the #204 test `cam1_burn_on_an_optical_blurred_frame_is_not_a_phantom_drop`: the run now FAILS on optical-undecodable but cam1 still reports NO phantom drop (the #204 anti-phantom contract — locked at the `burn_contiguity_in_window` level by the unchanged `tests/recording_verdict.rs` integration test).
- **Scope**: ONLY the verdict gate logic + its unit tests. Did NOT touch optical-decode robustness (QR size/painter/moiré/focus/exposure) — that is rig work the supervisor drives separately. Issue #363 stays OPEN (PR references it, no Closes) for the rig optical-robustness work.
- No deploy (probe binaries are CI-built artifacts; camera-box has no web dashboard).

## 2026-06-30 — #363 optical-robustness half: decode_qr_luma_all merges plain ∪ Otsu (clean-code PR, NO rig, v1.7.0-dev.167)

- **Why**: after #372 restored the HARD optical gate (`optical_undecodable == 0`), the stream recording still showed ~87% optical-undecodable — but the cam2 optical dual-QR pixels were PRESENT and readable. A DECODER gating bug, not the camera.
- **Root cause** (`src/probe/qr.rs::decode_qr_luma_all`): the Otsu-binarized rqrr retry ran ONLY when the plain pass found NOTHING (`if !first.is_empty() { return first }`). On the stream recording the plain pass reads the crisp DIGITAL BURNS (non-empty) but MISSES the SOFT optical dual-QR (filmed off a monitor: low-contrast + moiré + colour-cast) → the Otsu retry was skipped → the present optical QR was never recovered. PROOF: on the real failing frames f-5.png/f-150.png (run 354003) rqrr returns the optical dual-QR when `binarize_otsu`-ed but NONE on the plain pass.
- **Fix**: ALWAYS run both rqrr passes (plain AND Otsu-binarized) and `merge_payloads` (de-dup by `(run_id,frame_id)`). Result is a SUPERSET of the plain pass. Fixes `decode_qr_luma_all_robust` + `decode_qr_luma_all_fast_then_robust` for free. Cost: +1 cheap full-frame Otsu rqrr pass per OFFLINE-decoded frame; the ~10× tiles stay conditional. `decode_qr_luma_all_tile` unchanged (tile gating is about small node burns, not the soft optical).
- **TDD** (probe-gated, CI-only): version bump `1752e0b26` → RED `27ad90715` → GREEN `77508e3cc`. New test `optical_soft_dual_qr_recovered_on_real_stream_frames` + fixtures `tests/fixtures/optical-soft-f5.png` / `optical-soft-f150.png` (real run-354003 frames): plain pass returns NO run_id 354003; `decode_qr_luma_all` returns BOTH optical halves; the recording per-frame path surfaces it too. Verified locally RED (`decode_qr_luma_all must recover BOTH optical dual-QR halves … got optical frame_ids []`) → GREEN.
- **Test adaptations** (the fix strengthened the full-frame pass — the Otsu union now reads, full-frame, the synthetic 260px/blur-2.8 burn AND 3 of 5 real burn-unreadable fixtures, flipping them to the FAST path — a real improvement): the synthetic "full-frame MISSES it" premise no longer reproduces. `robust_recovers_a_softened_burn_the_full_frame_pass_misses` → `full_frame_otsu_union_recovers_a_softened_burn_bare_rqrr_misses` (now locks the #363 improvement: bare single rqrr misses → Otsu union recovers, same synthetic input). `robust_fallback_taken_when_plain_misses_an_expected_burn` → `fast_then_robust_falls_back_to_robust_on_a_real_burn_unreadable_frame` (the genuine full-frame-miss/tiles-recover gap is detector-coverage on real 4K pixels → repointed to real fixture cam1-frame-1148, burn 911001.1727). `tests/burn_fixture_decode.rs` still green (4/4).
- **Local verify** (sanctioned probe RED→GREEN exception): `cargo build/test --features probe` with `AIRULESET_ALLOW_LOCAL_BUILD=1 # airuleset:build-ok`; qr unit suite 25/25, burn_fixture 4/4, recording_decode 3/3, recording_verdict 12/12, clippy --features probe clean. `cargo clean` after to bound the shared dev1 target/ (#185).
- **Scope**: ONLY `src/probe/qr.rs` (+ fixtures, skill). Did NOT touch the verdict gate logic (recording-verdict.rs is_zero/membership) — that is #372, already merged.
- Closes #363. No deploy (probe binaries are CI-built artifacts; camera-box has no web dashboard).

### 2026-06-30 (cont.) — #364 colour scale → vertical column in the central dual-QR gap (geometry move)

- **Why**: rig proof showed the BOTTOM-band colour scale (y=960..1080) is CROPPED off the bottom by the camera's framing of the cam2 monitor — it never reached the recording, so the gate had nothing to sample. The cam2 PAINTED source (fb0) is clean; only the bottom band was out of frame. The two dual-QR halves ARE captured (they decode), so the central gap between them is reliably in frame.
- **Version**: 1.7.0-dev.168 → 1.7.0-dev.169 (Cargo.toml, commit `06a7577dd`). Same `dev` / PR #378 (Closes #364).
- **Change** (geometry ONLY — did NOT touch `classify_patch` / tolerances; the supervisor calibrates on live rig data): `colour_scale::colour_scale_patches` now takes `(canvas_w, canvas_h, qr_size, top_margin)` and derives the central gap with the SAME formula `blit_qr_bgra`/`render_qr_dual_bgra` use (half = canvas_w/2; each QR centered in its half via `(band_w−qw)/2`; top-anchored at `top_margin` over `qh = qr_size.min(canvas_h)`). New `dual_qr_gap()` helper returns the gap `[left_qr_end, right_qr_start) × [qr_top, qr_bottom)` or `None` when degenerate. The 13 `PATCH_COLOURS` (unchanged — gate contract) stack as a VERTICAL column inside the gap (10px inset each side → x∈[840,1080), y∈[24,724) at default 1920×1080/qr 700/tm 24), last patch absorbs the integer remainder. Removed the old `BAND_H` bottom band.
- **Single source of truth**: both call sites derive the SAME rects — painter `qr::blit_colour_scale_bgra(canvas, w, h, qr_size, top_margin)` (painter.rs passes `params.qr_size` + `qr::TOP_MARGIN_PX`); gate sampler `colour_verify::sample_patch_means`/`verify_rgb_frame` + `colour_sample::{colour_verdict_from_rgb_image,extract_recording_colour_summary}` thread `qr_size`/`top_margin`; `recording-verdict.rs build_node_colour_fail` passes `colour_scale::{DEFAULT_QR_SIZE,TOP_MARGIN_PX}`. `qr::TOP_MARGIN_PX` is now defined as `colour_scale::TOP_MARGIN_PX` (one literal). The column ends at the QR bottom (~724) above all three bottom-anchored burns, so burn-exclusion rects became belt-and-braces (no patch loses pixels).
- **RED→GREEN** (Tier-0, observed `cargo test --lib colour # airuleset:build-ok`): `test:[red]` `1bd8aa1bd` — new central-gap tests with the legacy bottom-band stub body ⇒ 5 FAIL (`every_patch_is_inside_the_central_gap_and_within_canvas`, `no_patch_intersects_a_qr_half_or_any_burn`, `patches_tile_the_column_top_to_bottom_contiguously`, `degenerate_or_too_small_gap_yields_no_patches`, + `colour_verify::sampler_dodges_a_burn_column...`). `fix:[green]` `22ab6e0ec` — real gap-derived column ⇒ all 23 colour tests GREEN. Tests mirror the QR-half + cam1-center-burn + corner-burn rects as consts (like the prior QR mirror) and assert no patch intersects any of them.

  (issue #505) committing directly to `dev` concurrently while this one ran** — violates
  "dispatch serially, one active worker per repo" (two-branch-workflow.md). Handled by pushing
  only through this worker's own last commit each time (`git push origin <own-sha>:dev`, never
  the local `dev` ref, which kept advancing with the other worker's commits) — but a later
  same-directory `git commit` landed on top of their already-advanced HEAD, and pushing that
  commit necessarily carried their ancestry along too (git push always includes ancestors; no
  way to exclude mid-branch commits without a banned force-push). Net effect: PR #506 ended up
  also containing #505's fully-complete, already-TDD'd work (test → fix → docs, 3 commits),
  which auto-closed #505 on merge via its own `fix: #505 ...` commit title (not something this
  worker wrote) — explained on `gh issue comment 505`. #501 stayed OPEN as intended (the #505
  fix says "root-causes #501", not "fixes"). No stray-close of #499/#500's OUT-of-scope
  neighbors occurred. **If dispatching two workers into the same repo/checkout concurrently,
  either use `git worktree` isolation per worker, or serialize dispatch — this collision cost
  real time untangling and could have shipped one worker's unreviewed code through the other's
  PR in a worse case (no auto-close and no CI trigger to catch it).**

## 2026-07-04 — #505 orphan the Linux GL PBO (root-causes #501 imag-nb multiview CPU stall)

(See the #499/#500 entry above + `gh issue comment 505` for the shared-checkout collision story
— this entry covers the fix's own substance and the CI verification completed after the merge.)

- Root cause (#501): imag-nb's 6-source OBS multiview cost ~24ms/frame, CPU 101% of one core,
  GPU idle 7-9%. Traced to `gs_texture_map()` (vendor/obs-studio/libobs-opengl/gl-texture2d.c)
  mapping a persistent per-texture Pixel Unpack Buffer with a bare
  `glMapBuffer(GL_PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER, GL_WRITE_ONLY)` every frame -> implicit CPU<->GPU
  sync/fence (driver must wait for the GPU to finish the PREVIOUS frame's upload before handing
  back a CPU pointer, since the buffer is never re-specified). Windows/D3D11 never pays this
  (`D3D11_MAP_WRITE_DISCARD` never blocks) -- why strih's multiview is 11.5ms.
- Fix: `glMapBufferRange(GL_PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER, 0, size, GL_MAP_WRITE_BIT |
  GL_MAP_INVALIDATE_BUFFER_BIT)` instead -- the same idiom `gl-helpers.c`'s `update_buffer()`
  already uses for vertex/index buffer streaming in this exact codebase. Extracted the PBO
  byte-size formula into a shared `pixel_unpack_buffer_size()` helper (used by both
  `create_pixel_unpack_buffer()` and `gs_texture_map()`) so allocation-time and map-time size
  can't drift apart.
- Investigation finding: `gl-texture3d.c`'s mirrored PBO was deliberately NOT patched -- this
  vendored OBS has no `gs_texture_map`/`gs_voltexture_map` path for `GS_TEXTURE_3D` on the GL
  backend at all (`gs_texture_map` hard-checks `is_texture_2d()`), and the only real
  `gs_voltexture_create` call sites (color-grade-filter.c LUTs) never request `GS_DYNAMIC` --
  confirmed independently by the deep-review subagent via a whole-repo grep, not just asserted.
  So there is no live instance of the anti-pattern there today; a guard test pins this so a
  future 3D map addition is forced to apply the same fix.

## 2026-07-04/05 — #456 range-aware V4L2 capture controls (cam5 dark-image fix; PR #509+#510+#511, v1.7.0-dev.237)

- Root cause: `color_production_controls()`/`certified_cam1_controls()` applied literal V4L2
  values (saturation=50/contrast=50, contrast=75/saturation=0) calibrated against the ShadowCast
  cards' native 0-100 range. cam5's grab card has a 0-255 range (default 128) -- the literal 50
  landed at ~20% of ITS range = dark/washed-out image.
- Fix (PR #509): `ControlIo` gained `query_range(id) -> ControlRange{minimum,maximum,default_value}`
  (VIDIOC_QUERY_EXT_CTRL via `Device::query_controls()`, implemented for the real `Device` + test
  `FakeDevice`). `CaptureControl.value: i64` became `CaptureControl.target: ControlTarget` --
  `Literal(i64)` (explicit `CAMERA_BOX_CAPTURE_CONTROLS=name=value` overrides, never scaled) or
  `RangeScaled{reference_pct}` (both certified sets, resolved via `resolve_control_target` +
  `scale_to_range` against the device's ACTUAL queried range). RED `f49bb7ffa` (2/4 new tests fail:
  the cam5-style 0-255 midpoint + sharp-set scaling), GREEN `9b19b121a`. Version bump `e400f34a1`
  (1.7.0-dev.233->234) was the first commit, per convention.
- Dispatched a nested async `general-purpose` review agent (mirroring `requesting-code-review`)
  in parallel with the merge decision -- it correctly re-invoked this worker on completion (a
  live confirmation that an async `Agent` dispatch from WITHIN an autopilot-worker subagent is
  safe and re-invokes the caller, unlike a `Bash run_in_background` CI poll which is NOT). It
  came back AFTER PR #509 had already merged (`0b7a53db8`) with 2 🟡 + 2 🔵: (1) `ControlRange
  .default_value` was queried but never used -- `scale_to_range` was pure proportional-midpoint
  math, which only happened to be correct for both known cards because their manufacturer default
  equals their numeric midpoint; a future card whose default ISN'T its midpoint would silently
  miss its true neutral; (2) missing test coverage for the SHARP set resolved on a 0-100
  ShadowCast-shaped range; (3) the degenerate-range (`minimum>=maximum`) fallback was silent, no
  log; (4) `query_range` re-enumerates all controls per call (O(n) per call, bounded to 2 calls at
  device open -- documented as a deliberate non-fix rather than wrapping the external `v4l::Device`
  type).
- Rather than revert the already-merged PR, shipped a same-day fast-follow (repo's own established
  pattern, e.g. #501's `9bfaaabfb` post-review commit): PR #510 -- `scale_to_range` now prefers the
  queried `default_value` directly when `reference_pct==50` (sanity-checked inside
  `[minimum,maximum]`), falling back to proportional midpoint only if the default is
  missing/out-of-range; degenerate-range fallback now `tracing::warn!`s; `query_range`'s doc
  comment records the bounded-scope trade-off explicitly. RED `a4318b22d` (a synthetic 0-200/
  default-140 card resolves to the midpoint 100 instead of the queried default 140), GREEN
  `2a59d3c8b`. PR #511 (docs-only) updated `.claude/skills/capture/SKILL.md` with the range-aware
  resolution mechanism + the two-PR lesson.
- All three PRs merged clean (`mergeable:true`, `mergeStateStatus:CLEAN`), main CI green on every
  merge (runs 28721198678, 28721654829, 28722012849). Issue #456 auto-closed via PR #509's `Closes
  #456` (confirmed `gh issue view 456` state=CLOSED). 415 lib tests pass on the final state (57 in
  `capture::tests`).
- NOT done by this worker: live deployment to cam5 + visual verification, and removal of the
  interim systemd drop-in workaround (`/etc/systemd/system/camera-box.service.d/capture-controls.conf`
  -> `CAMERA_BOX_CAPTURE_CONTROLS=contrast=128,saturation=128`) on cam5 itself. cam5 (10.77.9.65) is
  reachable on :22 but this worker has no `DEVICE_ROOT_PW` credential and key-based SSH is refused
  (`Permission denied (publickey,password)`) -- per this repo's own "drive rig steps in supervisor"
  convention (physical rig work belongs to the supervisor/user, not a death-prone worker), left for
  the supervisor/user to deploy + confirm cam5 is no longer dark, then remove the workaround.
