## issue 944 — emit-liveness watchdog (a dead capture loop keeps publishing a frozen NDI frame)

Version 1.7.0-dev.452. Worktree `autopilot-944`; supervisor integrates the round.

**Validated STILL real (not the stale 2 h incident).** The merged issue-945 capture-wedge
watchdog stamps its heartbeat after every `process_frame()` return (Ok OR Err), and
`VideoCapture::process_frame` returns `Ok(())` on a `V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR` buffer BEFORE the emit
callback (`src/capture.rs:1116-1125`). So on a corrupted-but-returning stream the issue-945
heartbeat keeps advancing while `emit_count` never moves → issue-945 reads Alive forever. Nothing
watched EMITTED-frame liveness. The cam4 2 h incident was itself a TRUE wedge (now caught by
issue-945), but the failure CLASS (takes error buffers, stops advancing) has this
capture-alive-but-emit-dead sub-case still uncovered. Scope decision (was needs-user-decision)
already resolved by the maintainer: stop the NDI sender + log at ERROR (source goes gone, not
frozen); the re-open/USB-rebind ladder was withdrawn (harness concern, out of scope here).

**Fix.** New pure Tier-0 `src/emit_freeze.rs` (emit-side sibling of `capture_wedge`), reusing the
issue-945 watchdog framework verbatim:
- `evaluate_emit_freeze(secs_since_emit, secs_since_capture_return, EMIT_FREEZE_THRESHOLD_S=15,
  CAPTURE_FRESH_BOUND_S=5)` → `Frozen` iff emit stale ≥15 s AND the capture-return heartbeat is
  younger than 5 s. Two-input discriminator: in a TRUE wedge both heartbeats freeze together, so
  the capture-return staleness passes the 5 s bound and emit-freeze SUPPRESSES itself → issue-945
  owns the wedge at 25 s. Compile-time `const _` guard `15 > 5 > 0` (clippy-safe).
- A second `Arc<AtomicU64>` emit heartbeat, stamped in the capture loop's `Ok` arm on a per-iteration
  `frame_dispatched` flag — set ONLY on a confirmed production send (`Ok`) or a queued burn job
  (`ring.submit` `Ok`), NOT on `emit_count` (which increments even on a send Err). Armed after the
  first dispatch (0-sentinel) so boot/NDI warmup never false-fires.
- The poll folds into the EXISTING issue-945 watchdog thread, AFTER the wedge check; on `Frozen`
  → `tracing::error!` a uniquely grep-able CRITICAL line + `std::process::exit(81)` (distinct from
  77/78/79/80) → systemd `Restart=always` tears the NDI sender down + re-opens the device.
- Adjacent (ticket ask): a periodic `#944 last-emit-age` info line on the 5 s stats cadence.

RED `ca9c40492` (stub always Publishing) → GREEN `e0f84f065` → review 🔵 fix `024270487`
(stamp on confirmed dispatch, catching a persistently-failing send too). Test:
`emit_freeze::tests::stale_emit_while_capture_returning_is_frozen` (RED on stub → GREEN), 9/9.
Tier-0: fmt clean, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.

## 2026-08-14 — flaky-test hardening bundle #970 + #980 + #975 (worktree autopilot-970, v1.7.0-dev.452)

#970 + #980 (SAME root cause, two facets): `rig_lease_holder_summary()` (scripts/lib/rig-lease.sh)
read holder.json via FIVE separate python3 field-reads; a releasing foreign holder rm-ing the
lockdir mid-summary TORE the read — `repo` succeeded then the file vanished and the rest read empty,
logging `RIG_LEASE_HELD_BY=zbynekdrlik/restreamer# run_url= job=` (#970) or `unknown (corrupt
holder.json)` (#980), flaking `foreign_lease_released_within_wait_budget_lets_us_proceed` in
tests/harness_rig_busy_gate_lease_830.rs. Reproduced 250/250 FAIL under 10x parallel load (0/60 at
low load). #980's "shared lockdir across sibling tests" hypothesis was wrong — tests already isolate
RIG_LEASE_DIR per-test; the race is intra-test (releaser thread vs summary), widened by load.
Fix (two structural-immunity parts): (1) rig_lease_holder_summary now reads holder.json in ONE
python3 open()+json.load() that formats the whole line — a concurrent unlink after open() cannot
truncate an already-open FD on Linux, so the result is all-or-nothing; output format byte-identical
(harness_rig_lease.rs + rig-busy-gate.sh sed parsing unchanged). (2) the flaky integration test now
releases the foreign holder DETERMINISTICALLY via a RIG_LEASE_RUN_STATUS_CMD stub that removes the
lockdir on the gate's 2nd poll (after poll 0 has observed+logged the live holder), replacing a
600ms wall-clock sleep that raced the gate's load-dependent first read. New deterministic RED test
tests/harness_rig_lease_holder_summary_atomicity_980.rs (python3 shim deletes holder.json after the
first read → RED on 5-read, GREEN on atomic). Post-fix: 376 whole-binary runs under 8x load + 40/40
no-load, 0 failures. Commits: RED test 06a0f3968, GREEN fix 1cf252db2, fmt 319c0d650.

#975: tests/harness_deploy_fleet.rs `run_fleet` keyed its per-call temp dir on pid(constant across
all test threads in one binary) + nanos, so two concurrent calls that read the same clock tick
shared a bin/ dir and their PATH-injected sha256sum stubs collided (a sha_match:false call's "bbbb"
stub contaminating a sha_match:true call — the `local aaaa != remote bbbb` coverage-runner flake).
Rare timing collision (SystemTime has true-ns resolution here — not reproducible on demand);
structural fix = tempfile::tempdir() (kernel-atomic O_EXCL, cannot collide; Drop cleanup removes the
manual remove_dir_all race too). 185 whole-binary runs under 8x load, 0 failures; 16/16 suite green.
Commit d3b875c13. GOTCHA for future workers: any test-harness helper that hand-rolls a temp path
from pid+timestamp is a latent collision — pid is constant within a binary, so timestamp is the only
key; use tempfile::tempdir() instead.

Worktree round; supervisor integrates (merge → CI → deploy). One PR closes #970 #975 #980.

## issue 1001 — strih/stream network-UNREACHABLE dev1-side alert watchdog (autopilot, worktree)

Closed the silent-outage gap: strih's NIC died 2026-08-06 (~50 min off the wire, no alert),
recurred 2026-08-13. Every existing watchdog probes a box it assumes is UP (OBS-WS GetStats / ssh
INTO the box) and treats a total outage as "no probe output = nothing to decide". Built a NEW
dev1-side systemd-timer watchdog that probes both boxes FROM dev1 with a MULTI-SIGNAL check
(ping OR TCP :4455 OBS-WS OR TCP :8899 bundle-state) — REACHABLE iff ANY, UNREACHABLE only when all
three fail (so an ICMP-firewalled-but-TCP-up Windows box is never a false page). Mirrors the
dev1-side topology + shared confirm/throttle framework of the imag-obs (882) / imag-power-envelope
(1040) / optical-chain (860) siblings; the intentional difference is probing FROM dev1 without
ssh-ing IN (impossible against an off-network box).

- Files: `scripts/lib/network-reach-health.sh` (pure seam), `scripts/network-reach-alert-watchdog.sh`,
  `systemd/network-reach-alert-watchdog.{service,timer}`, `tests/harness_network_reach_health_1001.rs`,
  `.claude/rules/network-reach-watchdog.md` (+ CLAUDE.md router).
- Per-box state (confirm/alert_sig/alert_passes/alerted) so strih+stream page independently;
  2-pass confirm; ~1h throttle; a one-shot recovery ("reachable again") ping.
- dev1-side-outage guard: any REACHABLE watched box OR any reference-node ping proves connectivity;
  only when NOTHING is reachable is the pass "nothing to decide" (never a false "both boxes down").
  Event-safe (generous timeouts for the tailscale-over-mobile venue link).
- RED `f177becce` → GREEN lib `fb7221b3f` (net_reach_classify_box / any_reachable / recovery_decision
  / alert_detail); watchdog+units `a0fe99f5c`; fmt `1b5df6c4e`; review-hardening `4d36c07e9`
  (anchor counts box-reachability, dry-run state isolation, injection-shape removed, single-probe,
  +ping-up test). Tests 11/11; shellcheck -x / fmt / clippy / cargo test --no-run all green.
- Review: SHIP, 0 red/yellow; 5 of 6 blue folded in, 1 dropped with reasoning (controlled alnum
  box names in sed keys). WoL BIOS enablement floated on the ticket = separate hardware follow-up,
  not bundled. Worktree; supervisor integrates the round.

## 2026-08-14 — harness-robustness bundle #857 + #850 (worktree autopilot-857, v1.7.0-dev.454)

#857: `rig_lease_release()` (scripts/lib/rig-lease.sh) tore the shared cross-repo rig lockdir down
with a non-atomic `rm -rf "$d"`. A recursive delete removes the dir CONTENTS (holder.json,
heartbeat) BEFORE the inode, exposing a "dir present, holder.json gone" window. The read side was
already made atomic by #970/#980; this is the WRITE side. In the window: (a) a reader logs an
unnamed holder; worse (b) a concurrent `rig_lease_acquire`'s `mkdir "$d"` fails EEXIST against a
holder-less dir, reclaims into `$d`, and has that fresh lease deleted by the departing release
(two runs momentarily both believing they hold the rig — proven by the RED test's acquire-race).
Fix: `mv "$d" "$d.releasing.$$"` (one atomic syscall: $d goes complete→absent) then `rm -rf` the
detached copy; new `rig_lease_sweep_releasing()` (called from acquire-entry + release) GCs any
`.releasing.*` copy leaked by a crash between the rename and the rm. NO `rm -rf "$d"` fallback on
mv-failure — the stale-reclaim heartbeat backstop self-heals a rare fs-error leftover, and a
fallback would reintroduce the exact window. RED test tests/harness_rig_lease_release_atomicity_857.rs
uses a PATH `rm` shim faithfully reproducing rm -rf's contents-first order + probes the torn window
AND drives a concurrent acquirer during the window (deterministic, no timing). RED `9de522651` /
GREEN `b74afe4a6` / fmt `0aa94385a`. shellcheck clean; 150/150 serial after 800 parallel shim runs.
GOTCHA discovered: the RED run (pre-fix) LEAKS a SIGTERM-immune orphan that INHERITS and holds the
test's stdout pipe open, so a `cargo test ... | tail` pipeline blocks forever until you `kill -9`
the orphan — kill it to flush the FAILED line.

#850: `struct Fixture` (tests/harness_rig_test_ledger_723.rs) had no `impl Drop`; every test's
explicit `fixture.force_kill()` is its LAST statement, so an earlier assert failure unwinds past it
and leaks the child. The SIGTERM-immune fixture (`trap "" TERM`, deliberate for the #721/#723
escalation proof) then reparents to init and only `kill -9` removes it — the five audited
`cam2-painter-stubborn` orphans. Fix: `impl Drop for Fixture { fn drop(&mut self){ self.force_kill(); } }`
(runs during unwind; force_kill idempotent so existing explicit calls stay a no-op — the fixture's
SIGTERM-immunity is untouched). RED test panics in a `catch_unwind` block before force_kill, then
asserts the pid is reaped. RED `83f54f66c` / GREEN `ce0390553`. 17/17 ledger tests green; 60/60
stress runs, zero orphan accumulation.

Worktree round; supervisor integrates (merge → CI → deploy). One PR closes #857 #850.

## 2026-08-14 — issue 916: rig→dev1 silent-drop VALIDATED CLOSED (no longer reproduces) + docs sync (docs-only)
- **Validate-first**: reproduced LIVE from CAM1 (10.77.9.61) → dev1's CURRENT rig IP (drifted to
  10.77.9.103 on enp2s0). Ping 3/3 0% loss; dev1 tcpdump shows an ICMP echo REPLY for every
  request; a full TCP 3-way handshake to a fresh `nc -l 0.0.0.0 9916` listener completes
  (S/S./ack/clean FIN). The 2026-08-01 symptom (ICMP arrives, kernel silently drops, no reply) is
  GONE. → closed with evidence (validator obsolete path; user's auto-close-overcome preference).
- **Root cause (inferred, consistent)**: dev1 multi-homed on the rig L2 via two NICs — enp1s0
  (MAC …c0, the incident NIC at .100) + enp2s0 (MAC …c1). Packet arrived on the ARP'd NIC while
  the kernel reply path resolved to the other → asymmetric-path silent drop (classic rp_filter /
  ARP-flux multi-homing failure). Resolved by the environment: enp1s0 is now DOWN/NO-CARRIER (rig
  on a single clean enp2s0), and rp_filter is persistently LOOSE (=2, /etc/sysctl.d/10-network-
  security.conf), which cannot silent-drop a source reachable via any iface.
- **No kernel/sysctl change applied** — rp_filter already loose+persistent and the incident NIC
  already down; a redundant nft/sysctl rule would be a patch on a non-problem (rejected — would
  change host-wide policy the tailscale/wg/zerotier ifaces rely on, for a bug that no longer
  exists). Belt-and-braces dev1-initiated deploys retained at zero blast radius.
- **Docs synced**: `.claude/skills/genlock/SKILL.md` (deploy-transfer bullet) + two notes in
  `.claude/rules/rig-state-inspection.md` now record box-pull works, keep dev1-initiated as the
  default, and correct the drifted IP/NIC (enp2s0/.103). Docs-only PR; self-review (no repo code).
  Version bump 1.7.0-dev.453. Observation (not this bug, out of scope): a uvicorn service binds
  :8791 on the tailscale IP only, not the rig IP — a service-binding matter, distinct from the
  kernel drop.

## issues #946 + #910 — unified run-integrity restart-event attribution (capture-wedge/emit-freeze + burn-log source) — 2026-08-14 (worktree autopilot-946, v1.7.0-dev.453)

- **Problem**: recording-verdict's per-window forensics had two blind spots in the restart-event
  attribution scan. (910) The self-heal-reset scan only grepped journald, but during an E2E burn
  each camera runs as a transient systemd-run unit logging to `/tmp/cbox-burn.log` (source) /
  `/tmp/cbox-burn-<cam>.log` (secondary) — journald is structurally blind to the recording window,
  so a `#663` reset there came back empty and its stale frames misclassified as `frozen_leg`.
  (946) The issue-945 capture-wedge (exit 79, `CRITICAL #945: capture/emit thread WEDGED`) and
  issue-944 emit-freeze (exit 81, `CRITICAL #944: NDI output FROZEN`) watchdog restarts were not
  correlated at all, surfacing as anonymous frozen_leg.
- **Fix**: ONE recognised-event table (`scripts/lib/self-heal-attribution.sh`'s `restart_event_*`
  functions) replacing three parallel greps — the shared #663 reset line + both watchdog CRITICAL
  lines. Read from BOTH journald AND each camera's burn-instance log (the burn log is
  tracing-subscriber stdout: ANSI-colour-wrapped, microsecond RFC3339-Z timestamps — ANSI-strip +
  `date -u -d "$ts" +%s%N`, mirroring the issue-992 capture-rate burn-log read). The pure Rust seam
  (`src/self_heal_attribution.rs`) gained `RestartEventKind` (SelfHealReset|CaptureWedge|EmitFreeze)
  carried by the event + attributed leg; `parse` accepts tagged `kind:cambox:ns` AND legacy
  `cambox:ns` (→ SelfHealReset). The harness threads `--restart-event KIND:CAMBOX:EPOCH_NS`;
  recording-verdict merges it with the legacy `--self-heal-reset` and tags each JSON entry + line
  with its kind. ALLOW-not-SUPPRESS preserved: a wedge/emit-freeze event still gates via
  `any_self_heal()`; `overall_pass_contribution()` untouched (report-only, #914).
- **Design decision**: extended the existing attribution seam in place (kind-tagged) rather than a
  sibling module — the correlation engine + gating + report shape are identical for all three, and
  a sibling parser is exactly the "competing attribution parser" the governing rule + the
  capture_wedge/emit_freeze module docs warn against. JSON key `self_heal_reset` + `--self-heal-reset`
  flag kept for back-compat (recording-verdict.rs is probe-gated, zero local test path).
- **Commits**: add57e237 (version) · 1cee31c8a/46690c477 (RED/GREEN Rust kind seam) ·
  8136a897b/6854accc8 (RED/GREEN bash table + burn-log parser) · d14c9ba18 (wiring: e2e scan +
  verdict flag + lib-helper removal).
- **Tests**: `src/self_heal_attribution.rs` 23/23 (`cargo test --lib self_heal_attribution`),
  `tests/harness_self_heal_attribution_895.rs` 14/14 (unified table + burn-log RFC3339 parse +
  wiring asserts; removed 5 superseded self-heal-only helper tests). fmt + clippy -D warnings +

  edit — anchor-collision guard); review-confirmed no `.find()`/region-slice collision from the

## 2026-08-14 — issue 1004: dock-vs-gate residual quantified UNSTABLE → no compensation (v1.7.0-dev.453)
- **Quantify**: paired the dock's own sign-corrected `av-sync-dock LOCKED/UPDATED offset=` lines
  (from the STREAM box OBS log — the dock locks on STREAM, not strih: `mbc` marker source lives
  there; strih logs `source 'mbc' not found` and never locks) against the offline optical
  `recording-verdict --av-sync` truth (`all_cambox_av_sync.av_offset_ms`) in the SAME recording
  window, across 5 healthy post-phase-fix E2E runs today. No fresh rig run (supervisor gate runs
  in flight; passive log/verdict reading only, per dispatch).
- **Finding**: dock − offline central ~+32ms but run-to-run spread +9..+53ms (σ ~13–15), AND the
  dock's OWN within-window swing (24–75ms, cluster mad 25–35ms, lock glitches to −805/+207ms)
  EXCEEDS that spread while offline is stable. Issue 952's ~55ms is NOT reproduced as a stable
  constant. No additive value reconciles the two different taps to the ±20ms the tightened gate
  needs → compensating would inject false precision.
- **Decision (from data, not a user fork)**: UNSTABLE → NO compensation. Kept
  `dock_lock_display_offset_ms` a pure sign negation (value byte-identical → parity gate
  untouched). Added the MEASURED, LOCKED additive term `DOCK_LOCK_DISPLAY_ADDITIVE_MS = 0.0`
  (Rust const + C++ `constexpr` + `static_assert`), guarded by
  `dock_lock_display_applies_zero_additive_1004` so no future edit can silently reintroduce a
  guessed constant. Offline optical `--av-sync` stays the sole authoritative gate; the dock is a
  coarse monitor. Unblocks the ±90→±20 gate tightening (the discrepancy is an expected monitor
  taps-bias, not evidence the offline gate is wrong).
- **Rejected**: (a) compensate with a measured constant (~+32) — residual not stable to ±20ms, a
  "measured" constant here is a guessed one wearing a measurement's clothes; (b) derive
  gate-equivalent from dock via a stable mapping — requires a stable relation that does not exist.
- **RED** `baeadee8f` / **GREEN** `3fe553b60` / review-polish `ce950e5df`, version bump
  `03e15b1c6`. Tests: guard `dock_lock_display_applies_zero_additive_1004` + `av_sync_dock_cpp_mirror_gate`
  (parity) + `av_sync_dock_latency_display_999` + `av_sync_dock_suggested_target_953` all green;
  fmt + clippy `-D warnings` clean. Review: 0🔴 0🟡 3🔵 (2 fixed, 1 kept-by-design).

## issue 1052 — stream FROZEN-INPUT dev1-side alert watchdog (network-reach phase 2, worktree)

Version 1.7.0-dev.453. Worktree `autopilot-1052`; supervisor integrates the round.

**Validated STILL real.** Reachability (#1001) only classifies a box REACHABLE/UNREACHABLE, blind
to a REACHABLE box whose NDI input is frozen on the last frame (the #767 receiver-rebind class).
Emit-freeze (#944) is CAMBOX-side and never fires for a receiver-side freeze. The closest existing
check, `scripts/frozen-camera-gate.py` (#365), is STRIH-side, screenshot-hash, and E2E-gate-scoped
(TEST mode, needs OBS-WS + scene warm-up) — zero coverage of the stream `NDI 2ME PGM` program feed
during a live event. So the class is genuinely uncovered.

**Tap decision (design comment on the issue): genlock-fifo `received=` per-source counter.** The
stream OBS log prints `genlock-fifo audit '<src>': received=N …` ~every 5 s
(`GENLOCK_AUDIT_LOG_INTERVAL_NS`); `received=` counts frames the FIFO RECEIVED, so a frozen input
stops advancing it. Chosen over (b) `GetSourceScreenshot` hash-delta — false-frozen on a live-but-
static source (a held slide), needs OBS-WS + scene activation each pass — and (c) QR/burn decode —
heaviest, TEST-mode only. `received=` works in BOTH test and event mode and is immune to static
content. Per-pass state-delta model (sample newest `received=`, persist, compare to prior pass)
sidesteps the audit's ~5 s intra-log cadence trap.

**Files.**
- Pure Tier-0 seam `scripts/lib/frozen-input-health.sh` (mirrors `network-reach-health.sh`):
  `frozen_input_classify <prev> <curr> <expected_live> <sender_reachable>` →
  FROZEN | ADVANCING | UNKNOWN | SKIP (SKIP first when not expected-live or the sender/receiver box
  is unreachable; UNKNOWN on no-prior / unreadable-current / counter-reset — never a false page),
  `frozen_input_recovery_decision`, `frozen_input_alert_detail`. Confirm/throttle stay the shared
  `obs-watchdog-decision.sh`.
- Impure watchdog `scripts/frozen-input-alert-watchdog.sh` (mirrors `network-reach-alert-watchdog.sh`):
  best-effort ONE flat `ssh … powershell` OBS-log tail (session-agnostic read, NEVER nested
  PowerShell — win-ssh-vs-mcp / rig-state-inspection), `FROZEN_INPUT_PROBE_CMD`-overridable. Reads
  #1001's OWN on-disk state (`alerted_<box>`) for the no-double-page guard — never re-probes.
- `systemd/frozen-input-alert-watchdog.{service,timer}` (dev1, 5-min cadence, ~10-15 min to page).
- `tests/harness_frozen_input_health_1052.rs`; `.claude/rules/frozen-input-watchdog.md` + CLAUDE.md
  router.

**TDD.** RED `54168a814` (harness sources the absent lib → `command not found`, rc=127) → GREEN lib
`760d4cf55` → watchdog+units. Rust harness 11/11 GREEN; the full watchdog flow (seed→UNKNOWN, 2-pass
confirm→alert, advancing→recovery, sender-unreachable→SKIP) smoke-tested via `--dry-run` with a stub
probe. shellcheck -x clean on both scripts.

**Future enhancement (recorded, not built):** surface `received=` from the `:8899` bundle-state
server so dev1 reads it via HTTP GET (retiring the ssh read) — deferred, needs an updated

## 1055 — dantesync-gate client rows slew-aware (master-independent journal step-correlation)

- Root cause: a CLIENT's 6-sample HTTP median lands in a master deadband-slew plateau (+2.7–3.3 ms
  transient, ~30–60 s) → drift_unstable. The #1022/#1041 client widening only covers this when the
  Windows master's `/status` is readable at gate-prime time (~50 % flaky live); when empty, the
  client is graded on the bare 2000 µs bound and false-DRIFTs. chase_bimodal only rescues an
  `unstable` (median-in-bound) verdict, never median-out-of-bound.
- Fix: `slew_transient_exclusion_verdict` / `slew_excluded_survivors_us` /
  `_newest_correction_epoch` / `slew_transient_exclusion_check` in `scripts/clock-offset-guard.sh`.
  The client's OWN journal co-timestamps each slew-transient `[NTP] offset:` sample with a
  `[NTP] (Stepped|step candidate)` marker; exclude samples within `--slew-step-window-s` (5 s) of a
  marker and pass only when the POST-most-recent-correction survivors (≥1, `--slew-min-surviving`=3
  window-sanity total) have a median in bound. Wired into `grade_http_node` as a linux-client rescue
  consulted only when the raw verdict is drift/drift_unstable and chase_bimodal said no.
- Adversarial review (fresh-context, 0🔴 1🟡 1🔵) found + I fixed the onset-drift masking hole:
  grade only survivors NEWER than the newest correction marker (proof the clock returned to µs-grade
  AFTER its last correction), so pre-onset baseline can't dilute an ongoing drift's median.
- Calibrated from today's live cam1/cam2 journals (spikes each bracketed by step markers, baseline
  µs; window insensitive at 5/10/20 s). RED→GREEN: tests/clock_offset_guard.rs (10 slew tests incl.
  onset-drift + recency-floor) + tests/dantesync_gate.rs (2 e2e: transient rescued, sustained desync
  still fails). Version 1.7.0-dev.454.
- Gotcha logged to `.claude/rules/dantesync-clock-offset-gate.md`: journal fixture env is a FILE
  PATH (not content); distinct `updated_ts` per HTTP sample; awk-rewrite drops the script +x bit.

  `true` and renders the QR burn onto the LIVE IMAG projection. The `[0/8]` exhaustive sweep only
  runs during a dev1 gate run, never on the box's OWN restart. Fix: force measurement burns OFF at
  imag OBS start in `imag_scenes.py --bootstrap` (the seam `imag-obs-start.sh` runs on every fresh
  instance — boot autostart, operator start, systemd Restart=on-failure). New pure
  `ndi_source_names()` (enumerate ndi_source inputs from GetInputList — NEVER a static/CAMS list,
  burn-target-enumeration rule) + `clear_measurement_burns()` (clear genlock_burn=false on every ON
  ndi input, read-back verify). Bootstrap-gated (like the 785 self-heal) so a bare reseed never
  nukes a burn a gate run set mid-measurement.
- **Standalone-seam decision:** `imag_scenes.py` is fetched standalone to `/usr/local/bin` and
  cannot import `obs_burn_filter.py` (not deployed to the box), so the tiny enumerate+clear is
  reimplemented locally — the SAME established imag precedent as `imag_latency_enforce.py`'s own
  `list_ndi_inputs`. The "route through ONE seam" rule is `paths:`-scoped to the shell consumers
  (rig-mode, recording-e2e), not this box script.
- **TDD:** RED `7c7951163` (functions absent → AttributeError) → GREEN `17ed4ce9c` → review-fix
  `57c43157a`. 9 pytest cases (pure enumerator + fake-WS clear: clears only ON, overlay merge,
  no-op when none ON, warn-not-abort on enum-failure / WS-raise-during-enum / WS-raise-mid-sweep /
  stuck-clear). No `.sh` touched → no static-anchor risk, no full-suite requirement; Python-only.

  hiccup" outcome the code prevents). Hardened the WHOLE sweep body in try/except → warn-and-return,

  Restart=on-failure = OBS restart loop). `clear_measurement_burns` now can NEVER abort OBS start;

New helpers `_dante_line_iso_ts`/`_servo_cadence_s`, env consts `PTP_LOCK_SERVO_GRACE_FACTOR`/`_FLOOR_S`. ## 2026-08-15 — #837 spread/stability check on the DanteSync journal-fallback path (worktree autopilot-837)
- **Root cause:** `dantesync_offset_verdict` (scripts/clock-offset-guard.sh) graded the MEDIAN alone (ok|drift|stale|absent) — no spread concept, `spread_of_ints` never called on the journal path. So a --linux node whose HTTP endpoint is unreachable (journal fallback) with a scattered-but-in-bound-median clock passed silently — the exact gap issue 836 closed for the HTTP path (sampled_offset_verdict). Reproduced live by sourcing: a 3-sample journal (median +10us, spread ~17900us) graded `ok`.
- **Fix (RED 5c1a32503 / GREEN e66fcf683 / review 598ad4129):** mirror the HTTP path exactly. New pure `_fresh_offset_samples_us` exposes the raw fresh set (ONE parse — the issue-595 single-source discipline); `_fresh_offset_median_us` refactored to `median_of_ints "$(_fresh_offset_samples_us …)"`, new `_fresh_offset_spread_us` = `spread_of_ints "$(…)"`. `dantesync_offset_verdict` gains an OPTIONAL 4th STABILITY_US arg: omitted = median-only byte-for-byte (every 3-arg caller unchanged, same back-compat model as sampled_offset_verdict's issue-1014 MODE arg); present = grade spread of the SAME K=11 fresh set, adding `unstable`/`drift_unstable` (same words as the HTTP path); non-numeric fails closed to `unstable` (the issue-595 numeric-guard gotcha). Callers gate on it: offset_verdict_check (+ CLI `--stability-us`/`DANTESYNC_STABILITY_US`), dantesync-gate.sh journal-fallback (passes GATE_STABILITY_US), verify-device.sh (DEVICE_CLOCK_STABILITY_US), verify-imag.sh (IMAG_CLOCK_STABILITY_US) — all default 2000us via the shared DANTESYNC_STABILITY_US.
- **Invariant honored:** strictly MORE failures, never fewer — the location bound never moves; the spread check only ever turns a today-`ok` into `unstable` or a today-`drift` into `drift_unstable`.
- **Deliberately NOT folded in — the issue-1055 slew-transient rescue.** It rescues a would-be median-`drift` too, so applying it here would turn a node that `drift`s TODAY into `ok` = FEWER failures = violates the invariant. The HTTP path itself landed the strict issue-836 check first and added the 1022/1041/1055 rescues later after live false-fails; the journal path mirrors that sequencing. Documented on the ticket, not filed (speculative — no observed false-fail).
- **Verification:** local RED proven by sourcing the pre-fix script; GREEN by sourcing + running the compiled test binaries directly (the local cargo RUN is disabled repo-wide, build-ok off — but `cargo test --no-run` compiles and the built binaries execute the `run_sourced` bash wrappers cheaply). 14 new #837 tests (9 verdict-unit + 2 CLI + 3 gate) pass; full clock_offset_guard 139 + dantesync_gate 76 stay green, 0 failed. shellcheck -x clean (verify-device/imag SC2317 = documented source-guard false-positives; the SC2015/SC2016 in verify-imag.sh are pre-existing, none on changed lines).
- **Gotcha (set -e in run_sourced):** the sourced clock-offset-guard.sh runs `set -euo pipefail`, so after sourcing the harness has `-e` active even though run_sourced starts with only `set -uo pipefail`. A test body calling an rc-2-returning function (offset_verdict_check) MUST guard it `rc=0; fn … || rc=$?` or the whole harness aborts and run_sourced's success-assert fails. The plain verdict functions (return 0, printf a word) are unaffected.
- Version 1.7.0-dev.457. Worktree autopilot-837; supervisor integrates.

  one EXPORTed libobs seam `obs_aux_sender_should_skip()` (obs.c) reads the tick globals + delegates
  to `obs_display_should_skip()`; `ndi-filter.cpp` gates its render+send with per-filter EWMA/counters.
  Program priority is STRUCTURAL (different source type, never routed through the gate; runs first).
  Audio path (`ndi_filter_asyncaudio`) untouched. Per-sender cadence via optional
  `ndi_filter_render_divisor` settings key (default 2; effective 1 on 30fps strih = pure budget gate).
- Commits: 696cd4b31 (bump) · 5f819cfaf [red]/1dd38b798 [green] effective_render_divisor Tier-0 seam ·
  9bcfeaa7c C enforcement · 3e98d5b33 parity+invariant harness (tests/aux_sender_budget_879.rs) +
  lock-step anchors (genlock_preload.rs + both windows-genlock*.yml) · 5a88cead8 review fixes.

## issue 1063 — order-independent aux-sender budget term (worktree autopilot-1063, v1.7.0-dev.458)
- Follow-up hardening of the issue-879 aux-NDI-sender render-budget gate. Root cause: the 879 seam
  `obs_aux_sender_should_skip()` fed `obs_display_should_skip()` a term `elapsed = now -
  graphics_frame_start_ns`, which reflects the program's cost ONLY if the aux ndi_filter decides
  AFTER `output_frames()` in the tick. An aux filter deciding EARLY reads a small `elapsed`, sees
  false budget headroom, and never throttles (render-order-dependent effectiveness; not a
  program-priority violation — the program is a separate ndi_output path).
- Fix (cross-cutting, one new graphics-thread global): `obs_graphics_thread_loop()` (obs-video.c)
  publishes the PREVIOUS tick's completed `frame_time_ns` into new `obs->video.last_tick_total_ns`
  (obs-internal.h); the seam gates on `max(elapsed, last_tick_total_ns)` via a ternary `consumed`
  (obs.c). Order-independent; fail-open (field 0 before the first completed tick = byte-identical to
  `elapsed` at startup). No signature/EXPORT change; no new deploy-coupling beyond 879's obs64 rebuild.
- Commits: 7bda63231 (bump) · ca2cd105c [red] (tests/aux_sender_budget_879.rs new test
  c_aux_sender_order_independent_budget_1063) · 12d1335c4 [green] (obs-internal.h/obs-video.c/obs.c +
  existing-stub field update + genlock_preload.rs anchors + both windows-genlock*.yml pwsh mirrors).
- Verify: standalone `cc` lift of the seam under -Werror — RED (current seam: early-decide + 28ms
  prior tick renders instead of skipping) → GREEN (fixed seam skips; startup/warmup/program-priority/
  late-decide invariants all hold). Anchors verified against the real squished C via a Python replica
  of both squish algorithms (pwsh not on dev1). Tier-0: fmt/clippy/`test --no-run` all clean.
- GOTCHA (seam brace-freedom): `tests/aux_sender_budget_879.rs` finds the seam's closing brace via
  the FIRST `"\n}"` after the signature, so the seam must stay brace-free — the new max-term uses a
  `? :` ternary precisely to avoid a nested `{}` block.
## issue 1060 — dev1 fresh-OBS-start burn-reconcile watchdog for unattended starts (worktree autopilot-1060, v1.7.0-dev.459)
- Follow-up to issue 1057. 1057 closed the DELIBERATE dev1-driven relaunch burn-resurrection window
  (launch-obs-genlock.sh's PLAN directs a post-launch obs_burn_filter.py sweep-off). Still open: the
  UNATTENDED strih/stream OBS starts (boot autostart, NL_STARTUP.ahk obs64 respawn, the issue-411
  self-heal Task-Scheduler relaunch) — all reuse launch-obs-genlock.sh's emitted PowerShell which
  never touches the burn, and the Windows box has no on-box python/WS client, so a saved
  genlock_burn=true reloads onto the LIVE program until the next gate run.
- Design (chosen candidate 1, dev1-side; on-box WS client rejected — issue 866 deployed-dep cost):
  ONE dev1 systemd --user timer keying on the OBS RESTART (not the cause), covering all three paths.
  Load-bearing discriminator = a FRESH OBS START, never "a burn is present": a persistent TEST-mode
  burn is legitimate operator state whose #281 rig heartbeat goes stale after ~10 min while the burn
  should remain. Fresh-start signal = GetStats.renderTotalFrames (monotone since OBS start, resets on
  restart) over the SAME WS obs_burn_filter speaks. Coordination = defer while a fresh #281 heartbeat
  OR a held #830 rig lease exists (never clear a burn a live gate/TEST set). Burn clear reuses the
  #938/#1011 enumerator; fail-CLOSED on an un-enumerable box.
- Files: scripts/lib/obs-burn-reconcile-decision.sh (pure NOOP/DEFER/SWEEP/CLEAN + fresh-start),
  obs_burn_filter.py (+session-probe action + render_total_frames pure helper),
  obs-burn-reconcile-watchdog.sh (per-box probe→decide→reconcile), systemd .service/.timer/.README
  (SHIPS DISABLED), tests/python/test_obs_burn_reconcile_decision.py + test_obs_burn_filter.py
  additions + tests/harness_obs_burn_reconcile_watchdog_1060.rs.
- Commits: 3775ce42c (bump) · eec20c702 [red] · bdf98f926 [green] · 706dfb9b2 (review fixes).
- REVIEW-DRIVEN HARDENING (the important lesson): the fresh-start baseline first lived in tmpfs
  (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tmp), wiped on every dev1 reboot. With "unknown baseline = fresh" that would
  false-clear a persistent TEST burn on the first post-reboot pass even though OBS never restarted.
  Fix: unknown/corrupt prev is NOT a restart (seed only) — ONLY an OBSERVED counter drop reconciles;
  baseline persisted in durable ~/.camera-box. Plus a self-healing `unresolved` retry (a
  partially-failed sweep-off retries until read-back clean, set only off an observed restart).
- Verify: no local cargo-test path (Tier-0, build-ok disabled) — decision truth table proven via the
  runnable python twin; watchdog wiring proven via an offline smoke with a stubbed obs_burn_filter +
  notify (seed/NOOP never sweeps unknown baseline; SWEEP on observed drop; retry self-heals; DEFER
  while coordinated; fail-closed enum). Tier-0: fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --no-run clean; 24 py.

## #870 — per-hop burn-id uniqueness / max-hold assertion (zero-loss gate blind to a REPEATING hop)

- Root cause: `src/probe/burn_contiguity.rs:80 burn_contiguity()` collapses decoded ids into a
  `BTreeSet` before the `first..=last` span check → presence-only, order-independent. A hop that
  REPEATS frames (identical rendered image delivered on consecutive frames) adds no missing id, so
  `full_chain.loss.<node>` reads clean (`real_drops==0`). Hid a real defect 3 days (issue 707: run
  396782734 carried the same strih burn id on 61% of consecutive stream frames).
- Fix: NEW pure crate-root module `src/burn_hold.rs` (default features, Tier-0) — one walk over the
  recorded-order `(frame_index, id)` pairs → run-length distribution (histogram + max_hold_frames +
  duplicate_pairs/fraction + distinct). Per-hop assertion `max_hold_frames <= MAX_HOLD_FRAMES=4`
  (topology v2: strih+stream record 30fps, node burns decimated 60->30 ⇒ legit hold=1; bound=4
  mirrors imag_tick_gate IMAG_OPTICAL_MAX_STUCK_RUN=3 pairs = 4 frames; matches the ticket's "never
  5"). REPORT-ONLY via the one-line `burn_hold::gates_overall_pass()->false` seam (mirrors
  presentation_cadence/optical_floor); flip-to-LIVE tracked on the ticket once green-run max_hold
  distributions accumulate + survive the issue-909 cam1 grabber defect. Probe glue in
  recording-verdict.rs emits `full_chain.loss.<node>.hold.*` (scoped flag) from the stream recording.
- Frame-index-aware (review): a run extends only when frames are recording-ADJACENT, so a recorded
  gap (undecodable burn in between) breaks a hold instead of merging two — `duplicate_pair_fraction`
  is exactly "% consecutive recorded frames byte-identical", never diluted by decode gaps.
- Commits: 922c0aef1 (bump) · e543cd897 [red] (blind stub fails the repeat fixtures) · 035e354fc
  [green] run-length walk · b18477409 [green] recording-verdict glue · fcff290e6 [green] clippy doc ·
  ddea28bd2 [green] frame-index run breaking + gap/tie-break tests, drop dead derive (review).
- Tier-0 verify: fmt/clippy --all-targets -D warnings/test --no-run --lib all clean (unit tests run
  in CI; build-ok bypass disabled for camera-box, issue 477). recording-verdict.rs is
  required-features=probe (CI-first-compile) — glue hand-type-checked + fmt-parsed.

## 2026-08-15 — #1026 imag OBS SIGSEGV in obs-websocket GetOutputList (get_const_root UAF)

- Root cause (coredump forensics on imag-nb, dumps 140969 + 278175, identical signature
  `get_const_root <- obs_enum <- GetOutputList <- RequestHandler::GetOutputList`, Qt WS worker):
  a use-after-free of a borrowed `output->video`. `output->video` is set once at obs_output_create
  (`= obs_get_video()`, raw outputs) and NEVER cleared on stop. When the main canvas mix video is
  freed in `obs_canvas_clear_mix` (startup video-settings reset), an output left over from before it
  — the inactive `virtualcam_output` (`active=0`, confirmed by walking obs->data.first_output in the
  core) — keeps pointing at the freed video_t; GetOutputList's obs_output_get_width ->
  video_output_get_width -> get_const_root then walks the freed+reused memory (video->parent read
  back as NDI string "MV Cam 5" in one dump, 0x1000000 in another) -> SIGSEGV. Intermittent because
  the freed block only sometimes holds a fault-triggering parent. NOT the earlier partial-bundle ABI
  skew (7 crashes on the matched full bundle). The issue-793 fix detached canvas->mix but never the
  output copies.
- Fix (obs-canvas.c, obs_canvas_clear_mix): before the mixes_mutex free, walk obs->data.first_output
  under obs->data.outputs_mutex (the exact list+lock obs_enum_outputs uses) and NULL any
  output->video == old_mix->video. Runs BEFORE mixes_mutex so the two never nest; the NULL-safe
  video-io getters (issue-793) then return 0. Extends issue-793's detach-before-free. Scoped to
  obs_canvas_clear_mix on purpose (create-path outputs only borrow the main VIEWED canvas mix, freed
  only here; moving it into obs_free_video_mix would nest outputs_mutex inside the mixes_mutex its
  other callers hold).
- Commits: 090059828 (bump .461) · 828e9272d [red] (tests/ws_enum_output_video_detach_1026.rs) ·
  0ad3359e9 [green] (obs-canvas.c) · 861dc7f21 (rustfmt) · 638550930 (review 0/0/2: scoping comment
  + fail-loud test terminator).
- Verify: lift-and-compile gcc -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion clean; brace balance vs HEAD +2/+2;
  source-anchor test RED->GREEN observed via standalone `rustc --test` binary (2 failed -> 2 passed);
  rustfmt clean. Vendored C compiles only on CI (Tier-0 ban) -> linux-genlock + CI is the first real
  type-check. Review clean 0 red / 0 yellow / 2 blue (both fixed).
- GOTCHA: gh api .../comments does NOT trigger post-record-design-comment.sh (it prefilters on
  `gh issue comment`), so a design/validated/review comment posted via `gh api` writes no marker and
  block-commit-without-design.sh stays blocked — post the design comment via `gh issue comment` (not
  `gh api`). Also the design-gate classifier needs literal phrasing: `Chosen approach:` /
  `Rejected alternative:` / numbered `Approach 1/2/3` / `trade-off`, not `(CHOSEN)`/`REJECTED`/plural
  "Approaches" (the `\bapproach\b` marker won't match "Approaches"). And `--host build-ok` bypass is
  disabled for camera-box, but a pure std source-anchor test compiles+runs standalone via

## #877 — aux-sender teardown wedge: re-characterised + teardown-ordering regression gate (2026-08-15)

- Ticket (predates the issue 879/1063 aux render-budget work) hypothesised a destroy-race: disabling
  all three aux NDI senders at once wedged strih PROGRAM to 0 fps, blamed on `send_destroy` racing an
  in-flight send. STEP-0 validation from CURRENT code REFUTES the trigger→destroy mapping and finds
  the mandated ordering already correct — so re-characterised (not obsolete), stays OPEN on a
  forward-looking coverage decision.
- Findings (code-grounded): (a) obs-source.c `render_video()` skips a DISABLED filter before
  `ndi_filter_render_video` (`ndi_filter` is OBS_SOURCE_TYPE_FILTER/OBS_SOURCE_VIDEO), so a mere
  disable calls NO destroy path — sender stays alive+idle; the "three senders destroyed at once"
  premise doesn't hold on disable. (b) The teardown ordering the ticket demands is upstream-original
  and correct: `ndi_filter_destroy` does `video_output_close()` (stop+join the raw_video send worker)
  BEFORE `ndi_sender_destroy`, which locks both sender mutexes before `send_destroy`. (c) No
  cross-sender lock; destroy/recreate not used as flow-control. (d) issue 879/1063 touched only the
  render-budget path, not teardown. (e) The observed 0-fps symptom's true root cause is NDI-SDK
  internal (program uses async `send_send_video_async_v2`; shared per-process transmit/connection
  threads churn when 3 senders go silent at once) — not in readable code, not reproducible without a
  rig write (forbidden to the worker).
- Ship: `tests/aux_sender_teardown_ordering_877.rs` — Tier-0 static gate locking the two ordering
  invariants (join-before-destroy; mutex-before-send_destroy), with a baked-in mutation proof
  (reordered + missing-lock fixtures must be rejected). Same static-anchor idiom as
  genlock_release_cadence / aux_sender_budget_879; sig anchors match the DEFINITION line `...)\n{`
  to dodge the forward-decl trap. No vendored code changed.
- Commits: bump to 1.7.0-dev.461 · test(#877) [green] teardown-ordering gate.
- Verify: checker logic replica-verified in python3 vs the real ndi-filter.cpp (both orderings PASS;
  both mutation fixtures REJECTED); `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. Local `cargo test --no-run` still
  compiling after ~58 min under extreme fleet load (~35 on 4 cores) — compile confirmation deferred to

## issue 1072 — E2E cleanup left cam2-painter dead: restore-retry + periodic dead-man + preflight self-heal (worktree autopilot-1072, v1.7.0-dev.462)
- Root cause (3 seams): (a) cleanup()'s cam2 restore was one-shot `systemctl start cam2-painter 2>/dev/null || true` (failure swallowed) + an UNCONDITIONAL dead-man disarm — a failed start left the painter dead AND tore down the on-box self-heal net; (b) the #872 dead-man was a ONE-SHOT `--on-active=90min` timer, so a SIGKILLed run's painter stayed dark up to 90 min; (c) the [0/8] optical-chain preflight did a passive grace re-probe then `exit 1`, no recovery attempt. Killed ≥3 gate runs 2026-08-15 at [0/8] "optical injection leg DEAD" (31869844646, 31880968359, 31887117614); supervisor started the service by hand before every rerun.
- Fix (a) new sourced-lib scripts/lib/cam2-painter-restore-retry.sh (`cam2_painter_restore_retry_cmds`, #675 pattern — ONE `$(...)` line, no anchored line edited): bounded retry (reset-failed+start, poll is-active, CAM2_PAINTER_RESTORE_RETRIES=3) that is fail-loud and sets remote var `_cprr_ok`; cleanup wraps the existing `$(cam2_painter_deadman_disarm_cmds)` in `if [ -n "$_cprr_ok" ]` so a failed restore LEAVES the dead-man armed. Kept the exact `systemctl start cam2-painter 2>/dev/null || true` + adjacent `$(cam2_painter_restore_verify_cmds)` (5+ tests pin them: #863/#872/#312/#713/coordination) as the retry's first attempt.
- Fix (b) cam2-painter-deadman.sh: window 90→5 min + `--on-active` PLUS `--on-unit-active` (periodic re-fire). Mid-run safety is now the existing `pgrep -x frame-probe` guard (every fire during a live run is a no-op — frame-probe is armed+launched within ~25s in one ssh command and runs the whole run), NOT a long delay. Unifies worst-case recovery to ~5 min for clean-cleanup and SIGKILL paths alike.
- Fix (c) optical-chain-preflight.sh: after the grace re-probe still-dead, EXACTLY ONE `systemctl start $service` over ssh + re-probe; existing `exit 1` stays as the fail-closed backstop.
- Tests: tests/harness_cam2_painter_restore_retry_1072.rs (retry sourced/wired, conditional disarm guarded by _cprr_ok, periodic + <=5min window + pgrep guard retained, preflight self-heal text anchor + a functional fake-systemctl/ssh test proving self-heal is tried EXACTLY once → proceed on recover / exit 1 fail-closed). Repurposed the old `deadman_delay_comfortably_exceeds_the_longest_run_872` (>=60 one-shot rule) into `deadman_window_is_short_and_made_safe_by_the_periodic_guard_1072` — the design premise flipped from one-shot-long-delay to periodic-short+guard.
- Local verify (camera-box Tier-0 forbids RUNNING cargo tests — build-ok disabled #477): cargo test --no-run exit 0 (tests compile); cargo fmt --all --check clean; bash -n clean on all 4 scripts; functional SHELL repros (standalone bash, not cargo) confirmed retry sets _cprr_ok+fail-loud, conditional disarm runs on success / skips on failure, preflight self-heal success→exit0/1-start + fail→exit1/1-start, composed remote bash syntax OK + `_cprr_ok` is a literal remote var. RED→GREEN of the Rust assertions runs on CI / supervisor integration.
- Anchors verified preserved by grep (no full-suite run possible locally): #863 start+verify adjacency, #872 disarm-after-start, #312 pkill/rm block, #713 device-restore needles all intact.

## issue 828 — no-capture-device backoff + preflight "no capture card present" wording (worktree autopilot-828, v1.7.0-dev.462)
- RESCOPED ticket (validator 2026-08-15): original cam4 restart-storm headline is gone (grabber now fitted), but two software items stand "regardless of hardware" (owner-confirmed). Both membership-agnostic — never hardcode a cam.
- Root cause: src/config.rs::find_capture_device() bail!s "No video capture device found" → main() exits 1 immediately → systemd Restart=always + RestartSec=3 with NO StartLimit = ~3s restart loop forever (cam4 incident NRestarts=27719). And preflight_fleet_check_verdict() (scripts/lib/preflight-fleet-check.sh) reported a generic "service is <state>, not active" for any non-active state, with no signal for the physical no-card cause.
- Mechanism decision (design comment): binary-level in-process slow retry, NOT pure systemd. RestartSec is GLOBAL so a longer value would slow a genuine mid-stream transient recovery; StartLimit→failed kills USB-hotplug auto-recovery. The binary now loops (probe → clear one-line log → 30s backoff sleep) so the no-device path never exits (0 restarts) and auto-recovers on (re-)plug; RestartSec=3 stays fast; a GENEROUS StartLimitIntervalSec=300/StartLimitBurst=20 in [Unit] is a belt-and-braces cap on ANY OTHER runaway.
- Item 1 files: src/no_device.rs (new crate-root pure seam wait_for_capture_device<D,S>(detect, sleep) — Tier-0 testable), src/config.rs (find_capture_device_opt() Option seam; find_capture_device() reuses it, behaviour + error text unchanged), src/main.rs (auto-detect branch waits via the loop; explicit --device / explicit configured device paths unchanged), systemd/camera-box.service (StartLimit* in [Unit]).
- Item 2: preflight gather emits VIDEO_NODES=<comma-list of /dev/video*> (kept LAST so an empty value is an unambiguous trailing field); verdict says "no capture card present — fit/check the grabber (#828)" when VIDEO_NODES is present-but-empty (checked FIRST, wins over the generic message), stays honest generic when nodes exist but service is down for another reason, and is back-compat (skips) when the field is entirely absent (presence via grep -q, not the value alone). This is the issue's own repro signal (ls /dev/video*), binary-independent.
- TDD: test(#828) [red] (tests/no_device_828.rs loop; tests/systemd_startlimit_828.rs [Unit] anchor; tests/harness_preflight_no_capture_card_828.rs verdict+gather) → fix(#828) [green]. RED proven for shell+systemd directly via bash (verdict empty on a no-card line; gather emits no VIDEO_NODES; unit has no StartLimit); binary RED by the non-looping placeholder.
- Verify (camera-box Tier-0 forbids running cargo tests locally, build-ok DISABLED #477): cargo fmt --all --check clean; cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; cargo test --no-run (3 new binaries) exit 0 (linked); shell verdict + gather verified functionally via bash with a fake ls (both node-present and no-node cases + verdict over the gathered line). RED→GREEN of the Rust loop proven on CI at integration.

## issue 732 — dev1-side :8899 BundleStateServer active health-check watchdog + auto-restart (worktree autopilot-732, v1.7.0-dev.463)
- STILL VALID (worker validate 2026-08-16): 4 documented recurrences through 2026-08-13; both :8899 endpoints happened to be UP at validation (strih 200/6.6s, stream 200/1.4s) — the chronic issue is the MISSING active watchdog, not a current outage. The recent bundle-state-server.py log() dead-stdout hardening (c162e56c9) is a different fix (server's own logging), not an external prober. The #1001 network-reach watchdog probes :8899 but only as one of three OR-signals for full-box reachability, so a :8899-only death (box up) classifies REACHABLE and never pages — genuine uncovered gap.
- Root cause: Task Scheduler restart-on-failure only re-launches after a SCHED_E_*/0xC0* FAILURE exit; the recurring death SCHED_S_TASK_TERMINATED (0x40010004) is an informational/SUCCESS class, so RestartCount=999 never engages; it also failed to restart a 0xC000013A crash (silent 3 days) and cannot cover a cold-start-never-happened. A passive Task-Scheduler policy cannot cover a non-failure termination — needs an ACTIVE external prober.
- Design decision (comment on the ticket, before first code): alert + AUTO-RESTART (not alert-only). ## 2026-08-17 — issue 768: report-only COLD-CUT onset verdict seam

- Blind spot closed: issue 767 (genlocked NDI receiver never rebinds after a sender restart → 41-min off-program black) passed every gate because nothing measured the TRANSITION ONSET (first ~1s after a program cut). The segmenter's 1s transition guard (`DEFAULT_TRANSITION_GUARD_NS`) discards exactly the onset; per-segment `copies`/`gaps` dilute a single wake-up gap over the whole ~30s window; `residual_events` start after the guard (0 onset events across 364 historical ≥60s cold cuts — the guard hiding them, not proof of cleanliness).
- Approach: new PURE crate-root module `src/cold_cut.rs` (default features, Tier-0) mines the EXISTING all-cambox sweep. For each cambox 2nd+ appearance whose hidden gap (this window `start_ns` − same cambox's prior window `end_ns`) ≥ `COLD_HIDDEN_SECS` (60s), a thin probe consumer in `recording-verdict.rs` reads the raw `seg_frames` in the first `ONSET_WINDOW_NS` (1s) after the switch (bypassing the guard) → wake-up latency + onset (un)decodable counts. Emitted at `all_cambox_continuity.cold_cut_onset`. No `recording-e2e.sh` change (zero anchor risk); the sweep already produces the cold cuts (3-box CAM1/CAM2/CAM3 @30s → ~60s hidden; median 60.4s across 76 verdicts, 364 ≥60s transitions). A first appearance (unknown prior hidden duration) is never a cold candidate.
- Report-only / calibration-first: `gates_overall_pass()` hardcoded `false` (one-line-restorable, mirrors `optical_floor`/`presentation_cadence`). The onset was never serialized before, so no bound is calibratable locally; the seam starts producing the warm baseline. Follow-up flips it LIVE once (a) the baseline exists and (b) a deliberate keepalive-bypass makes a cut genuinely cold.
- Decodability signal (review finding, empirically resolved): onset `decodable` = `SegmentFrame::tick.is_some()` (cam2 optical Vernier). `recording_segments.rs` doc claims non-cam2 windows carry no tick (would make it cam2-only), but that doc is STALE for this rig — ONE camera → HDMI splitter → all camboxes all film the same cam2-painted Vernier, so every box decodes it. Verified across 76 verdicts: CAM1/CAM3 windows have undecodable=0-1 of ~847, non-null first_tick/last_tick, populated presentation_cadence (needs ≥2 decoded ticks). Metric IS cross-cambox actionable here; documented + noted the LIVE-flip precondition (re-confirm per-cambox onset tick-decodability) in the module doc.
- Commits: `338bd24a6` bump 1.7.0-dev.465 · `5ef10e147` RED (stub `build_report` + inline tests) · `49525575b` GREEN (real derivation + probe consumer) · `5cebe316b` review-fix (doc: decodability-signal is the shared cam2 tick + LIVE-flip precondition; reworded a test comment). Review: 0 🔴 1 🟡 0 🔵 (🟡 addressed in 5cebe316b). Local: fmt + clippy -D warnings clean, `cargo test --no-run` compiles; recording-verdict.rs probe-gated (CI-first-compile), hand-type-checked + fmt-parsed.
- Follow-up filed as #1086: deliberate keepalive-bypass cold cut (issue 768 test-design bod 1) + OBS-log receiver-restart evidence (bod 4) + sustained-receive-fps + the segfault-confound discrimination (event RESCOPE) + LIVE gating — needs a live E2E run to calibrate + rig writes (this worker was rig-read-only).

## 2026-08-17 — issue 794: dev1-side non-60 source-cadence alert watchdog

- Gap: a camera set to 50 fps into the 60 fps chain went undetected for weeks (live 2026-07-17; no frame loss, 5:6 pulldown judder). Every fps counter reads the CANVAS rate, and the audit line's `@ X.XXXfps` decoration is `genlock_video_fps` = the GLOBAL CANVAS fps (60 on stream / 30 on strih, shared by every source) — useless per-source. The ONE per-source delivered-rate signal is strih's genlock-fifo `received=` cumulative counter; a genuinely-non-60-delivering camera advances it at that rate.
- Approach (dispatch-scoped): a 4th dev1-side alert-watchdog sibling (network-reach #1001 → frozen-input #1052 → bundle-state #732 → this). Per pass, sample the newest `genlock-fifo audit '<src>'` line's `received=` AND its OWN log timestamp; persist both; rate = Δreceived ÷ Δ(the two lines' OWN timestamps). LOAD-BEARING: never a wall-clock divisor — the issue-797 phantom-50.1 (a 6 s wall window spans ~one 5.017 s tick, +301 frames = 301/6 = 50.17 at every true-60 source, the retracted "OBS caps at 50" thesis). The single-tick guard test reads 59.996, not 50.17.
- Classify vs 60 ± 3 fps (59.94 NTSC in-band; 50/43 cleanly separated); a frozen source (Δreceived 0) is UNKNOWN not "wrong 0 fps" (defers to #1052); reuse obs_watchdog confirm(2)/throttle(6 ≈ 30 min) + recovery ping + #1001 no-double-page (strih down → SKIP) + fail-loud require_tools + a ~2 h "tap broken" WARN. Watch STRIH (raw camera NDI), not stream (2ME PGM is 30 fps by design).
- Pure kernel `scripts/lib/cadence-health.sh` (Tier-0). Local verify (cargo does NOT run here, #477): 44/44 direct-bash assertions on the pure fns incl. the phantom-50 guard; watchdog end-to-end via a `CADENCE_PROBE_CMD` stub (seed → WRONG-confirm → alert 50.0 fps → throttle → recovery-60), the #1001 SKIP path, and require_tools-fails-loud-on-missing-sshpass; `bash -n` + shellcheck clean; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.
- Ships DISABLED (systemd units committed, supervisor enables + sets the live `CADENCE_SOURCES` — see the README). Rig READ-ONLY.
- Commits: `becaf3576` bump 1.7.0-dev.466 · `d27129bb8` RED (harness) · `20e81ae66` GREEN (pure lib) · `07f4af783` feat (watchdog + systemd units + README + rule + CLAUDE.md router).
- Follow-up filed as #1088: the duplication-masked 50→60 "hard layer" (a padded 60 delivery reads a clean 60 here, the ACTUAL live case) — per-frame content-hash dup-rate, a categorically different mechanism needing pixel access (cross-cutting; the genuine where-to-hash design fork).

## #788 — imag-obs-alert-watchdog: distinguish operator quit from crash (2026-08-17, worktree-788-obs-quit)
- STILL-VALID but NARROWED. The RELAUNCH half of #788 was already solved by the issue-882/791 model: `imag-obs.service` `Restart=on-failure` (a clean exit(0) is left alone, deliberate stops route through `systemctl --user stop`), and the old relaunch-everything `imag-obs-watchdog.py` stays installed-but-DISABLED (live: `is-enabled` → not-found on the box). Only the FALSE-ALARM half remained, on the dev1-side alert path.
- Root cause: `scripts/imag-obs-alert-watchdog.sh` (dev1 timer, ENABLED+ACTIVE) fired "OBS is DOWN" on ANY `OBS_PROCESS_ABSENT` with no crash-vs-quit discrimination → a deliberate operator quit (test latency) still paged the crew (the live 2026-07-16 incident).
- Discriminator SOURCE = systemd's own `Restart=on-failure` verdict on imag-obs.service: a clean quit / operator `systemctl --user stop` reads `LoadState=loaded ActiveState=inactive Result=success`; a crash-loop ends `failed`. Live-confirmed the systemd quirk (a not-found unit ALSO shows inactive/success) → the classifier REQUIRES `LoadState=loaded`.
- Two pure seams in `scripts/lib/imag-obs-reachability.sh`: `imag_obs_deliberate_down_probe_cmd` (remote-snippet builder; `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` for the user bus; always exit 0) + `imag_obs_down_is_deliberate` (pure token classifier; `while-read` over a herestring → `-e`/pipefail safe, no pipe SIGPIPE). Watchdog does a 2nd ssh only on `OBS_PROCESS_ABSENT`; deliberate → INFO + reset the alert throttle (confirm/alert_sig/alert_passes, symmetric with the healthy branch) + return WITHOUT alerting. Fail-safe: ssh failure / unreadable unit / failed / activating / `OBS_PORT_NOT_LISTENING` all fall through to the existing alarm. Plus a time-bounded operator override file `/tmp/imag-watchdog-pause` (default 60 min from mtime, so a forgotten pause can't mask a real crash forever).
- Reuses the existing issue-391 obs-watchdog-decision + issue-882 reachability machinery — no new mechanism, no new box-deployed file (dev1-only script, remote probe is inline text). Preflight ([0/8] recording-e2e.sh) is untouched (its two reachability functions unchanged).
- Local verify (Tier-0, cargo never RUN — issue 477): `tests/harness_imag_obs_quit_discriminator_788.rs` 17/17 (RED was 15 fail/2 pass); `harness_imag_obs_alert_watchdog_882` 10/10 (backward compat) + 5 sibling suites green; `cargo fmt --all --check` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `shellcheck -S warning` clean on both scripts (CI's binary gate).

## #1077 — dantesync-fleet-upgrade.sh: non-root escalation, curl-less staging, master-aware verify, real ro-mount detection (worktree 1077-cd, v1.7.0-dev.467)

- Three Linux-path defects surfaced by the v1.8.42/43 live roll (3/8 boxes hand-rolled). (c) sudo escalation + (d) master-verify sawtooth were done by the prior (killed) worker; this resume finished + committed the playbook rule AND implemented the issue-title's third named defect (real ro-mount detection), which the prior STEP-0 had scoped as "self-resolves via escalation".
- (c) escalation: the generated Linux script is uploaded as a FILE and run escalated — `bash "$path"` for a root@ node (cam boxes), `sudo -n` where passwordless (dev1 --local), else `printf '%s\n' '<pw>' | sudo -S -p '' bash "$path"` (imag-nb newlevel@; password only in the run command, never the on-disk file; mirrors `imag-presented-frame-check.sh`). `dantesync_needs_sudo USER` decides.
- (c) curl-less: `ensure_linux_binary_staged` downloads+sha256-verifies ONCE on dev1 (memo published only AFTER the sha passes), `stage_linux_binary_to` scp's it per node; the on-box resolver is staged → curl → wget → fail-loud, re-sha-verified before `systemctl stop`. cam3 (no curl, broken apt) upgrades from the pre-placed binary; metered LAN pays one download.

Blanket `--ntp-master ""` on the master rolled back a HEALTHY swap (rc=20 twice, live v1.8.43).
- (3) real ro-mount detection: BOTH generated blocks read the ACTUAL mount state — `findmnt -no OPTIONS / || awk '$2=="/"{print $4; exit}' /proc/mounts`, matched `case "$opts" in ro | ro,*)` — never a `touch` write probe (conflates ro with a permission error; doubly so now the script runs escalated). Adopted VERBATIM from `setup-device.sh`'s `ensure_root_writable()`/`root_mount_is_readonly()` (#599); the reviewer flagged the first cut's write-probe fallback as reintroducing the exact conflation.

## #1080 — DistroAV recv_create_v3 reset-path silent permanent receiver-thread death (worktree fleet, 2026-08-17)
- Root cause: `ndi_source_thread` reset block `break`s on a NULL `recv_create_v3`. A `break` exits `while (s->running)` WITHOUT clearing `s->running` (only `ndi_source_thread_stop()` does), so `ndi_source_update`'s `if (s->running)` reattach sees the dead thread as alive and never restarts it → permanent, reattach-proof black. The #767 stale watchdog now reaches this reset path unattended, so a transient create failure = unattended permanent death.
- Fix: never break. New pure `ndi_recv_create_retry_backoff_ns(unsigned)` helper (250 ms→3 s bounded exponential, shift-clamped for overflow, retry COUNT never capped); the NULL branch increments a fail counter, blanks the source, backs off (chunked 100 ms so OBS shutdown isn't blocked), re-arms `reset_ndi_receiver` under `config_mutex`, and `continue`s. Plus a defensive null-guard before `recv_get_no_connections` (a racing `ndi_source_update` could clear the re-armed flag).
- Gate: std-only `tests/distroav_recv_create_retry_1080.rs` (source anchors + lift-compile `-Werror -Wconversion -Wformat=2` truth table; truth-table mutation watched go RED; two new anchors proven to bite) + mirrored pwsh token anchors in BOTH windows-genlock*.yml. Followed the #767/#1026 pattern; captured the lifecycle gotcha in `.claude/rules/distroav-receiver-lifecycle.md` (auto-loads on ndi-source.cpp).
- Local verify (Tier-0, cargo never RUN — issue 477): `cargo check`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `test --no-run`, `fmt --all --check` all clean; the compiled 1080 test binary 3/3; ndi-source.cpp brace/paren balanced Δ0.
- Review: one fresh general-purpose subagent, 0🔴 1🟡 3🔵. 3🔵 fixed in `4ae44d3ed`; the 1🟡 (sibling `framesync_create` break, same class, UNREACHABLE — framesync forced OFF on the genlock rig) filed as issue 1097. Also recorded the issue-1096 finder-poison-wedge cure direction on issue 1096 (distinct from this break/silent-death class).
- Commits: `bf627faea` bump 1.7.0-dev.468 · `a3282692f` RED (`backoff_helper_present`/`create_failure_retries_instead_of_breaking`/`backoff_computes_the_spec_truth_table`) · `e0370f10c` GREEN · `58aa893e7` rustfmt test · `4ae44d3ed` review fixes.

## #1088 — duplication-masked 50→60 dup-rate detector (content-hash), report-only (worktree 1088-duprate, v1.7.0-dev.468)

- The #794 hard layer: the cadence watchdog reads strih `genlock-fifo received=` and is STRUCTURALLY blind to a grabber that pads a 50fps source to 60 by DUPLICATION (delivers a genuine padded 60/s → `received=` reads clean 60). Surviving signal = per-frame CONTENT identity.
- STEP-0: no content-hash dup detector existed. Existing `copies`/`presentation_cadence.duplicate_fraction` are TICK-based (decode-dependent); `dupe_decimation.rs` (#889) handles the OPPOSITE (over-rate ~64fps, isolated ~6.7% dupes, cam-box gate SHEDS them). The slow-source 50→60 pulldown flows through un-detected. Cadence-watchdog rule already named this an OPEN follow-up.
- Design fork resolved with a THIRD option the ticket didn't enumerate: neither cam-box-side (rig write) nor receiver-side (live-box perturbation) — the OFFLINE recording-verdict worker path already streams every gray8 frame via ffmpeg, so hash there (on the worker, once per verdict).
- Pure crate-root `src/dup_cadence.rs` (Tier-0): `measure_dup_cadence(&[u64])` counts exact consecutive content-dups, classifies `duplication_masked` on THREE orthogonal checks — rate floor `DUP_RATE_PULLDOWN_MIN`=0.10 (above #674 ~4.3% beat + #889 ~6.7% over-rate, below 5:6 ~16.7%), inter-dup CV `DUP_GAP_CV_MAX`=0.35 (rejects an irregular burst), coverage `DUP_COVERAGE_MIN`=0.5 (rejects a localized freeze that has high local rate + uniform local spacing). Reports `inferred_source_fps=60*(1-dup_fraction)`. `frame_content_hash` = row-sampled FNV-1a gray8 (mirrors #889's approach). Gate seam `dup_cadence_gate_pass` + `gates_overall_pass()==false` (REPORT-ONLY, calibration-first — same discipline as #1036/#915).
- Probe surface: `probe::recording::hash_recording_frames` (a SEPARATE luma-only offline ffmpeg pass, index==frame_index — additive to avoid churning the ~15 `analyze_recording_*` callers, all CI-first-compile); `recording-verdict` per-cambox-window consumer via `partition_frames_by_window`, emitted REPORT-ONLY as `all_cambox_continuity.duplication_masked_cadence` (mirrors the `cadence_judder_gate`/`cold_cut` seams). Skipped in merge mode (needs the recording file). Hashes the STREAM recording per-window — the same tap the existing per-window `copies`/`presentation_cadence` metrics use.
- TDD: RED (stub `measure_dup_cadence` → None) → GREEN (impl). One RED-commit test's MECHANISM assertion corrected in GREEN (a clustered burst has UNIFORM inter-dup gaps → the correct veto is coverage, not gap-cv; split into a freeze case + an uneven-gap case). No test weakened.
- Verify (Tier-0, cargo does NOT run here #477): `src/dup_cadence.rs` 23/23 (20 at GREEN + 3 added by the review fix) via `cargo test --no-run --lib` + direct binary run; fmt-check clean whole-tree (parses the CI-only probe files → brace-balanced); clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean; hand type-audit of the probe wiring (`partition_frames_by_window` sig, `cam2_pin` Option<u32>, `SwitchWindow.cambox` String, `stream_rec` borrow scope). No local compile path for the probe code — CI is first compile.
- Report-only by design: the `all_pass &=` fold is a no-op (`gates_overall_pass()==false`); the first real runs calibrate the thresholds + the tap before any thought of promoting to a LIVE gate (one-line `gates_overall_pass()` flip).
- Fresh-context review: 0🔴 0🟡 3🔵. Fixed in-branch: (1) the gate bounded the RAW worst dup-fraction → added pure `worst_masked_duplicate_fraction` (worst among `duplication_masked` windows only) so a freeze/glitch can't double-jeopardy frozen_leg on a future LIVE promotion; (3) renamed a misleading "calibrated_values" test. ## #1006 — strih CG-bridge black-on-air: DIFFERENTIAL republish-black detector + dev1 alert (worktree 1006-cgbridge, v1.7.0-dev.470)

- Investigation ticket. Root cause is INTERNAL to Resolume Arena (third-party): its "CG_Bridge light" composition republishes a BLACK Spout while its upstream NDI `cg` is live. Proven by a read-only Arena screenshot (win-strih MCP: Composition Monitor fully black, Group 7 moderatori live) + OBS-WS luma probe. Receiver side healthy (sibling `spout moderatori` on the same plugin renders fine; `spout CG` bound to the right registered sender). NOT our code — rewiring Spout→NDI was rejected under 941, so Spout must stay. camera-box can only DETECT.
- STEP-0 (live 2026-08-17): `CG bridge`/`spout CG`/`cg` all stably BLACK; `spout moderatori`/`Moderatori`/`Grading`/`Cam 1` live; program on Cam 1 (healthy). One changed detail vs the ticket: upstream `cg` was peak=180 (live) on 2026-08-06 but is peak=0 (idle) now, so the exact "upstream live + republish black" divergence was not reproducible live (operator/content-driven). Still VALID as a class.
- KEY design finding: the ticket's literal scope ("every production scene renders non-black") is provably WRONG — `Ableset` (lyrics) AND `CG bridge` are BOTH legitimately black at idle on a healthy rig, so a blanket check false-fails constantly. Chosen instead: a DIFFERENTIAL detector — page ONLY when a reference upstream NDI is LIVE but its Spout republish is BLACK (the 2026-08-06 signature); both-black = legitimately idle = no alarm.

## #802 — LIVE crash: Aitum SRT-CALLER tap start against unreachable target killed OBS → listener-mode redesign + guard + bench (worktree 802-srt, v1.7.0-dev.470)
- Root cause traced in code: the tap is an `ffmpeg_mpegts_muxer` output (Aitum Multistream plugin, NOT vendored) started as an SRT CALLER to `srt://…:9998`; when no listener is bound, `connect_mpegts_url`→`libsrt_open`<0 → `ffmpeg_mpegts_finalize` "Failed to open the url" → `set_config` fail: → OBS died. VLC 3.x SRT is caller-only so the intended local listener never bound. No repro/backtrace/bench-OBS-with-Aitum/Windows in a Tier-0 worktree.
- Approach chosen: the ticket's plan #2 — redesign the OBS-side tap as an SRT LISTENER (`srt://0.0.0.0:9998?mode=listener`; a listener bind never fails on a missing peer → the failing-start crash trigger structurally cannot occur; the player connects on demand as caller). Delivered as camera-box's own Tier-0-testable tooling since camera-box can't create the Aitum output over WS. Rejected: patching the vendored obs-ffmpeg cleanup path (unprovable as THE crash without a backtrace, high blast-radius on the real streaming output type, needs the full vendored gauntlet) → filed as bench-gated follow-up issue 1104.
- Deliverables: `scripts/srt_tap.py` (pure-stdlib guard module: `assert_safe_to_start` refuses caller/rendezvous + hands back the listener URL; `recommend_tap_url`; `srt_mode`/`is_listener_url`/`parse_srt_target`; `probe_listener_bindable`/`probe_udp_port_refused`; `reader_should_grab`; CLI). `scripts/av-sync-tap-bench.sh` bench harness (guard checks + a REAL ffmpeg SRT-listener-start-with-no-player probe + pytest). `av_sync_measure.py` opt-in `--tap-preflight` reader-side NO-SIGNAL (fails OPEN; no-op without the flag).
- TDD: RED `1df00b105` (guard stubbed to the unguarded baseline → 5 guard tests fail, reproducing the un-refused caller start) → GREEN `412800fef` (real guard). Bench + wiring `c47990b6f`.
- Verify (Tier-0, pytest not blocked): `tests/python/test_srt_tap.py` 28 + `test_av_sync_measure_tap_preflight.py` 6 green; full `tests/python` 965 passed (no regression from the measure edit); `scripts/av-sync-tap-bench.sh` 0 failures incl. the live ffmpeg-libsrt listener probe (listener output alive 2s with no player); shellcheck clean. No Rust changed (only Cargo.toml version bump).
- Related: monitor design in issue 801, desync investigation issue 800, crash catalogue issue 793. Worktree mode: supervisor integrates; no PR/deploy by this worker. Ticket stays OPEN (supervisor closes on merge).

- Scope: the REMAINING item 2 of #784 — a `drift-guard --check-imag` facet that FAILs loudly if `/proc/cmdline` carries kernel CPU-isolation the current design does not prescribe. The live večerný-kolaps fix (grub cleaned; setup-imag.sh made affinity-only by #842) was already done, and verify-imag.sh (d)+(s) guard it at PROVISIONING time — this is the CONTINUOUS / drift-guard counterpart. ## 2026-08-18 — #1104 obs-ffmpeg-mpegts.c leaks ff_data on the failed-SRT-start cleanup path (worktree 1104-mpegts, v1.7.0-dev.473)
- Scope: an 802 follow-up. `ffmpeg_mpegts_finalize()` (vendored `vendor/obs-studio/plugins/obs-ffmpeg/obs-ffmpeg-mpegts.c`) freed `ff_data` only on the `data_init`-fail exit; the three post-init failure branches (`init_streams`, `open_output_file != SUCCESS` = the SRT-unreachable crash path, `pthread_create != 0`) `return false` WITHOUT freeing. Worktree lane, authority=full, STOPS at local-green (supervisor integrates).
- STEP-0 validate: read the current dev finalize body (vendored file last touched only by the upstream subtree merge `5fde60999` — stock, unpatched). All three branches confirmed leaking; the caller's `set_config` `fail:` → `stop()` skips `full_stop()`/`data_free` because `active()` is false on a failed start (`write_thread_active` never set). The pthread branch is the worst: `open_output_file` already succeeded so for SRT/RIST an *established* avio (`has_connected`) is leaked, not just the format context.
- Design (non-trivial, 3 approaches): (1) inline `ffmpeg_mpegts_data_free` before each of the 3 early returns, mirroring the existing `data_init`-fail branch — CHOSEN; (2) a single `goto cleanup` label — rejected (larger diff, diverges MORE from upstream + the early-return idiom); (3) make the caller free unconditionally — rejected (shared with the normal user-stop/reconnect paths → double-free risk). `ffmpeg_mpegts_data_free` is partial-init-safe (guards each field, gates the SRT close on `has_connected`, `av_write_trailer` on `initialized`, `memset`s at end) so it is the correct idempotent cleanup at every early exit.
- TDD: Tier-0 static anchor gate `tests/mpegts_finalize_frees_ff_data_1104.rs` (vendored C compiles on CI only). Slices the `ffmpeg_mpegts_finalize` body (sig → first column-0 `}`) and asserts each failure branch's window (anchor → its first `return false;`) contains a `ffmpeg_mpegts_data_free` call, plus a baked-in mutation proof (checker MUST reject a synthetic no-free branch + accept a with-free one). RED `73adc7121` (3 branch tests fail, mutation proof passes) → GREEN `1aad98acb` (4 pass). Observed for real via the `rustc --test` standalone recipe (`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=<wt> rustc --test --edition 2021 tests/…rs`).
- Verify (Tier-0): RED→GREEN observed via rustc --test; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; diff-vs-HEAD = exactly the 3 inserts; brace balance `{`/`}` delta 0, `(`/`)` +3/+3 (balanced call parens). No local C compile path (vendored) — CI is first compile.
- Review (fresh-context general-purpose, NOT the built-in Skill): in-diff clean 0/0/0. Confirmed no double-free / no UAF on the live SRT/RTMP output path (the `has_connected` gate holds; the pthread branch's `log_error` correctly precedes `data_free`, else a fresh `last_error` would leak into the zeroed struct). Two PRE-EXISTING, out-of-scope, non-`ff_data` findings DROPPED with reasoning on the ticket (neither clears the follow-up gate): (a) a `dict` AVDictionary not freed on `open_output_file`'s `OBS_OUTPUT_BAD_PATH` return — unreachable in camera-box (`protocol_settings` is always `""` → empty dict); (b) a dangling `stream->h` after `connect_mpegts_url`'s fail path — confirmed NOT a leak and NOT a live UAF, defensive-only.
- Deploy note: obs-ffmpeg is a vendored OBS plugin → ships in the FULL OBS bundle on strih/stream, not a fast-dll. Defense-in-depth only (the listener-mode redesign from issue 802 already removes the crash trigger), so no urgent rig deploy; a WER/gdb bench repro of the original crash remains the separate item the ticket describes.
- Commits: `1b19d1163` bump dev.473 → `73adc7121` [red] → `1aad98acb` [green] → `[review]` this docs entry. Worktree branch worktree-1104-mpegts; supervisor integrates.

## 2026-08-18 — #1107 imag HDMI tearing: vsync the EGL program projector (worktree 1107-tearing, v1.7.0-dev.474)
- Scope: fix horizontal-motion TEAR on imag-nb's HDMI-1 program (LED-wall IMAG) scanout. Worktree lane, authority=full, STOPS at local-green (supervisor integrates + deploys FULL-BUNDLE + runs the live tear/60fps acceptance). Ticket STAYS OPEN after merge (live deploy + physical HDMI tap verification pending).
- STEP-0 validate (code + LIVE imag): `gl_x11_egl_device_present()` still hardcodes `eglSwapInterval(edisplay, 0)` (gl-x11-egl.c ~568) + the gl-wayland twin; LIVE imag OBS confirmed `Using EGL/X11` + Intel Mesa 25.2.8, NO compositor (picom absent), two 60Hz fullscreen projectors (HDMI-1 Program + eDP-1 Multiview) on one graphics thread. Tear is a SCANOUT artifact (unreadable via WS screenshot) but every causal precondition is confirmed live + in code. Pre-deploy trap CLEARED: no `vblank_mode`/MESA/driconf clamp in imag's OBS launch env (plain `obs --disable-shutdown-check`), so Mesa honors interval 1.
- Root cause: EGL present disables vsync; on Intel/modesetting with no compositor + no TearFree (issue 841; issue 777 masked it on the old NVIDIA box via FFCP) nothing aligns the swap to vblank → tear.
- Design (non-trivial, Fable design consult via the open budget gate, digest-in→decision-out): rejected (2) a DRM atomic page-flip rewrite (correct long-term but out of scope for a hotfix) and (3) unconditional interval-1 on ALL presents (stacks 2 different-monitor blocking swaps — main window eDP-1 + program HDMI-1 — and would drop genlock 60fps). CHOSEN: per-display OPT-IN vsync armed for ONLY the fullscreen non-multiview program projector. KEY live finding: `render_divisor <= 1` is NOT a valid discriminator — the OBS main window is also a divisor-0 display on eDP-1 — so the frontend `savedMonitor > -1 && !isMultiview` marks the program specifically, mirroring the 276 isMultiview→render_divisor pattern.
- Plumbing (12 touches, all layered; libobs-d3d11 UNTOUCHED): `bool present_vsync` on GL `gs_device` (default false via bzalloc = old behavior) ← NEW export `device_present_set_vsync` (gl-subsystem.c) ← the x11+wayland EGL present read it via a `present_vsync ? 1 : 0` ternary. `gs_present_vsync()` (graphics.c/.h) delegates via a NEW `GRAPHICS_IMPORT_OPTIONAL(device_present_set_vsync)` vtable member — D3D11/metal don't implement it → NULL → no-op → Windows strih/stream byte-identical. `bool vsync` on `obs_display` + `obs_display_set_vsync()`; `render_display()` arms `gs_present_vsync(display->vsync)` each tick immediately before `gs_present()`. Frontend marks the fullscreen program projector at DisplayCreated AND re-arms on OpenFullScreen/OpenWindowed runtime toggles (review 🟡).
- Genlock risk (on ticket, supervisor rig-acceptance): one HDMI-1 blocking present couples the genlock thread to the panel clock; sign-dependent vs DanteSync 60.00 (== / faster → no perturbation; slower → ~1 dup encode frame per beat). Acceptance = 30+min motion run, render must stay 60.00fps / 0 renderSkip / 0 lagged_frames growth; fallback = +50–100 ppm-fast HDMI-1 modeline.
- TDD: `tests/gl_egl_present_vsync_1107.rs` (issue 756 gl-x11-egl text-anchor precedent, Tier-0, pure std) 11→12 assertions, RED→GREEN observed directly via the issue-1026 standalone-rustc recipe (heavy compilation banned locally, #477). Verify: lift-and-compile of the added C (gcc -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Wformat=2, flag threads end-to-end); brace/paren balance = 0 across all 12 files; cheap default-feature compile-check GREEN; fmt clean; clippy-driver on the test clean. NO edit to recording-e2e.sh/rig-mode.sh → no static-anchor-collision risk; anchor sweep confirmed no collisions with genlock_preload / 756 / setup_imag_guards / windows-genlock*.yml.
- Review (fresh-context Fable adversarial dispatch, gate OPEN; NOT the built-in Skill): 0 🔴, 1 🟡 (runtime toggle re-arm gap — FIXED in-branch `e628c870a` + anchored), 1 🔵 (single-projector invariant — DOCUMENTED). Final 0/0/0.
