## 2026-08-18 — #825 CI-BREAK FIX: two real OBS-32.2 breaks the rebase surfaced (worktree 825-ci-fix, v1.7.0-dev.476)
- Context: the first CI build of the integrated 32.2 stack failed on BOTH platforms (Windows run 32138592528, Linux run 32138592522). Both are genuine 32.2 API/build-system changes, not resolution errors. NEW worktree lane off current dev (4a2506c3e), authority=full, STOPS at local-green; supervisor re-runs CI. #825 stays OPEN.
- Break 1 (Windows, "Configure OBS (windows-x64 preset)"): OBS 32.2's `vendor/obs-studio/CMakePresets.json` pins the windows-x64 + windows-arm64 presets to `"generator": "Visual Studio 18 2026"` — no GitHub runner has VS 2026 (VS 17 2022 only), and CMake REFUSES a `-G` override when a preset names a generator, so `cmake --preset windows-x64` (both windows-genlock*.yml) errors `Could not create named generator Visual Studio 18 2026`. Fix: pin both vendored windows presets to `"Visual Studio 17 2022"`. Guard: `tests/vendored_windows_preset_generator_825.rs`.
- Break 2 (Linux, "Compile-check DistroAV"): OBS 32.2 marked the 4-arg `obs_properties_add_button` `OBS_DEPRECATED` (+ added `obs_properties_add_button2(...,void *priv)`); DistroAV compiles with `-Werror=deprecated-declarations`, so `ndi-filter.cpp:159` (the ndi_apply button) fails. It is the ONLY deprecated-in-32.2 API DistroAV uses (cross-checked every `OBS_DEPRECATED` symbol in the vendored headers vs DistroAV usage). Fix: migrate to `obs_properties_add_button2`, naming `ndi_filter_getproperties(void *data)` and passing that filter instance as the explicit priv. BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING — `obs_property_button_clicked()` (obs-properties.c:820) hands `p->priv` to the callback exactly as the old path handed `context->data` (same `ndi_filter_t*`). Guard: `tests/distroav_add_button2_825.rs`.
- Verify: RED→GREEN — both new guards RED-proven against un-patched HEAD (0/2 each), GREEN on the fix (2/2 each); final anchor sweep 12/12 (the 2 new guards + linux_genlock_workflow_gate + windows_manifest_gate + distroav_source_config_lock/genlock_lockdown/timecode/teardown + genlock_release_cadence + gl_pbo_orphan + obs_updater_disabled + frontend_obs_data_json_null_guard_1106). `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. Genlock libobs C compiled clean on the Linux run (only the DistroAV step failed) — no genlock-C 32.2 break. Windows OBS compile is not yet proven (it failed at configure before compiling) — CI re-run is the proof.

## issue 1094 — imag-leg extract precondition: topology-adaptive decode CPU pin (worktree round)

- SCOPE: precondition only (root-cause WHY recording-e2e.sh [8/8c] never verifies the imag leg; 0/76 historically). NOT the report-only->blocking flip and NOT the issue-887 fold — those stay gated on a green imag-verdict distribution (`.claude/rules/imag-leg-report-only.md`).

## 2026-08-18 — #1112 wire the dup-cadence content-hash surface to EMIT in the production merge gate (worktree 1112-dupwire, v1.7.0-dev.478)
- Context: the issue-1101 calibration lane proved the issue-1088 `all_cambox_continuity.duplication_masked_cadence` surface is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE in the production gate — it fired only inside `match stream_rec { Some(rec) => hash_recording_frames(rec) … }` (the fused `--stream` path), but `VERDICT_ON_STREAM=1` runs extract-partial-on-box + merge-on-dev1 with no recording on dev1 → `stream_rec=None` → skip arm → 0 of 81 verdicts carried it. STEP-0 re-mined live: still 0/81.
- Design (chosen approach 3 of 3, see the issue design comment): compute the per-frame row-sampled content hash ON the stream box during `--extract-partial stream` (recording local), CARRY it in a new `RecordingPartial.content_hashes: Option<Vec<u64>>` (schema v3→v4, additive `#[serde(default)]`), and have the dev1 merge slice it per cambox window. Rejected approach 1 (attach to `RecordingFrame`, fold into the decode — the ticket's "do them together") + approach 2 (churn `analyze_recording_*` return type): both need 54-site / ~15-caller BLIND edits on CI-first-compile code whose last emit-wiring (worktree-1111-emitgate) was just reverted in round 32 — too risky for a report-only first cut. §9 sanctions the additive separate pass; the fold optimization stays issue-1101 Part 2.
- Plumbing that avoided churn: (a) `RecordingPartial` is built ONLY via `from_frames(...).with_*` builders → adding an optional field + `with_content_hashes` churns ZERO callers; (b) `build_and_print_verdict` was SPLIT — a thin back-compat wrapper keeps the original 8-arg signature (so all ~35 test + the fused-main call sites are byte-for-byte unchanged) and delegates to a new `build_and_print_verdict_with_stream_hashes(…, stream_content_hashes)`; only `run_merge` calls the 9-arg form. `RecordingFrame` / `DecodedRec` / `partition_frames_by_window` / the `dup_cadence` classifier all UNTOUCHED.
- Emit gate: computed on the stream box when `box_name=="stream" && args.switch_schedule.is_some()` — the ALL_CAMBOX gate already pushes `--switch-schedule` to the stream box (recording-e2e.sh ~4096), so default-on, no new forgettable flag; delivery-only extracts pay nothing; hash failure is NON-FATAL (report-only). `dup_cadence::gates_overall_pass()` stays `false` (report-only; issue-1101 owns the LIVE flip + bound calibration).
- Tier-0: extracted the per-window slice math to `dup_cadence::window_content_hashes(frame_indices, frame_hashes)` (crate root, default-feature) — RED→GREEN 5 tests (pick-by-frame_index-not-position, contiguous==slice, out-of-range-skip, empty, feeds-measure_dup_cadence-unchanged); RED proven by mutating the impl to index-by-position (4/5 fail). Plus a probe-gated `content_hashes` partial round-trip test.
- Verify (probe glue is CI-first-compile — no local type check): `cargo fmt --all --check` clean (parses probe files, proves brace/format balance); full hand type-audit of the wiring + all call-site arities; the 28 dup_cadence Tier-0 tests GREEN. First LIVE emission rides the next production E2E (honest UNVERIFIED — the merge-path emit cannot be exercised without a full hardware run).

## issue 1119 — E2E dantesync gate: master NTP median bound is a coin flip under the bounded-step slow-GM regime (worktree)
- Root cause: dantesync v1.8.46 reports ntp_deadband_us as the NO-STEP threshold (live: 1000us), NOT the <=2500us bounded PER-STEP cap the master's UTC offset sawtooths toward under a ~23ppm-slow GM. The issue-1021 widening max(2000, 1000+1000)=2000 gives NO widening, so a healthy sawtooth median (failed run 32178766136: 2699us) false-DRIFTs the bare 2000us bound. Reproduced live: strih :8898/status ntp_deadband_us=1000, LOCK, GM 10.77.9.184, storm=false, 85 steps/h; offset sawtooths 0->1691us. The issue-1055 slew rescue is linux-client-journal-only, never applies to the win-http master.
- Fix: ntp_master_effective_bound_us gains an optional STEP_CAP_US 4th arg (default "0" = byte-identical pre-1119); when a numeric ntp_deadband_us is present the median floor also includes step_cap+margin (2500+1000=3500). Gated on numeric deadband so a pre-84 master keeps the bare bound (preserves the issue-1021 no/null-deadband tests). New pure ntp_master_step_storm_verdict (reads dantesync's own ntp_step_storm boolean) + ntp_steps_last_hour accessor; grade_http_node median-only branch hard-fails an affirmative storm (rc_off!=3 only). New GATE_NTP_MASTER_STEP_CAP_US const (default 2500, DANTESYNC_NTP_MASTER_STEP_CAP_US), loud widened-bound note, --help doc. CLIENT rows untouched.
- TDD (Tier-0, no local build): 7 unit tests tests/clock_offset_guard.rs + 6 e2e tests tests/dantesync_gate.rs. RED proven via direct dantesync-gate.sh runs (sawtooth DRIFTs, storm PASSES pre-fix); GREEN proven directly (sawtooth PASS bound 3500us, storm/unlock/foreign-GM/15ms-offset FAIL, no-deadband 2850us still DRIFTs). ## 2026-08-19 — #1131 emit-gate robustness: never multi-slot skip while captured frames exist (worktree 1131-emitgate, v1.7.0-dev.484)
- Root cause (validated live via standalone rustc, no cargo #557): `genlock_pacing::genlock_emit_gate`'s #707 forward-resync is QUEUE-BLIND — it leaps the wall-clock boundary grid whenever a single poll's lag > `GENLOCK_MAX_CATCHUP_INTERVALS` (8), dropping the intervening boundaries. On a sick/wobbly grabber the V4L2 driver buffers REAL captured frames during a stall (live signature: `#707 SKIPPED ... 9 boundary interval(s)` with 0 capture-dropped = frames exist, delivered late); the resync leaps past them → decimated in a run → visible multi-frame content judder (1110/1130 P0). #1111 already fixed the dupe-deferral lag-ratchet; this is the residual queue-blind resync. Repro confirmed: 4 buffered frames → emits 1, skips 10.
- Design (non-trivial, 3 approaches): rejected raising the fixed bound (breaks 131 cold-boot resync — a genuine multi-second NTP step would creep through hundreds of stale-frame emits) and rejected reorder-on-resync (timecode-regression risk). CHOSE the queue-occupancy discriminator: reuse the existing `FrameInfo.dequeue_duration_ms` signal (the #707 capture-stall diagnostic) via a new pure `capture_stall::frame_from_nonempty_queue(dequeue_ms, capture_interval_ms)` (< 0.5x interval = the driver already had it buffered) → thread `queue_had_frame` through `DecimationGate::poll` → `genlock_emit_gate`; resync trigger becomes `lag > BOUND && !queue_had_frame`. Buffered frame → catch up ONE interval (fill its boundary, never leap); empty-queue frame (loop genuinely waited — device gap / clock step) → keeps the honest resync. 131 preserved for free: a cold-boot step inflates CLOCK_REALTIME `now_ns` but NOT the monotonic `Instant` dequeue duration, so the post-step frame reads as a normal wait → resync still fires.

## #1145 — Emit dupe-shed v2: over-rate takt absorbed without cadence damage (v1.7.0-dev.496)
- Root cause: at over-rate the unique rate is EXACTLY 60/s -> emit-gate lag is a driftless random walk; V4L2 timestamp jitter pushes a #889 on-time deferral over the lag==0 hair-trigger, next content-dupe arrives LATE, #1111 valve EMITS it as a delta-0 copy which (paired with the compensating dropped-unique) is the strih 15fps-judder the #1142 uniformity gate REDs (cam1 ~0.69, cam2 ~0.81; cam3 @60.00 dupe-free = clean).
- Key physics: shedding a frame BETWEEN boundaries (blind-shed) costs 0 lag; shedding a boundary-CROSSING frame (deferral) always adds ~1 interval lag. "defer iff lag<BOUND" never CANCELS the lag debt so a driftless walk eventually trips the #707 resync -> #1110 judder. Bounded-lag alone is insufficient (verified in the sim).
- Fix (advisor-shaped consult, gate OPEN, verified off-rig against the REAL DecimationGate::poll): stale-boundary RETIREMENT gated on the measured unique rate. genlock_pacing::genlock_lag_intervals (numeric staleness signal, shares genlock_latched_boundary; emit_gate resync UNTOUCHED). dupe_decimation::dupe_shed_action (replaces dupe_preferring_decimate) -> ShedAction {Emit{copy},Defer,Retire,BlindShed}. A dupe crossing an already-stale boundary (lag>=1) is RETIRED (shed + advance the stale boundary, emit nothing: 0 copy, 0 unique sacrificed, drains lag). RETIRE_MAX_LAG_INTERVALS=4 (<< resync 8). Retire only when a trailing 2s window holds >= RETIRE_MIN_UNIQUES_IN_WINDOW=118 uniques (~59fps) — VecDeque on DecimationGate — so a genuinely starved source (50->60 pulldown) stays on the #1111 copy path (holds 60, keeps content-dupes for the duplication-masked pulldown detector: no emit-deficit / no detector-blinding regression). DupeShedLog gains `retired`; take()/summary/main.rs 4-count.
- Divergence from advisor: added the unique-rate gate (advisor dismissed a takt gate); a capture-takt gate would wrongly retire a takt>60.3 excess-dupe deficit — the UNIQUE rate is the correct "enough content to hold 60" signal, which also preserved the #1111 62/period-15 "hold 60" guarantee byte-identical.
- REVIEW (Fable, gate OPEN) found a 🔴: a FROZEN source (100% dupes — dead painter/wedged input) left the unique window stale-TRUE so retirement fired forever and the NDI emit COLLAPSED to ~0.2fps (blackout, worse than the pre-fix graceful 60fps-of-copies). FIXED: prune the window every poll (honest count) + a FRESHNESS gate (retire only if the last unique arrived within 5 emit intervals) → a freeze falls back to the copy valve (frozen picture on a live stream). Also fixed 🟡 (floor now PARAMETRIC on interval; lowered to 57fps == the #666 floor because a 2s count can't separate 60-unique-jittery (dips to ~115) from 57.9-unique (~117) — they OVERLAP, so prioritise the rig and let a genuinely-57.9-unique source emit its honest rate; the #1111 62/period-15 test updated to that intentional v2 behavior) + 🔵 (stale docs, tautological summary test, backward-clock-step window clear). 🔵 file-size (>1000 lines) deliberately not split (code ~500 lines; tests inline per module convention + the ONLY local Tier-0 route runs inline tests).
- Verified: rustc --edition 2021 --test SCRATCH (genlock_pacing+dupe_decimation submodules run the real poll) — 47 pass. Off-rig against the REAL poll: emitted copies -> 0 at takt 61.x+jitter, 0 skips; FROZEN -> ~59fps of copies (never a blackout); cam3 exactly-60 + 50->60 pulldown byte-identical; under-59 unchanged. cargo fmt --all --check clean. Live uniformity >=0.95 in an MEQ E2E = supervisor/rig-ops step.
- WORKTREE MODE — stopped at green LOCAL result; supervisor integrates (merge/CI/deploy/card).

## #1129 — Windows client step-threshold read from /status for the step-aware gate widening (v1.7.0-dev.500)
- Root cause: `grade_http_node` reads `client_journal` ONLY for kind="linux" (`read_linux_node_journal`); a WINDOWS client (strih/stream) is HTTP-only (no journald), so BOTH the median widening (`client_chase_bound_us`) and the #1123 stability widening (`client_chase_stability_us`) fell back to `client_step_fallback` (700us). Its stability bound stayed the base 2000us and a healthy ~3.4ms client step straddling the sample window false-UNSTABLE'd the whole E2E (PR #1125 attempt 4, "client step threshold via fallback(700us)", spread 3380>2000). dantesync 1.8.48 published no client step threshold in /status (`ntp_deadband_us` is server-mode-only per issue 83).
- Fix (two repos, graceful): (camera-box) new pure fn `client_max_step_threshold_us_from_status_lines` in clock-offset-guard.sh (window-MAX of `ntp_step_threshold_us` across the sampled payloads, mirror of `client_max_step_threshold_us_from_journal`); grade_http_node's win branch reads it and passes it as the client step term into BOTH widenings via the existing step-fallback slot — no widening-fn signature change. Honest note: "its own /status (Nus)" when served, "fallback(700us)" when absent. LINUX path byte-identical (still passes 700us fallback; journal provides the real value internally). (dantesync PR #102 / issue 101) new additive `SyncStatus.ntp_step_threshold_us: Option<i64>` (`#[serde(default)]`) populated in update_shared_status regardless of mode: server=server_step_threshold_us, client=calculate_ntp_adaptive_threshold (the same value the journal logs as threshold:Nus).
- Decision: rejected (a) deriving the threshold from config (it is a DYNAMIC MAD estimate, not static) and (b) reusing `ntp_deadband_us` for clients (changes its documented server-only semantics). New additive field is the smallest robust path.
- Verified LOCALLY (Tier-0, gate is a bash script so RED->GREEN ran directly with fixtures): win straddle median1924/spread2938 + /status step 3400 -> stability widened 2000->4400, exit 0 GREEN (was exit 20 UNSTABLE pre-fix); win scatter spread15000 + step500 -> still FAIL(20); win no-field -> fallback(700us) FAIL(20) graceful; LINUX #1123 straddle UNCHANGED (PASS via journal 7860 stability). New pure fn direct: max/null/absent/empty correct. bash -n + shellcheck (both scripts) clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean. dantesync CI: Lint + Version-Consistency + Build(ubuntu) + Test(ubuntu) GREEN (Rust type-checks + all tests pass).
- HAND-OFF (live-fleet, supervisor): merge dantesync PR #102 -> cut dantesync release (CI artifacts) -> canary-first fleet upgrade (dantesync-fleet-upgrade.sh) -> bump DANTESYNC_VERSION_PIN in scripts/dantesync-version-gate.sh AFTER the upgrade lands -> then the #1129 fix takes live effect. camera-box gate change merges safely first (graceful 700us on the current 1.8.48 fleet).
- WORKTREE MODE — stopped at green LOCAL result; supervisor integrates the camera-box branch (merge/CI/deploy/card) + drives the dantesync release/deploy.

## #1146 — imag HDMI tearing: persist picom vsync + HDMI-primary; flip display-path facets (v1.7.0-dev.501)
- Root cause: imag drives TWO 60Hz outputs (eDP panel + HDMI projector) on independent crystals; GL/scanout vsyncs only the PRIMARY CRTC, so the #841 "compositor-free direct scanout = tear-free" doctrine (correct for ONE output) does not anchor the projector -> the two clocks BEAT -> intermittent walking tear line ("raz dobre, raz zle"). Live fix (deployed by hand 2026-08-20): picom v10 glx vsync compositor (unredir-if-possible=false) ANCHORED on the projector by making HDMI the xrandr primary. This ticket = PERSISTENCE + VERIFICATION (the fix was live-only, NOT reproducible in provisioning: setup-imag.sh had no picom step and still primaried the PANEL, so the next X restart would undo it).
- STEP-0 (live 10.77.9.182): picom v10 running (pid 2038724) + user service enabled+active + conf at ~/.config/picom/picom.conf; HDMI-1 live-primary but autostart still PANEL-primary (persistence gap CONFIRMED). #781 physical HDMI tap is ops-wait (hardware) -> tear CANNOT be machine-measured -> verification is honest report-only config-state, never a "tear-free output" claim.
- Fix: (1) scripts/lib/imag-display-path.sh — picom_process running=OK/off=DRIFT (REVERSES the #780/#841 picom-off facet), picom_autostart -> picom_service (bus-free *.target.wants enable symlink), NEW hdmi_primary facet (HDMI primary=OK, panel=DRIFT, missing xrandr/empty read=UNKNOWN by #833 two-tier). drift-guard --check-imag + the E2E [0/8] preflight consume the SHARED verdict (generic loop, zero edits there). (2) setup-imag.sh — TOTAL_STEPS 26->27; step 16 autostart primaries HDMI PROJ not PANEL (reverses the #522/#488 panel-primary; projector placement is by connector type in imag_scenes.py, not --primary, so safe); NEW step 27 installs picom + writes byte-faithful conf/service + enables (enable-only, never --now). Inert 20-tearfree.conf deliberately NOT provisioned (#841 proved TearFree dead on modesetting; keeps that gate green). (3) verify-imag.sh — check (z) reuses the shared verdict as the post-reboot acceptance gate. (4) .claude/rules/imag-display-path.md updated for the doctrine reversal.
- Verified: bash-level RED->GREEN (old lib reports live gather as picom-DRIFT + 4 facets; new lib = 5 OK); LIVE end-to-end gather over ssh from imag-nb = 5/5 OK; drift-guard check_imag_report picom-off + panel-primary each -> exit 20; cargo fmt --all --check clean; bash -n + shellcheck -S error clean on all 3 scripts; anchor occurrence-sweep clean (only the intended primary reversal + TOTAL_STEPS counts changed). - Scope: robustness automation (#297/#265 class) for the ShadowCast 2 stuck state — free-run ~62.5 fps + persistent corrupted frames, which `systemctl restart camera-box` does NOT clear but a USB re-enumeration does (live #1110 comment 5338231650, 2026-08-19). A new pure detector fires STUCK only on over-rate (fps>=61.5) AND persistent-corrupted (delta>0), both sustained 6 windows (~30s). A benign over-rate wobble (0 corrupted, absorbed by the decimation gate — #909) can NEVER fire, so it does not re-introduce the #909/#914 reset-spam. Verified via rustc --edition 2021 --test scratch.

## #1148 — consolidate the 5x-duplicated cam2-painter genuine-painting signal (v1.7.0-dev.508)
- Scope (cross-cutting review-lane follow-up from issues 1114/1126): the presenter-aware "is cam2-painter GENUINELY painting, not just process-alive" predicate (KMS page-flip line parse + `fuser` device-held + `vblank-locked` + `/dev/fb0` fallback) was copy-pasted into 5 `scripts/lib/*.sh` `_cmds` builders and had begun to drift (recheck polled 6x, verify 8x). Black-monitor-safety code (issues 863/860/464): a signal fix in one copy would leave the other four able to false-pass a dead monitor.
- Design (recorded on ticket): extract the SIGNAL into ONE source-only lib `scripts/lib/cam2-paint-signal.sh` — `cam2_paint_signal_remote_fn` emits a remote bash fn `_cb_paint_signal [FB_DEVICE]` (reads log on stdin, echoes a reason token KMS_OK/KMS_NODRM/KMS_NOVBLANK/FBDEV_OK/FBDEV_DEAD, `return`s 0 iff painting; never `exit`, safe in a set -e remote AND cleanup()'s WARN-only trap). Each of the 5 builders lazy-sources it (the bundle-state-selfheal.sh `command -v ... || . "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/..."` idiom), emits the fn def OUTSIDE its own heredoc (uniform across single-quoted + $-escaped heredocs), and pipes its own log source in — keeping each site's poll count + exit semantics. The reason token lets presenter-liveness keep its granular operator messages. Rejected: a dev1-side shared fn (predicate must run `fuser` ON the box) and string-only extraction (leaves the structure duplicated).
- Out of scope (documented): `scripts/verify-device.sh`'s 6th REDUCED variant — journal-only, no fuser/fb0, runs dev1-side (greps a remotely-captured journal), so it can't share the on-box predicate.
- REVIEW CATCH (fresh-context general-purpose reviewer, 0R/2Y/1B → 0/0/0 after fix): my presenter-liveness functional tests used `set -uo pipefail`, but the production caller (rig-mode.sh painter_launch_remote) runs the snippet under `set -e`, where the consolidated `_reason="$(… | _cb_paint_signal …)"` assignment aborted on a FAIL token BEFORE the case — silently swallowing the granular FAIL message + log tail (the 464 operator-blindness regression). Fixed: `|| true` on the substitution (token still captured, case runs, FAIL arm exits 1 loudly) + harness now runs under `set -euo pipefail` (RED→GREEN guard). Restored the original KMS-not-held wording (the 1B). GOTCHA learned: a backtick in a comment INSIDE an unquoted heredoc is build-time command substitution — moved to plain text.
- Commits: bump 1.7.0-dev.508 (ef461119d); refactor (47e1c849c); playbook doc (f32956cd7); review fix (cbc9466fe).
- Verification (Tier-0, zero cargo compile): all 5 builders' emitted output + exit semantics verified against fakes exactly matching their Rust harness assertions (restore-verify 4 cases, recheck 4, handoff anchors+pass/fail, mv-reverify 3, presenter-liveness 7 under set -euo); the shared predicate's 8 token/exit cases pinned by a NEW `tests/harness_cam2_paint_signal_1148.rs`; recheck-1126 anchor test moved from lib-source-read to emitted-output assertion. `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `shellcheck -S warning` clean on all 6 shell files; occurrence-count anchor sweep OLD-vs-dev shows no test-source-read regression (only the recheck-1126 signal-literal move, which the test update covers). CI is the first place the Rust tests type-check + run.

## 2026-08-20 — #1153 A/V dock marker measurement chain reliability (worktree lane)
- Root cause: the QPSK marker demod accept gate checked only preamble-nibble(0xF)+CRC-4 = 8 bits, never the always-zero nibble at bits[15:12] the emitter always sends (payload_word). Enumerated: of 4096 words passing preamble+CRC, 256 valid vs 3840 "poison" (nonzero zero-nibble) => 16x-inflated false-positive cloud drowning the real cluster. Live-confirmed on stream dock (15:05 today): crc_ok flooded (48278), matched only ~26, mad ~30ms, offset center wandering 127-139ms; the "98.7% CRC fail" is inherent CRC-4 physics, NOT the disease.
- Fix (c940c4a40): add the zero-nibble conjunct to the accept gate, mirrored lockstep in the pure Rust kernel qpsk_marker::decode_markers_with_stats (feeds BOTH offline recording-verdict --av-sync AND the live dock StreamingMarkerDecoder) + the byte-for-byte C++ mirror camera-box-audio.hpp::cb_decode_markers_with_stats. Shrinks the CRC-passing accept-space 4096->256 (exactly 16x), all 256 real markers retained.
- TDD: RED 1f5488e30 test(#1153) decode_rejects_crc_valid_word_with_nonzero_zero_nibble_1153 (+ decode_still_accepts_a_real_marker_and_every_index_has_zero_nibble_1153) — poison word 0xF1002 (preamble F, zero-nib 1, CRC valid) was accepted by the OLD decoder. GREEN c940c4a40 enforces the zero nibble. Added a C++ selftest poison CHECK too.
- Tier-0 verification (local compilation blocked, incl. no-run per #557): standalone rustc replica proved OLD accepts poison / NEW rejects (crc_ok 1->0) + real marker preserved; g++ -Wall -Wextra -Werror selftest ALL PASS (256 real indices still round-trip + poison rejected); rustfmt check clean.
- Refactor: extracted pure marker_signal_for_word(word,p) (Rust) / marker_signal_from_word(word) (C++ selftest) so a test can synthesize an arbitrary word; marker_signal(index) delegates (behavior-preserving; no caller stranded).
- Honesty: the fix LOWERS the crc_ok/crc_fail "success rate" proxy (it moves poison decodes into crc_fail) — that proxy is misleading (a 4-bit CRC can never exceed ~1/16 "success" on a noisy mix); the RIGHT metric (cluster size/tightness/stability) improves. The final live cluster size ("stovky vzoriek") is the supervisor's Faza-3 re-measurement AFTER the C++ dock is rebuilt (windows-genlock-fast.yml avsyncdock-fast-dll) + deployed. Secondary residual causes (marginal acoustic SNR at the 442Hz≈concert-A carrier; ASRC/Dante rate smear) are rig/protocol-level, proposed as follow-ups.
- WORKTREE MODE — stopped at green LOCAL result; supervisor integrates (merge/CI/deploy) + does the live re-measurement.

  shipped the placeholder ("NDI preview — M2"); M2 is the real pipeline.
- Presenter technique (dev2 read-only): NDI recv = dynamic libloading of libndi.so (presenter-ndi
  src/ndi_sdk.rs), web delivery = gstreamer ndisrc -> webrtcsink (WHEP/WebRTC, gst-plugin-ndi 0.15).
  DECISION: WebRTC+gstreamer is too heavy + CI-unverifiable for a ~3fps shading preview; extracted only
  the minimal "NDI recv -> per-frame" pattern; delivery is JPEG-over-HTTP instead.
- KEY reuse: the APPLIANCE already has a full native NDI receiver at src/ndi.rs (NdiReceiver::connect +
  capture_frame, recv_create_v3 with bandwidth field, recv_capture_v3, recv_free_video_v2). The real
  preview receiver mirrors that FFI exactly, only swapping bandwidth HIGHEST(100) -> LOWEST(0). Source
  naming = substring match, convention "NAME (hostname)" (matches M1 ndi_preview = "CAM1 (usb)").
- Design (NON-TRIVIAL design comment on the ticket): Approach 1 (CHOSEN) stub-source-default +
  real-NDI feature-gated OFF + pure decimate/encode/convert core + JPEG over HTTP latest-frame.
  Approach 2 REJECTED = WebRTC/WHEP like presenter (heavy, CI-unverifiable). Approach 3 REJECTED for M2
  = WS binary push (M1 has no WS surface; more moving parts, worse through cloudflare, marginal at 3fps).
- Structure: new preview module in bkshading/service. Pure/CI-tested: frame, pattern, decimate, encode
  (jpeg-encoder 0.7, pure Rust), convert (UYVY/BGRA/RGBA->RGB), store (per-camera latest JPEG). Runtime
  glue: source (PreviewSource trait + StubSource), worker (one OS thread per camera, backoff reconnect).
  Feature ndi (OFF by default): ndi_source.rs = minimal libloading FFI mirror of src/ndi.rs at LOWEST.
  HTTP: GET /api/cameras/<id>/preview.jpg (image/jpeg, no-store; 404 unknown cam, 503 until first frame).
  Web UI: 4+4 preview block renders a live <img> reloaded ~3x/s; no-preview camera stays params-only.
- Commits: dbe0088ef feat (service code + web + Rust tests + example), 762dd3f2e test (python web-UI/
  config asserts + CI clippy on the ndi feature). Backup ref refs/autopilot-wip/808-m2-preview.
- GOTCHAS captured (see .claude/rules/bkshading.md candidate): (1) jpeg-encoder 0.7 Encoder::new(w,q)
  returns Encoder NOT Result; encode(self, &[u8], u16, u16, ColorType). (2) Rust 1.98 clippy rejects
  chunks_exact(N) with a constant N -> use index math (or as_chunks::<N>().0). (3) FFI init: inline
  *lib.get(...)? temporaries in a struct literal live to end-of-statement, so moving the Library into the
  last field is E0505 — deref-copy each fn pointer into its own `let` FIRST (each ? temp ends per stmt),
  then move lib into _library. (4) private unread fields on #[repr(C)] FFI structs trip dead_code under
  -D warnings -> #[allow(dead_code)] (appliance src/ndi.rs used pub fields instead).

## 2026-08-21 — #1145 round 3: noise-tolerant content-compare dupe detection (CAM2 churn)
- Issue #1145 (over-rate takt absorbed without cadence damage) round 3. v1 retire / v2 depth-drain /
  v2.1 fast-drain (merged) removed content-COPIES but left CAM2 at 0.93-0.95 (below the 0.95 floor).
  Root cause (issue-1130 comment 5364318219): CAM2 is the marginal jittery ~61 fps painter box; over a
  full optical hop its surplus is a NOISY re-sample (sensor noise), not a byte-identical buffer-repeat
  like CAM1's steady ~64 — so the exact-FNV `is_dupe` missed it, it emitted as a "unique" (Δ1) and
  forced a compensating shed (Δ3) = the balanced-pair churn.
- Fix: `dupe_content_sig` (exact hash + luma lattice, one pass; legacy `dupe_content_hash` delegates)
  + a noise-tolerant `frames_are_content_dupes` two-threshold sparse-diff (median-offset; theta 48 /
  max-changed 6) + `note_frame_luma` staged before poll; `is_dupe = exact || (sustained_over_rate &&
  !prev_was_noisy_dupe && compare)`. Structural cage (over-rate-armed + never-two-consecutive + exact
  first) makes a false-positive physically impossible for the burn geometry and biases hard to
  false-negative (a miss = status quo). poll stays 6-arg → all pre-round-3 tests byte-untouched.
- Commits: 7958d72e0 (bump 526) -> def21ded5 [red] -> 6361c47fa [green] (+ main.rs wiring).
- Sim (REAL poll, root.rs #[path]): marginal noisy 61.0/61.3 -> 1.0000, 61.5 -> 0.9766 (all >=0.95,
  Δ1/Δ3 collapsed) vs exact-hash baseline 0.9415/0.9245/0.9130; CAM1-64 byte-identical WITH==WITHOUT
  note_frame_luma (identical decisions); healthy 60.00 inert. 61/61 pure-seam tests green via
  rustc --test scratch; cargo fmt --all --check clean. Design pressure-tested via a gated Fable consult.
- Design gate: STEP-0 validated + non-trivial design comment posted (standalone gh issue comment).
- WORKTREE MODE: stopped at green LOCAL result; supervisor integrates (merge + full CI + deploy + the
  live uniformity>=0.95 + QR-contiguity re-measure — the acceptance is that live step, NOT off-rig).
  No PR/merge/deploy/run-card by the worker. Ticket stays OPEN (acceptance is a live measurement).

## issue 1101 — calibrate + optimize the #1088 dup-cadence surface before a LIVE gate (worktree)
- Premise re-validated: the #1088 duplication-masked 50→60 surface, structurally unreachable in the merge gate when #1088 shipped (0/81 verdicts), now EMITS in production after #1112 (18/22 retained `/tmp/recording-e2e-*/verdict-*.json` carry `all_cambox_continuity.duplication_masked_cadence`), so calibration is finally possible.
- Calibration verdict (data-first, no fresh E2E): mined all 18 emitting verdicts + their `stream-partial-*.json`. `duplicate_fraction` reads 0.0 in EVERY window of EVERY run (180 windows) — but it is a FALSE zero. Correlating consecutive frames in the stream partials: 147 tick-proven copies (repeated Vernier tick = a byte-duplicate camera frame, exactly what `copies` counts) vs only 2 content-hash duplicates ≈ 1.4% observed. Root cause: `frame_content_hash` is BYTE-EXACT FNV-1a over the STREAM box's LOSSY `.mp4` recording; byte identity does not survive lossy encode+decode. So NO LIVE threshold is honestly calibratable — a flip would be a permanent false-green (a real pulldown's dupes also become byte-unique). cam1 (issue 1145) segregation is moot: with the signal dead, cam1 reads 0.0 like every box.
- Optimization shipped (report-only, Tier-0): pure crate-root signal-viability self-diagnosis in src/dup_cadence.rs — `CopyObservation` + `copy_observation`/`aggregate_copy_observations` (cross-check content-hash dups vs tick-copies over the SAME frames) + `SignalViability{Viable,Blind,Indeterminate}` + `signal_viability`/`signal_promotable`, consts `MIN_TICK_COPIES_FOR_VIABILITY=3` / `COPY_OBSERVATION_RATE_MIN=0.5`. Emitted into the merge dup-cadence node (`signal_viability`/`signal_promotable`/`tick_proven_copies`/`copies_observed_by_content_hash`/`content_hash_duplicates`/`copy_observation_rate`) so an all-zero distribution can no longer be mistaken for promotable. `gates_overall_pass()` stays false; its doc now records the flip precondition = `signal_promotable == true` on real runs (NOT a bare threshold tweak). Replica over mined data: 10 runs Blind, 8 Indeterminate, 0 Viable.
- TDD (Tier-0, #477/#557 block ALL local cargo incl --no-run): [red] 7dd4eec0f stubs+tests, [green] 1643f11ee real impls, [feat] 5805f6695 merge emit. Verified via `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` (parses dup_cadence.rs + probe-gated recording-verdict.rs) + a Python classifier replica over the real partials; CI is the first type-check.
- Closes verdict: NO. The surface is NOT promotable (signal blind); the flip stays a documented one-line seam. #1101 stays OPEN carrying the promote step. The signal FIX (codec-tolerant near-duplicate hash / lossless re-tap + a real 50→60 pulldown run to validate) filed as #1166. PR body must NOT add `Closes #1101`.
- Playbook: added §11 to `.claude/rules/verdict-gate-seam-calibration.md` (a content metric needs a VIABILITY cross-check, not just a reachability check, before threshold calibration; all-zero green ≠ promotable).

  with its only caller (DecimationGate) so no private item crosses a submodule boundary; (3) shed.rs's
  6 cross-module intra-doc links repointed to full crate::dupe_decimation::DecimationGate:: paths (its
  code is self-contained -> `use super::*` would be an unused import = CI clippy -D warnings fail);

  include-path edit.
- GOTCHA (this split): the test module lives as a top-level `mod tests;` child of mod.rs (SIBLING of
  gate.rs), so it can NO LONGER reach DecimationGate's private methods the way an in-file
  `mod tests {}` child of the impl could — hence the 2 pub(crate) promotions. Alternative (nest tests
  under gate.rs) was rejected: it would file the signature/shed tests under the gate module and relies
  on `super::*` transitivity for a std type. Also: rustfmt REQUIRES the moved test body at column 0 for
  a top-level module file, so it de-indented tests.rs (whitespace + dropped now-optional trailing
  commas on re-wrapped lines) — token-identical, proven by a whitespace+comma-stripped diff (67425==67425).

## 2026-08-21 — issue 1166: dup-cadence content-hash was blind on the lossy tap — signal FIXED (codec-tolerant near-duplicate), report-only kept
- Root cause (re-mined from retained partials): the #1088 dup-cadence surface hashed the STREAM
  box's lossy .mp4 with a BYTE-EXACT row-sampled FNV-1a; byte identity does not survive H.264, so
  the 1101 viability cross-check read Blind (run 460600987: 68 tick-copies, 0 observed by hash; 32
  tick-copy PNG pairs across 12 runs, 0/32 observed).
- Fix (Approach 1 of the ticket, the only locally-validatable one): replace the per-frame hash with
  a codec-tolerant near-duplicate signal — a row-sampled mean-abs-luma-DIFFERENCE (MAD) to the
  recording predecessor, thresholded at NEAR_DUP_MAD_MAX=10.0. Validated on the retained real lossy
  diagnostic PNGs: 26/32 = 81% of tick-proven copies observed at 0/381 = 0.0% motion false-positive
  -> SignalViability::Viable. Downscaled thumbnails destroy the separation; full-width row-sampling
  (MAD_SAMPLE_ROWS=64) preserves the full-res separation cheaply, so the MAD is computed on the box
  between consecutive full-res frames and carried per frame.
- Files: src/dup_cadence.rs (frame_content_hash->frame_row_sampled_mad + is_near_duplicate;
  measure_dup_cadence/copy_observation/window_content_hashes->window_prev_mads re-typed onto
  Option<f64>; DupCadence.exact_duplicates->near_duplicates; CopyObservation fields renamed; embedded
  real-lossy-copy fixture test). src/probe/recording.rs (hash_recording_frames->frame_prev_diffs).
  src/probe/recording_partial.rs (content_hashes->frame_prev_diffs Option<Vec<Option<f64>>>,
  PARTIAL_SCHEMA_VERSION 5->6). src/bin/recording-verdict.rs (producer + merge + wrapper rename;
  one window sequence feeds both classifier + cross-check, resolving the 1101 sequence-mismatch).
  .claude/rules/verdict-gate-seam-calibration.md section 13.
- LIVE flip stays BLOCKED / report-only: the PNG corpus is biased and existing partials carry the
  old byte-exact hashes, so the full-run signal_viability distribution + a DUP_RATE_PULLDOWN_MIN
  recalibration need a fresh green run emitting the new signal. gates_overall_pass() stays false;
  promotion gated on signal_promotable==true on >=2 consecutive real runs + a recalibrated bound.
- Tier-0: pure module RED->GREEN via the rustc --test scratch route (28/28 green); probe-gated
  files verified via cargo fmt --all --check + hand type-audit (no local type-check exists).

## 2026-08-22 — #1167 (over-rate emit under-runs the 60fps grid; the merged make-up doesn't fire) — worktree worktree-agent-af30b32337f454ed6, base 31ea0cb00 (dev.532)

(2) The real 58.5 fps deficit (over-rate; cam3 at-rate holds 60.0 on identical hw) is the over-rate absorption ADVANCING a boundary while emitting nothing — a SKIPPED slot the buffered surplus could have filled; continuous send-jitter re-injects shallow lag every window (live: retired>0, drained>0, fast_drained==0). Diagnostic identity from existing journalctl: `sent + retired + drained + 2×fast_drained ≈ 300/5s`.

Make-up code kept but DORMANT.
- **#1142-safe:** a fill during a lag episode occupies a slot no unique could fill (missed boundary) → unpaired Δ0, not the paired copy+dropped-unique churn. `retired`→~0, `dupe_emitted`→legit nonzero on the over-rate box. `WINDOW_COPIES_GAPS_TOLERANCE` is the live-E2E re-check.

## 2026-08-22 — #1167 v4 (UNDER-rate empty-queue starvation under-runs the grid) — worktree worktree-agent-ac639c776936326c2, base 0270c2cc8 (dev.534)

- **Root cause (off-rig, real `poll`, #557 scratch).** v2/v3 fixed OVER-rate; the grabber WANDERS across 60 (57.9–63.6). In an UNDER-rate window the v2/v3 fills have nothing to fill with — the whole machinery runs INSIDE `poll` (fired per captured frame; `capture.process_frame`'s blocking dequeue has no grid timer), and only CONVERTS a captured frame's shed into a copy. Fewer than 60 captures/s ⇒ fewer than 60 polls ⇒ fewer than 60 emits. Each empty-queue boundary (`queue_had_frame==false`) goes unfilled; grid lag creeps to the #131 resync which skips it. Reproduced: 57.9fps → 290/300 sent, 36 #707 skips/20s, ZERO dupe-decimation events (`sustained_over_rate` FALSE at 57.9). The #1145 copy valve can't help (needs a DUPE arriving; an under-capturing source delivers FEWER all-unique frames). The #1167 corrupted make-up (TENTH piece) stays DORMANT — that was the over-rate corruption case.
- **Fix = bounded last-frame REPEAT (poll Emit arm; NO new ShedAction; the pure `dupe_shed_action` DECISION byte-unchanged).** On `!copy && !queue_had_frame && sustained_under_rate() && !converging_deep_backlog && 1<=lag<=GENLOCK_MAX_CATCHUP_INTERVALS`, `poll` reports `min(lag, STARVATION_REPEAT_MAX-consecutive)` repeats via `last_poll_starvation_repeats()` and advances `next_boundary = candidate_next + repeats*interval` (capped, never past `now`). `main.rs` re-emits the CURRENT good frame (passed the corruption check) that many times with distinct per-slot timecodes, then the current frame.
- **POSITIVE under-rate gate, not `!sustained_over_rate`.** New `sustained_under_rate()` = `takt_ema != 0 && takt_ema > STARVATION_MIN_TAKT_INTERVAL_NS (1e9/59.8)`. The `takt_ema != 0` requirement is load-bearing: legacy over-rate/starved tests pass `capture_mono_ns==0` (EMA disabled → `!sustained_over_rate` TRUE even at over-rate), which wrongly armed v4 and broke 5 tests; the positive signal fires only on a MEASURED under-rate. over/under mutually exclusive (16.722 > 16.584); healthy 60.0 (EMA 16.667) reads FALSE for both.
- **FORWARD-FILL, not a saved last-good buffer.** The dispatch suggested a saved buffer; that adds a ~4MB memcpy PER FRAME to the zero-copy production hot path (#279/#280) — a jitter/throughput regression #899 can't afford. The current frame is GOOD (corruption-checked); the ≤4-frame content-freshness diff the strih genlock FIFO re-times away, identical in the id-contiguity + uniformity metrics.
- **Bounded + dead-leg exposed.** `STARVATION_REPEAT_MAX`=4 CONSECUTIVE repeats, reset by any on-time capture (`lag==0`). A live-but-slow 57.9fps card (crosses a boundary ~2×/s, ~27 on-time frames between) is fully filled; a frozen source (dupes → `Emit{copy:true}` → the `!copy` gate excludes it → 0 repeats) and a 30fps half-rate source stay exposed under 60 → visible to #666 / frozen-leg attribution (checked `.claude/rules/self-heal-frozen-leg-attribution.md`: no masking).
- **Decoupled from v2/v3 + #707.** Separate `starvation_repeats` counter (drained via `take_starvation_repeats()`; the 6-tuple `take_shed_counts` byte-frozen), separate gate, never touches the v3 `last_converge_skip_mono_ns` budget. Folded into `last_poll_intentional_extra_advance` (= fast_drain_extra + starvation_repeats, mutually exclusive) so a FILLED slot is deducted from the #707 diagnostic. APPENDED a summary segment (existing substrings byte-frozen). Pure Tier-0 `starvation_repeat_timecode_100ns` helper for the per-slot stamps.
- **Off-rig (real `poll`, #557 scratch):** 57.9 290→300/window, 59.7 299→300, 0 net #707 skips; over-rate 63.6 + healthy 60.0 byte-inert; frozen 0 repeats; 30fps exposed under 60. RED (2 starvation tests fail on pre-fix) → GREEN; 83/83 module tests (75 orig + 2 core + 4 guards + 2 timecode); `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. main.rs UNVERIFIABLE locally (#557) — the `emit_one` closure refactor's type/borrow is CI's first check.
- **Review (Opus 4.8, Fable gate CLOSED at 88%) = SHIP-WITH-FIXES, 0 red 0 yellow 2 blue, both INSIDE the diff → fixed.** Independent: 83/83 scratch tests, genuine RED, every composition axis verified against the actual code. The 2 blue: (1) `poll` grew to ~349 lines (over the ~300-line budget) → extracted the starvation block into a private `apply_starvation_fill` helper (mirrors `fill_slot`) → poll ~316; (2) the cap-reach doc overstated "half-rate leg hits this cap" → narrowed to ≤~30fps (the 31–56fps band is filled + exposed by the capture-rate health guards on the same takt EMA, not this cap; a frozen source is excluded by the `!copy` gate). UNVERIFIABLE-locally (Tier-0): main.rs `emit_one` closure type/borrow under both cfg — reviewer found no error; CI is the first real compile.

## 2026-08-24 — #1186 frame-probe SIGTERM handler runs the issue-660 fb0 blank on any unit stop (worktree agent-ad95e62f60fb81bba)
- Prong 1 of issue 1176. Root cause (traced, probe-gated code, no local compile): the issue-660 blank (src/probe/fb.rs::blank_fbdev) is called from EXACTLY ONE place — impl Drop for KmsPresenter (src/probe/kms.rs). The presenter is owned by the painter thread run_painter (src/probe/painter.rs); its Drop runs only when the paint loop breaks (clean --duration-secs self-exit or the outer loop setting `stop`). No SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP handler existed anywhere (frame-probe.rs main is a plain fn main; only src/main.rs, the production binary, handles tokio ctrl_c = SIGINT). So `systemctl stop cam2-painter.service` (SIGTERM default disposition = terminate, no unwind) skipped Drop, /dev/fb0 kept the last painted frame, kernel fbdev emulation revealed it on cam2's monitor. The existing bash mitigation (scripts/lib/cam2-fb0-blank.sh, painter_stop_remote) covers ONLY the rig-mode.sh EVENT path (prong 2). STEP-0 validation comment 5388827326.
- Design (comment 5388836833, non-trivial, 3 approaches): chose (1) an async-signal-safe global flag polled by the existing loops — handler body is ONLY an AtomicBool store; the loops break so the EXISTING tested KmsPresenter::Drop teardown runs (blank BEFORE releasing DRM master, #660 ordering preserved). Rejected (2) a dedicated signal thread blanking fb0 directly (can't guarantee blank-before-release ordering while the painter holds DRM master) and (3) libc::atexit (never runs on signal-driven termination — fixes nothing).
- Implementation: NEW crate-root src/shutdown.rs — PURE half (SHUTDOWN_REQUESTED AtomicBool + request_shutdown/is_shutdown_requested + painter_should_continue(local_stop, shutdown_requested)) is std-only + Tier-0-testable; OS-GLUE half (install() -> libc::sigaction for SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, handler = the atomic store) is cfg(target_os="linux") on the existing Linux-only libc dep (NOT probe-gated, so cargo fmt + CI default build compile it). Wired: painter.rs paint loop `while painter_should_continue(stop, is_shutdown_requested())`; run.rs run_paint_only + run call install() at start + break their outer loops on is_shutdown_requested().
- Review finding folded IN-BRANCH (hook chain-depth cap steered it to a fix, not a depth-2 follow-up ticket): the fbdev fallback presenter VsyncFb had NO Drop at all, so neither clean exit nor SIGTERM blanked fb0 on the fbdev path (only KMS was covered). Added `device: String` field + impl Drop for VsyncFb calling the same blank_fbdev (best-effort, mirrors KmsPresenter::Drop) — completes #1186's "any unit stop leaves a clean surface" on BOTH presenters; matters on the issue-854 silent KMS->fbdev fallback. Corrected two now-stale docstrings (fb_blank.rs "VsyncFb neither clears it on exit"; blank_fbdev stale-source note).
- TDD (Tier-0, no local cargo #477/#557): the PURE flag + painter_should_continue proven RED->GREEN via a rustc --test replica of BOTH the stub (2/2 FAIL) and the shipped module extracted from the real src/shutdown.rs (2/2 PASS). rustfmt --check clean on every changed file (parses the probe-gated + libc glue). sighandler_t cast is the std idiom; libc::sigaction glue + VsyncFb::Drop + probe wiring first type-check at CI (probe/glue has no local path). VsyncFb::Drop carries [no-test:] — hardware fbdev glue over the already-tested visible_page_range, mirrors the untested issue-660 KmsPresenter::Drop precedent.
- Review (fresh-context, /review + requesting-code-review standards): 0 red 0 yellow 5 blue (comment 5388947380). Blue 1 + blue 3 fixed in-branch; blue 2/4/5 non-actionable notes (std-idiom cast; no cross-test race; harmless test cleanup). Async-signal-safety, #660 ordering, no-regression (wedge watchdog / audio-marker loop / clean exit) all confirmed clean.

## 2026-08-24 — #1187 lipsync-test-mode playback off raw /dev/fb0 → DRM/KMS via mpv (worktree agent-a2ae9d4f35540458a, no version bump — supervisor versions at integration)
- Root cause: `scripts/lipsync-test-mode.sh`'s `lipsync_playback_cmds` wrote video into raw `/dev/fb0` via `ffmpeg -f fbdev` (lines 315/332). fbdev is legacy — no CRTC ownership, no exit teardown — so a killed ffmpeg left its last frame resident in fb0 memory, and the kernel fbdev emulation revealed it on cam2's HDMI the instant the painter's DRM master was released (prong 3 of #1176; the pacing guard was a SECOND raw fbdev writer, existing only because fb0 has no clock of its own). STEP-0 validated live (comment 5388837226): defect present in current code, mpv not provisioned, parent #1176 OPEN, no dup.
- Design (comment 5388844670, non-trivial, 3 approaches): chose owner-preferred mpv `--vo=drm` over (2) extending the frame-probe KMS presenter with video (owner: "more work, same effect", zero local compile path) and (3) keep-ffmpeg+blank-only (the "just a blank" non-fix the owner declined).
- Implementation (`scripts/lipsync-test-mode.sh`): `lipsync_playback_cmds` ffmpeg/fbdev → ONE `mpv --vo=drm` process — mpv takes the DRM master, page-flips its own buffers at vblank (never touches fb0), restores the CRTC on exit; audio to the SAME ALSA device (`--audio-device=alsa/...`, `--audio-channels=stereo`), `--loop-file=inf`, optional `--drm-device` pin via new `LIPSYNC_DRM_DEVICE` (default auto per the #854 unstable-card-numbering rule), fail-loud liveness. A/V lead moved from a two-demux ffmpeg `-itsoffset` to mpv native `--audio-delay` (NEGATIVE = delays video = equivalent of the old positive video itsoffset; 408→-0.408, 0→0.000). `lipsync_pacing_guard_cmd` → `lipsync_preflight_cmd`: the fbdev-no-clock cadence apparatus (~150 lines of showinfo/python) deleted (mpv paces off vblank), replaced by a `command -v mpv` presence check (fail-loud provisioning hint) + `mpv --vo=null --ao=null --frames=120` decode probe that touches neither fb0 nor the CRTC. `lipsync_stop_playback_cmds` blanks fb0 belt-and-braces after the kill, reusing the canonical #660 builder `rig_test_ledger_clean_paint_fallback_cmds` (sourced from scripts/lib/rig-test-ledger.sh, a pure lib — one source of truth). New `LIPSYNC_MPV_BIN` env seam (default mpv) for testability/pinning.
- Provisioning: setup-device.sh STEP 16 installs `mpv` on the same fail-loud lipsync-runtime apt line (mpv Depends on the ffmpeg libav* codecs already present, so --no-install-recommends still decodes H.264) + advertises it in the Installed echo; verify-device.sh gains an `(x2)` mpv present+runnable acceptance check mirroring the (x) ffmpeg check, inserted BEFORE the (q) last-check.
- TDD (Tier-0 #557, ZERO local cargo): [red] tests/harness_lipsync_test_mode.rs rewritten for mpv/DRM (fail vs current ffmpeg/fbdev) -> [green] the script -> [red] provisioning tests (mpv install + verify) -> [green] setup-device.sh + verify-device.sh (+ re-anchored the setup echo test on the unique `Installed: ffmpeg` prefix — the bare `  Installed:` is shared by 3 STEP-16 groups). RED proven by direct bash-source of the OLD script (ffmpeg/fbdev, `lipsync_preflight_cmd` absent); GREEN proven by direct bash-source of the NEW script — every generated line byte-matches the Rust assertions (one mpv process, `--audio-delay=-0.408`/`-0.125`/`0.000`, DRM auto-vs-pinned, preflight null-sinks present/missing/decode-fail via LIPSYNC_MPV_BIN, stop fb0-blank == canonical builder). `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S warning` clean on all 3 scripts; `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` clean on all 3 test files. No cross-file anchor collisions (the runbook `ffmpeg -version` anchor + the setup ffmpeg-install anchor intact).
- Review: self-review (my tier) + a fresh-context reviewer both → VERDICT CLEAN (0 🔴 0 🟡 0 🔵, comment 5388956133). Two sub-🔵 quoting nits ($mpv_bin / alsa/$audio unquoted) deliberately kept — single-token values, matches existing discipline, quoting would break the deterministic generated-text test contract.
- UNVERIFIED (supervisor rig steps, by design — code+tests lane, cam2 painter untouched): live mpv/DRM playback on cam2, and the 408 ms LIPSYNC_AUDIO_LEAD_MS constant may need re-derivation for mpv's ALSA buffering (the knob lets the supervisor re-tune via the paired cross-check campaign without a code change). The fb0-blank-in-rig-mode-event (prong 2, shipped) and the frame-probe SIGTERM blank remain necessary regardless (issue 1176 note; relates to the open issue-1173 deadman half).
- Worktree branch worktree-agent-a2ae9d4f35540458a; durability backup refs/autopilot-wip/worktree-agent-a2ae9d4f35540458a. Closes #1187 allowed in the round PR body; supervisor integrates.

## issue 1185 — pin 2ME PGM to the first NDI port (:5961) via early module-post-load reservation (worktree, split from issue 1181)
- Root cause: libndi assigns each NDIlib_send_create a TCP port sequentially from 5961 in CREATION ORDER. DistroAV plugin-main.cpp defers main_output_init()/preview_output_init() to OBS_FRONTEND_EVENT_FINISHED_LOADING (QMetaObject::invokeMethod queued) — AFTER scene load — so the per-source ndi_filter republishes (Grading/MULTIVIEW/interkom) win :5962-:5964 and the program (2ME PGM) lands on a high port; a stock NDI Studio Monitor / building TV reconnecting by cached port then gets the wrong sender after an OBS restart (issue 1180/1181). obs_module_post_load previously did only updateCheckStart().
- STEP 0 validation (comment 5388825122): confirmed still real against current vendored code — the deferral + post_load-does-nothing + inline send_create in ndi_output_start all present; no prior reservation code (grep) and no 1185/1181/1180 commit on dev.
- Design (comment 5388829267, non-trivial, 3 approaches): chose Option (b) reserve-and-reuse over (2) move the whole output start to post-load (video mix not ready — black/frameless, likely fails) and (3) an SDK/OS-level port pin (NDIlib_send_create_t exposes no per-sender port pin — investigate-existing-first, none fits).
- Implementation: (a) ndi-output.cpp — mutex-guarded reservation holder + ndi_output_reserve_main_sender (idempotent early send_create), ndi_output_release_reserved_main_sender (destroys an unadopted reservation), static ndi_output_take_reserved_sender (transfers ownership on an exact name+groups match, else nullptr -> fresh send_create); adoption wired into ndi_output_start. (b) plugin-main.cpp — obs_module_post_load reserves gated on config->OutputEnabled + non-empty name; obs_module_unload releases before ndiLib->destroy(). (c) both windows-genlock*.yml pwsh source-patch gates + tests/distroav_pgm_first_port_1185.rs Rust guard (mirrors distroav_timecode_patch.rs).
- TDD (RED->GREEN, Tier-0 no local cargo #557): [red] 12a4714ff guard test only; [green] b9f236c57 impl + workflow gates. Observed RED (3/3 fail) -> GREEN (3/3 ok) via the #1026 standalone-rustc recipe (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=<wt> rustc --test). Reservation helpers lift-and-compiled clean under `g++ -Wformat=2 -Wconversion`; brace/paren balance OK; both YAMLs parse; pwsh gate tokens verified against the real squished source.
- Review (comment 5388964151): adversarial fresh-context reviewer (gated Fable) + /review standards -> 0 crit, 2 warn, 2 sugg, ALL fixed in-branch (124ff530c): [warn] destroy the adopted sender if obs_output_begin_data_capture fails (else a frameless PGM ghost leaks + a duplicate high-port sender defeats the pin); [warn] re-anchor the pwsh + Rust plugin-main gates on the call-site-unique tokens (bare names also appear in the extern decls — the issue-832 anchor class, matters on the hot-swap path); [sugg] release an unadopted reservation in main_output_init when the output will not be created (enabled-but-unsupported ghost); [sugg] widen the thread comment (take() also on the obs-websocket thread).
- UNVERIFIED (this worker does NOT touch the live rig): the early-idle-sender tolerance of a stock NDI Studio Monitor / building TV (does it drop/blacklist a frameless source for the ~seconds of OBS load?) — must be checked on the live rig at integration per the ticket. Vendored send-path change: CI is the first compile.
- Closes: NO auto-close from this worker (leaves issue 1181 open — do not auto-close it). Worktree branch worktree-agent-a6aeaebce7e4094fb; durability backup refs/autopilot-wip/worktree-agent-a6aeaebce7e4094fb. Supervisor integrates; Closes #1185 belongs in the round PR body.

## 2026-08-24 — issue 1190 (lipsync-test-mode.sh start: mpv dies instantly) — worktree worktree-agent-a7128f9e46c81470d, base fb6667ca8 (dev)
- **Root cause:** `scripts/lipsync-test-mode.sh` `lipsync_stop_painter_cmds` freed cam2's display by killing the painter BY PIDFILE ONLY. But the steady-state painter runs under `cam2-painter.service` with `Restart=always` (`systemd/cam2-painter.service:10`, issue 1008 model): systemd respawns it ~100 ms after the kill and the respawn re-takes the DRM master, so `mpv --vo=drm` (the issue-1187 playback transport) started ~10 s later cannot acquire the CRTC and dies instantly. Secondary: mpv runs `--no-terminal` (swallows its stderr) with no `--log-file`, so `/run/rig-lipsync-playback.log` is empty and the death is undiagnosable.
- **Validated (STEP 0, comment 5390201698):** verified against current dev by sourcing the script — the stop builder has no unit stop / no is-active guard, the mpv builder has `--no-terminal` and no `--log-file`; `Restart=always` confirmed on the unit; not overcome by the 1187 rework (which is what made the collision fatal). Still valid.
- **Design (comment 5390213262, Triage: trivial):** chose (1) `systemctl stop cam2-painter` BEFORE the pidfile kill (systemd won't respawn a stopped unit; pidfile kill stays as a belt for the transient unit-less nohup painter per cam2-painter-lifecycle) + a post-stop fail-loud `systemctl is-active` guard mirroring the survived-TERM+KILL exit 1, and (2) mpv-native `--log-file` (keeping `--no-terminal`). Rejected: dropping `--no-terminal` for a bare stderr redirect (that redirect already existed + was empty; the native log is the reliable capture), and `systemctl disable` (EVENT-mode semantics, would fight the reboot-persistence the restore re-arms). Restore path unchanged: `cmd_stop` → `rig-mode.sh test` → `cam2_painter_steady_state_handoff_cmds` already `enable --now`s the unit (`scripts/lib/cam2-painter-handoff.sh:23,85`) — verified, no duplication.
- **TDD (RED→GREEN, Tier-0 no local cargo #557):** [red] `0196fa86b` (3 harness tests: unit-stop-before-pidfile-kill ordering, is-active fail-loud guard, mpv `--log-file` presence) → [green] `9d8b36e77` (fix). Observed RED (5/9 issue-1190 anchors absent) → GREEN (9/9 present) by sourcing the script + asserting the pure builders' generated text (the same thing `tests/harness_lipsync_test_mode.rs` does). `bash -n` on every generated remote-bash string OK; `shellcheck -S warning` clean (no new findings); `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; anchor occurrence-count sweep OLD vs NEW = 0 dangerous (1→0 / 1→N) transitions.
- **Review:** fresh-context read-only reviewer (general-purpose, no model override = Opus 4.8; NEVER the built-in review skill) satisfying `/review` + `/requesting-code-review` → **0 🔴 0 🟡 0 🔵, approve** (reviewed comment on the ticket). It independently confirmed: `Restart=always` does not fire on a COMMANDED `systemctl stop` (so the unit stays down for the mpv window) and the is-active guard trips only on a genuinely-still-active unit; the ERR-trap window cannot leave cam2 black; the restore path's `enable --now` re-starts the stopped unit; heredoc escaping + no newline-glue; RED→GREEN genuine; every existing harness invariant preserved (no pkill / no fbdev / one nohup mpv / preflight untouched) and no cross-file anchor collision (only this harness reads this script).
- **WORKTREE MODE:** stopped at green LOCAL result; supervisor integrates (merge current dev + full CI; live mpv/DRM playback on cam2 is a supervisor rig step — cam2 painter untouched by code+tests). Solo lane; my files disjoint from sibling lanes. No version bump (dev 1.7.0-dev.545 > main 1.7.0-dev.481). ## 2026-08-24 — issue 1191 (lipsync-test-mode.sh: peak-normalize playback speech + stale 408ms lead) — worktree worktree-agent-a27255377df405e02, base 35847a1fd (dev)
- **Root cause (both live-verified on the rig by the supervisor):** (1) the lipsync asset SPEECH is quiet (peak -9.8 dBFS, mean -27.8 dBFS) while the QPSK marker is bursty ~0 dBFS; the mic-chain AGC (mbc, hand1/Dante) operating point is pinned by the loud marker, so un-boosted speech captures ~25 dB down (~-50 dBFS) — below SyncNet's floor → conf ~1 on EVERY chunk (issue 1174 round 2: 16/16 UNMEASURABLE). (2) `LIPSYNC_AUDIO_LEAD_MS` default 408 was a stale ffmpeg-era ALSA-pipeline-depth constant; under the mpv transport (issue 1187) the measured offset at lead=0 is +40 ms (≈ ±1 frame of zero), so 408 injected a false ~0.4 s shift.
